The wallet holds 10 granted credits at rate 1.00, i.e. 1_000¢ of cover, which is less than the invoice — so it is fully consumed and the customer still owes 3_000 − 1_000 = 2_000¢. fees_amount_cents stays 3_000: credits reduce what is owed, not what was charged. Granted credits are free, so no `credit` invoice is issued and the count stays at 1.

Credits→cents is `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27), a HALF-UP round of the currency amount, not a truncation. At rate 0.6665 the granted grant is 10 × 0.6665 = 6.665 → 6.67 → 667¢ and the purchased top-up is 50 × 0.6665 = 33.325 → 33.33 → 3333¢, so the settled balance is 4_000¢ exactly. Truncating instead of rounding would give 666 + 3332 = 3_998¢ — name both: 4_000 vs 3_998, and the invoice total 2_000 vs 2_002. Three events (10/30/20) so sum 60 is distinguishable from max 30 and latest 20: 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of fees. The draw is capped at `[remaining_fee_amount, remaining_wallet_balance, remaining_invoice_amount].min` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53) = min(6000, 4000, 6000) = 4_000, so the wallet is emptied and 2_000¢ stays owed. The split across pools is the point: one outbound transaction of 4_000¢ is decomposed by `WalletTransaction.in_consumption_order` (wallet_transaction.rb:81-88), which orders inbound priority ASC then `CASE WHEN transaction_status = granted THEN 0 ELSE 1 END` then created_at. Both inbounds default to priority 50 and the PURCHASED one is created FIRST (create_from_params_service.rb:36-53 handles paid before granted), so a created_at FIFO would report prepaid_granted nil / prepaid_purchased 3_333+667=4_000 — but granted sorts ahead of purchased at equal priority, giving 667 granted + 3_333 purchased (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:83-92 buckets the consumptions by transaction_status).

Under a limitation, "full cover" means the wallet covers the whole slice it is ALLOWED to pay and keeps a surplus. With `accepts_target_wallet` the charge's grouped_by keys gain "target_wallet_code" (fees/charge_service.rb:496-499), so the 100 units split into TWO charge fees by the property the events carry: 60 units → 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_g_fc_a and 40 units → 4_000¢ tagged b06_twc_g_fc_b, plus the 0¢ subscription fee — fees_count 3, fees 10_000¢. Allocation keys buckets by [fee_type, billable_metric_id, target_wallet_code] (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:83-85) and `applicable_fee?` short-circuits on a present tag: only the wallet whose `code` equals it may pay (:109-114). Wallet a holds 100 granted credits at rate 1.00 = 10_000¢ — more than the entire invoice — and still pays only its own 6_000¢ bucket: min(6_000, 10_000, 10_000) = 6_000 (:53). Wallet b, reached second, pays min(4_000, 1_000, 4_000) = 1_000. Prepaid 7_000¢, and 3_000¢ of the b-tagged fee is still owed in CASH even though wallet a is sitting on 4_000¢ that would cover it — the limitation, not the balance, is what binds, which is the whole point of the column. The counterfactual is the pre-capability state: with no tag there is ONE 10_000¢ bucket, wallet a (priority 1) pays min(10_000, 10_000, 10_000) = 10_000, prepaid 10_000, total 0, balance 0, fees_count 2. Name both: total 3_000 vs 0, balance 4_000 vs 0. Three events in the a bucket (10/30/20) so sum 60 is distinguishable from max 30 and latest 20. Both wallets are traceable (wallets/create_service.rb:44,245-246 — a fresh customer's wallets all are), so prepaid_granted 7_000 equals prepaid_credit: every cent came from granted inbounds (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91). Granted credits raise no `credit` invoice, so invoices stays 1.

A wallet holding 10_000¢ against an invoice of 3_000¢, where the only fee it may pay is capped at 1_800¢ — the sharpest form of "could the total go negative". It does not, and the surplus is not refunded either: every draw is bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53, decremented at :57) and by the per-fee cap at :77-81, so 1_800¢ leaves the wallet, 8_200¢ stays in it, and 1_200¢ is still owed in cash. The three alternatives, named: total −7_000 if the whole applicable balance were drained, a `credit` invoice or credit note for the surplus (none is issued — invoices stays 1), or the wallet drained to 0. The cap is the second half of the row. Two tagged charge fees: 30 units → 3_000¢ tagged b06_twc_g_nt_a (10/15/5, sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 5) and 20 units → 2_000¢ tagged b06_twc_g_nt_b, 5_000¢ of fees. A fixed_amount coupon spreads BY WEIGHT, `credit × (amount_cents − precise_coupons_amount_cents) / invoice.sub_total_excluding_taxes` (fee.rb:232-236 via credits/applied_coupon_service.rb:35-37): 2_000 × 3_000/5_000 = 1_200 onto the a fee and 800 onto the b fee, nothing onto the 0¢ subscription fee. Caps are then `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` (allocate:77-79) = 1_800 for a and 1_200 for b. Wallet b is declared with NO credits, so `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65) drops it from the allocator entirely and its 1_200¢ can never be paid by anyone — wallet a is refused it by `applicable_fee?` (:109-114) despite holding 8_200¢. Prepaid credit is the LAST reducer (calculate_fees_service.rb:57-62), so credits applied BEFORE the coupon would have seen a 3_000¢ cap on the a fee and left balance 7_000 and total 0. Name both: prepaid 1_800 vs 3_000, balance 8_200 vs 7_000. And a tag-blind allocator would pay both caps, 3_000 in total, for the same total 0 and balance 7_000.

A mid-period read, and a DIFFERENT implementation of the same rule: no invoice is built at all (invoices 0). `perform_wallet_refresh` runs Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService, which re-derives the tag itself at allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-123 and re-implements the refusal at :127-130 — a second copy of the branch, so the billing rows do not cover it. Current-usage fees are grouped exactly as billed ones: `UsageFilters::WITHOUT_PRESENTATION_FILTER` leaves skip_grouping false, so grouped_by survives (fees/charge_service.rb:493-499). The pool is `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents` per key (:88): 6_000¢ tagged a (10/30/20 — sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b. Each bucket's `applicable` list has exactly ONE wallet, so `index == applicable.length - 1` holds and that wallet takes the whole bucket (:47-58) — wallet a absorbs 6_000 and NOT the 4_000 that belongs to b, giving ongoing_balance_cents = balance − ongoing_usage = 10_000 − 6_000 = 4_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63). Without the tag both wallets are unrestricted, the two keys merge into one 10_000¢ pool and wallet a — first in `in_application_order` (customers/refresh_wallets_service.rb:48) with room 10_000 — absorbs all of it: ongoing_usage 10_000 and ongoing_balance 0. Name both: 6_000 vs 10_000 and 4_000 vs 0. `balance_cents` stays 10_000 either way: the ongoing figures are a projection and never debit the wallet, which is why the row also asserts the current-usage payload — the full 10_000¢ is still owed by the customer, the wallet has merely reserved the part it is allowed to reserve. There is no granted/purchased split on this path: ongoing usage is allocated against `balance_cents` as a single pool and no WalletTransactionConsumption rows are written.

Credits→cents is `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) — a HALF-UP round of the currency amount, not a truncation. 50 credits at rate 0.6665 is 33.325 → 33.33 → 3_333¢; truncating gives 33.32 → 3_332¢. Both numbers are named because this row propagates the single cent all the way to the invoice total. Two tagged charge fees: 60 units → 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_g_rn_a (10/30/20, so sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 20 units → 2_000¢ tagged b06_twc_g_rn_b, plus the 0¢ subscription fee = 8_000¢. Wallet a may only pay its own bucket and holds less than it (3_333 < 6_000), so it is drained: min(6_000, 3_333, 8_000) = 3_333 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53). Wallet b holds 10_000¢ — five times what its own bucket needs — and may NOT top up a's shortfall (:109-114), so it pays exactly its own 2_000¢ and keeps 8_000¢. Prepaid 5_333¢, total 2_667¢. Truncation instead of half-up would give prepaid 5_332 and total 2_668; ignoring the tag would merge the buckets and let b pay a's remaining 4_667¢, giving prepaid 8_000, total 0 and balance 5_333. All three are separated by the pair (total 2_667, wallet b 8_000). b is the asserted wallet because a ends at 0 under every one of those implementations, while b's balance is the only place the refusal to cross buckets is visible — and `expect.wallet` takes one wallet, not a list.

Target beats priority — the one thing a single-wallet target row cannot say. Both wallets hold 100 credits at rate 1.00 (10_000¢) and the charge fee is 30 × 1.00 = 3_000¢, so EITHER could cover it alone. `Wallet.in_application_order` walks priority ASC (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:34 over :126), which reaches b06_hns_twp_beta (priority 1) FIRST; but the fee carries grouped_by["target_wallet_code"] = b06_hns_twp_alpha, and `applicable_fee?` returns `wallet.code == target_wallet_code` before it ever looks at targets, types or the unrestricted case (:109-114). So beta is skipped entirely and alpha, reached second, pays all 3_000¢ — total 0¢, and beta's balance is UNTOUCHED at 10_000¢. The interval rule grants a flat 70 credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111) at rate 0.3335: `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) is HALF-UP on the currency amount, so 70 × 0.3335 = 23.345 → 23.35 → 2_335¢, where truncation would give 2_334¢. The wallet is created empty on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to, excluded that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74) and due on the day-1 anniversary of 1 April (:120-130); granted credits settle at once, so invoices stays 1. Fees 1_100¢: a 500¢ subscription fee and a 600¢ charge fee (60 units from 10/30/20 — sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20 — × 0.10 = 6.00). allowed_fee_types is ["charge"], so the subscription bucket is skipped outright by `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:108-122) and the charge bucket draws min(600, 2_335, 1_100) = 600 (:53). The limitation and not the balance binds: 500¢ stays cash beside 1_735¢ of unusable credit, and payment_status is pending. The outbound is sized by `WalletCredit.from_amount_cents` (wallet_credit.rb:7-11), which carries the 600¢ through unrounded, so the balance ends 2_335 − 600 = 1_735¢ and a truncating implementation would print 1_734¢ — the single cent that separates them, since prepaid and total are 600 and 500 under both. Ignoring allowed_fee_types would instead give prepaid 1_100, total 0 and balance 1_235 (or 1_234 truncated); a hollowed interval verb gives prepaid 0, total 1_100 and balance 0.

Two wallets declared in the WRONG order on purpose: the 50-credit one (priority 20) first in the YAML, the interval-refilled one (priority 1, created empty) second. Consumption follows `Wallet.in_application_order` — priority ASC then created_at (wallet.rb:69-71) — so the interval wallet is drawn first even though it was created second and is the poorer of the two. Both pools are purely GRANTED, so the granted/purchased breakdown cannot separate them (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:83-92 would report prepaid_granted 6_000 either way) and the invoice total is 0 either way. The one number that moves is wallet b's ending balance, and it is the whole assertion. 60 units (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of fees. At 00:30 on 1 April the interval rule grants wallet a a flat 30 credits = 3_000¢ (a granted inbound, settled on creation, no `credit` invoice, so invoices stays 1); the anniversary matches because both wallets were created on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to and create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74 only excludes wallets born TODAY. At billing there is one bucket, [charge, bm_id] = 6_000¢, and the loop is wallet-outer / bucket-inner (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:34-62). Wallet a draws min(6_000, 3_000, 6_000) = 3_000 and empties, leaving the bucket at 3_000 and remaining_invoice_amount at 3_000. Wallet b then draws min(3_000, 5_000, 3_000) = 3_000 and ends at 5_000 − 3_000 = 2_000¢. Creation order instead of priority would drain b FIRST: min(6_000, 5_000, 6_000) = 5_000, b ends at 0 and a covers the last 1_000, ending at 2_000. And with the interval verb hollowed, a has a 0 balance so `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65) drops it entirely, b pays 5_000, ends at 0 and 1_000 stays cash. Name all three: b at 2_000 (correct) versus 0 under either wrong answer, with total 0 versus 0 versus 1_000.

A scheduled rule that grossly over-refills — a flat 200 granted credits = 20_000¢ landing on an invoice whose payable ceiling is 4_500¢ — which is the case where the total could go negative. It does NOT. Lago clamps at zero and leaves the surplus in the wallet: every draw is bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53, decremented at :57), so exactly 4_500¢ leaves and 15_500¢ stays. The three alternatives, named: (a) total −15_500 if the whole balance were drained against the invoice, (b) a `credit` invoice or a credit note for the 15_500 surplus — none is issued and invoices stays 1, (c) the wallet emptied to 0. Nothing scales the top-up down to what is needed: `compute_granted_credits` returns the rule's amount verbatim for a non-target rule (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111), and unlike a threshold rule it is not even a function of the ongoing balance — the interval path reads `credits_ongoing_balance` only for the paid leg (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service .rb:9-11). The wallet is created empty on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to, so it is excluded that day (:74) and due on the day-1 anniversary of 1 April (:120-130). The 4_500 ceiling is the row's second half. Prepaid credit is the LAST reducer (calculate_fees_service.rb:57-62: coupon → tax → credit note → prepaid) and the per-fee cap is `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` (:77-79), where `sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents = amount_cents − precise_coupons_amount_cents` (fee.rb:238-240): 6_000 − 1_500 = 4_500 on the single charge fee (60 units from 10/30/20 × 1.00), which equals invoice.total exactly so `reconcile_remaining_amounts` (:93-106) adds nothing. Credits applied BEFORE the coupon would have taken 6_000 and left 14_000 — name both: prepaid 4_500 vs 6_000, wallet 15_500 vs 14_000. The coupon is `frequency: once` and is still unspent when the period invoice is built, because a granted interval top-up raises no invoice for it to be consumed on.

A mid-period read of a wallet whose credits arrived from a SCHEDULE rather than from a threshold, which is why the two clock jobs have to appear in the same timeline and in this order. `perform_interval_wallet_top_ups` (Clock::CreateIntervalWalletTransactionsJob, the sole caller of Wallets::CreateIntervalWalletTransactionsService) puts the credits in; only then does `perform_wallet_refresh` (Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob) compute an ongoing balance against them. Neither verb substitutes for the other: the refresh job's only top-up path is Wallets::ThresholdTopUpService (update_ongoing_service.rb:26), i.e. `trigger: threshold` alone. March is deliberately EMPTY of events and is never billed — the timeline holds no perform_billing — so invoices is 0 and the ongoing pool contains April usage only. The wallet is created on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to, is excluded from the rule that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74) and is due on the day-1 monthly anniversary of 1 April (:120-130), where it receives a flat 50 granted credits = 5_000¢ (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111). Granted credits settle immediately, so no `credit` invoice appears either. Three April events 10/30/20 (sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of unbilled usage, pooled as `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents` from Invoices::CustomerUsageService output for the CURRENT period (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:114-123 via refresh_wallets_service.rb:52-54). One wallet, so it is the last applicable one for the single key and absorbs the whole 6_000 rather than being capped at its balance (:47-58): ongoing_usage_balance_cents 6_000 and ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63) — the wallet is allowed NEGATIVE and `depleted_ongoing_balance` flips true (:41-45). There is no cascade here: nothing re-arms, because an interval rule is fired by a date and not by a balance. The plausible wrong answers, all named: a hollowed interval verb (or `perform_wallet_refresh` standing in for it) → balance 0 and ongoing_balance −6_000; a clamp of ongoing usage at the balance → ongoing_usage 5_000 and ongoing_balance 0; a top-up re-armed by the deficit the way a threshold rule would be → balance 10_000 and ongoing_balance 4_000.

The interval sibling of b06/threshold-rule/none/partial-cover, and it under-covers for a completely different reason. A threshold rule under-covers because it fires at the wrong TIME (the balance was already spent); an interval rule fires exactly on schedule and under-covers because its AMOUNT is flat. `compute_granted_credits` returns `granted_credits` verbatim for a non-target rule (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111), so nothing scales the 40 credits to the 60 the invoice actually needs, and no re-arming loop exists: the interval path has no cascade at all, unlike Wallets::Balance::IncreaseService re-enqueueing the refresh for a threshold rule (increase_service.rb:36). The wallet is created EMPTY at setup time, i.e. inside the travel_to of the first timeline step (2024-03-01T00:00:00Z), which is what makes the rule reachable: the service drops wallets born today outright (`DATE(wallets.created_at AT TIME ZONE ...) != DATE(:today ...)`, create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74) and matches the monthly anniversary on `DATE_PART('day', COALESCE(rule.started_at, wallets.created_at)) = DATE_PART('day', :today)` (:120-130) — day 1 on both sides. Silent on 1 March, due on 1 April. Three events 10/30/20 so the sum 60 is distinguishable from max 30 and latest 20: 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of fees. At 00:30 on 1 April the rule grants a flat 40 credits = 4_000¢ — an inbound GRANT, settled on creation, raising no `credit` invoice, hence invoices stays 1. At 01:00 billing draws min(6_000, 4_000, 6_000) = 4_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53), leaving 2_000¢ owed in cash and payment_status pending rather than succeeded, and the wallet at exactly 0. Name the counterfactuals: a hollowed verb (or a `perform_wallet_refresh` in its place, which reaches `trigger: threshold` only) gives prepaid 0 and total 6_000; a rule sized to the deficit instead of the flat 40 gives prepaid 6_000, total 0 and balance 0 — the same balance, which is why prepaid_credit_amount_cents and total_amount_cents are the load-bearing assertions here and the balance is only the third witness.

One credit→cents conversion landing exactly on a half-cent, so the asserted balance moves if the rounding mode changes. `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) is a HALF-UP round of the currency amount, not a truncation: the interval rule's flat 70 granted credits at rate 0.3335 are 70 × 0.3335 = 23.345 → 23.35 → 2_335¢. Truncating instead would give 23.34 → 2_334¢. Fees: 60 units (10/30/20, so sum 60 is distinguishable from max 30 and latest 20) × 0.10 = 6.00 → 600¢, deliberately small so the top-up over-covers it and the residue carries the rounding difference into the asserted balance rather than into the invoice. The wallet is created empty on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to; the rule is silent that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74 excludes wallets born today) and due on 1 April on the day-1 monthly anniversary (:120-130). Granted credits settle at once and raise no `credit` invoice, so invoices stays 1. At billing the draw is min(600, 2_335, 600) = 600 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service .rb:53), the total clamps to 0, and the outbound is sized by `WalletCredit.from_amount_cents` (wallet_credit.rb:7-11), which carries the 600¢ through unrounded. Balance ends 2_335 − 600 = 1_735¢; a truncating implementation would print 1_734¢, and that single cent is the only asserted number that separates the two, since prepaid and total are 600 and 0 under both.

The tag confines a SCHEDULED top-up to the fee it was tagged for, and that is a different claim from the threshold sibling: there the tag decided how much usage the wallet could see and therefore how often its rule fired, here the rule's amount is fixed by the calendar and the tag only decides what the credits may pay. `accepts_target_wallet` on the charge gives the fee's grouped_by keys a `target_wallet_code` (fees/charge_service.rb:496-499) and the fee key gains a third element (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:83-85), at which point `applicable_fee?` refuses every wallet whose `code` does not match it (:109-114) — ahead of fee-type and metric limits. It needs `events_targeting_wallets` as well as the premium licence, hence the organization block. Two tagged charge fees plus the 0¢ subscription fee that a plan with amount_cents 0 still emits, so fees_count is 3 and fees_amount 10_000¢: 6_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tfc_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tfc_b. Wallet a is created EMPTY on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to — excluded from the rule that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74), due on the day-1 monthly anniversary of 1 April (:120-130) — and receives a flat 90 granted credits = 9_000¢ (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111), settled at once, raising no `credit` invoice, so invoices stays 1. Wallet b holds its initial 1_000¢. At billing wallet a pays only its own bucket: min(6_000, 9_000, 10_000) = 6_000 (:53 gated by :109-114) — full cover of the allowed slice with 3_000¢ of surplus — and wallet b pays min(4_000, 1_000, 4_000) = 1_000 and empties. Prepaid 7_000, total 3_000 owed in cash that wallet a's surplus may not touch, so payment_status is pending. Tag-blind the two buckets merge into one 10_000¢ key and wallet a, first in `Wallet.in_application_order` (wallet.rb:69-71), would draw min(10_000, 9_000, 10_000) = 9_000 and end at 0, b would add its 1_000, prepaid 10_000 and total 0. Name both: a at 3_000 vs 0, total 3_000 vs 0. A hollowed interval verb leaves a with a zero balance, dropped by `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65): prepaid 1_000, total 9_000, a at 0.

Target beats priority, with a scheduled top-up as the thing being confined. Three wallets: b06_itv_tmp_g at priority 1, unrestricted, 10_000¢; b06_itv_tmp_a at priority 20, created EMPTY, with an interval rule; b06_itv_tmp_d at priority 30 with 500¢. Both charge fees carry a tag — 3_000¢ to a (5/15/10: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 10) and 2_000¢ to d — plus the 0¢ subscription fee a plan with amount_cents 0 still emits, hence fees_count 3 on 5_000¢ of fees. g is applicable to NEITHER tagged bucket (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:109-114) even though `Wallet.in_application_order` reaches it first (wallet.rb:69-71); an unrestricted wallet is not unrestricted against a tag. Wallet a is created on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to, so its rule is excluded that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74) and due on the day-1 monthly anniversary of 1 April (:120-130), granting a flat 80 credits = 8_000¢ (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111) — settled at once, no `credit` invoice, invoices stays 1. At billing g contributes nothing and is dropped on `next if total_amount_cents <= 0` (:64), keeping all 10_000¢; a pays its own 3_000¢, min(3_000, 8_000, 5_000) = 3_000, ending at 5_000¢; d pays min(2_000, 500, 2_000) = 500 and empties. Prepaid 3_500 of 5_000¢, total 1_500 owed in cash — d's unfunded remainder, which the wallet with 10_000¢ in it is forbidden to pay. g's balance is the whole assertion because it is the number the tag decides: tag-blind, the two buckets merge into one 5_000¢ key and g, first in application order, pays all of it — prepaid 5_000, total 0, g at 5_000. A hollowed interval verb leaves a on a zero balance, dropped by `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65): prepaid 500, total 4_500, g still at 10_000, which is why the invoice figures are asserted beside it. Name all three: g 10_000 / 5_000 / 10_000 with total 1_500 / 0 / 4_500.

A wallet refilled on schedule to five times the invoice's payable ceiling while 1_200¢ stays unpaid: the total never goes negative and the surplus is never refunded. Wallet a is created EMPTY on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to, excluded from the rule that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74) and due on the day-1 monthly anniversary of 1 April (:120-130), where a flat 80 granted credits = 8_000¢ land (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111). Granted credits settle at once and raise no invoice, so invoices stays 1, and nothing scales the grant to what is owed. Fees 5_000¢ over three fees (two tagged plus the 0¢ subscription fee a plan with amount_cents 0 still emits, hence fees_count 3): 3_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tnt_a (10/15/5: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 5) and 2_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tnt_b. The fixed_amount coupon spreads BY WEIGHT (fee.rb:232-236 through credits/applied_coupon_service.rb:35-37): 2_000 × 3_000/5_000 = 1_200 onto the a fee and 800 onto the b fee, so the caps are `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` = 1_800 and 1_200 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:77-79) and invoice.total is 5_000 − 2_000 = 3_000. Wallet b holds no credits at all, so `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65) drops it and its 1_200¢ can be paid by nobody — wallet a is refused it by the tag (:109-114) while sitting on 6_200¢. Every draw is also bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (:53, :57), so prepaid is 1_800 and the total clamps at 1_200 rather than −5_000. Named alternatives: credits applied BEFORE the coupon would cap the a fee at 3_000 → prepaid 3_000, total 0, balance 5_000; a tag-blind allocator would let a pay both caps → the same 3_000 and 0, balance 5_000; a `credit` invoice or credit note for the surplus, or a wallet drained to 0 — neither happens. Nothing re-arms after billing either: an interval rule is due on a date, so the post-billing refresh (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:34-39) cannot top a up the way it would a threshold wallet, and 6_200 is stable.

The tag decides how much unbilled usage a scheduled top-up is measured against, and that is exactly where a tag-blind implementation is visible: the two wallets have DIFFERENT balances, so merging the buckets changes which of them absorbs what. Both clock jobs appear and do different things — the interval verb (Clock::CreateIntervalWalletTransactionsJob → Wallets::CreateIntervalWalletTransactionsService, its only caller) puts a flat 40 granted credits = 4_000¢ into wallet a on the day-1 monthly anniversary of 1 April (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:120-130, both wallets having been created on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to and therefore excluded that day, :74); the refresh verb (Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob, premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) then computes the ongoing balance. March carries no events and is never billed, so invoices is 0 and the pool is April usage only. Current-usage fees keep their grouping (fees/charge_service.rb:493-499), so the pool holds two keys: 6_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tob_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tob_b. `applicable_fee?` gives each key exactly one wallet (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137), and that wallet is therefore the last applicable one for its key, so it absorbs the whole amount with no room check (:47-58) — wallet a reserves against its OWN 6_000, not the 10_000 of total usage. ongoing_usage_balance_cents 6_000 and ongoing_balance_cents = 4_000 − 6_000 = −2_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63): a wallet is allowed NEGATIVE on the ongoing side and `depleted_ongoing_balance` flips true (:41-45). Nothing re-arms — an interval rule is due on a date, not on a balance, so unlike a threshold wallet there is no cascade after the read. Tag-blind, the two keys merge into one 10_000¢ pool with both wallets applicable. Wallet a (priority 1) is then NOT the last applicable one, so it is capped at its own room: take = min(10_000, 4_000) = 4_000 (:52-55), leaving ongoing_usage 4_000 and ongoing_balance 0, with b absorbing the remaining 6_000 as the last wallet. Name both: ongoing_usage 6_000 vs 4_000 and ongoing_balance −2_000 vs 0. A hollowed interval verb gives balance 0, ongoing_usage 6_000 and ongoing_balance −6_000, which is why the balance is asserted beside the pair.

Target-wallet is the ONE limitation whose partial-cover row is separable on the invoice figures, because the tag partitions the buckets rather than merely filtering them: a rich wallet that is forbidden the OTHER wallet's bucket leaves that remainder in cash, and prepaid is therefore not min(total balance, invoice total) at all. Fees 10_000¢ over three fees (two tagged, plus the 0¢ subscription fee a plan with amount_cents 0 still emits, hence fees_count 3): 6_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tpc_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b06_itv_tpc_b. Wallet a is created EMPTY on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to, excluded from the rule that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74) and due on the day-1 anniversary of 1 April (:120-130), where it receives a flat 20 granted credits = 2_000¢ (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111) — settled at once, no `credit` invoice, so invoices stays 1. Nothing sizes that 20 to the 60 credits its own bucket needs: the interval path never consults the deficit (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:9-11 reads `credits_ongoing_balance` only for the paid leg), and there is no cascade to re-arm it. At billing wallet a (priority 1) is confined to its own bucket and holds a third of it: min(6_000, 2_000, 10_000) = 2_000, and it empties (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53 gated by :109-114). Wallet b then finds a's bucket at 4_000 but is refused it by the tag, pays its own 4_000¢ in full — min(4_000, 10_000, 8_000) = 4_000 — and keeps 6_000¢ it may not put against a's remainder. So prepaid is 6_000 and 4_000¢ of a's own usage is owed in CASH beside a fully solvent wallet; payment_status pending. b is the asserted wallet because a ends at 0 under every behaviour. Tag-blind, the buckets merge into one 10_000¢ key: a draws its 2_000, b draws min(8_000, 10_000, 8_000) = 8_000 and ends at 2_000, prepaid 10_000, total 0. Name both: b at 6_000 vs 2_000, total 4_000 vs 0. A hollowed interval verb drops a entirely on `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65), leaving b at 6_000 as asserted but prepaid 4_000 and total 6_000 — which is why the invoice figures are asserted alongside the balance.

Two wallets at DIFFERENT rates, each confined to its own tagged fee, so the half-cent conversion is observed on one of them without the other's arithmetic being able to absorb it. The interval rule grants wallet a a flat 70 credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111) at rate 0.3335: `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) is HALF-UP on the currency amount, so 70 × 0.3335 = 23.345 → 23.35 → 2_335¢, where truncation would give 2_334¢. Wallet a is created empty on 1 March inside the first step's travel_to, excluded from the rule that day (create_interval_wallet_transactions_service.rb:74) and due on the day-1 anniversary of 1 April (:120-130); granted credits settle at once, so invoices stays 1. Fees 1_000¢ over three fees (two tagged plus the 0¢ subscription fee a plan with amount_cents 0 still emits, hence fees_count 3): 60 units tagged a (10/30/20 — sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) × 0.10 = 6.00 → 600¢, and 40 units tagged b × 0.10 = 4.00 → 400¢. At billing each wallet may only pay the bucket carrying its own code (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:109-114): a draws min(600, 2_335, 1_000) = 600 and b draws min(400, 1_000, 400) = 400, so prepaid is the full 1_000 and the total clamps to 0. The outbound is sized by `WalletCredit.from_amount_cents` (wallet_credit.rb:7-11), which carries the 600¢ through unrounded, so a ends at 2_335 − 600 = 1_735¢ and a truncating implementation would print 1_734¢ — the single cent, and the only asserted number that separates the two, since prepaid and total are 1_000 and 0 under both. Tag-blind the one merged 1_000¢ bucket would be paid by a alone (priority 1, 2_335¢ ≥ 1_000): a at 1_335, b untouched at 1_000, prepaid and total unchanged — so the same assertion also carries the tag. A hollowed interval verb drops a on `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65): prepaid 400, total 600, a at 0.

Two charges: metric a 10+30+20 = 60 units → 6_000¢, metric b 5+10+5 = 20 units → 2_000¢, fees 8_000¢. Three events per metric so sum is distinguishable from max and latest. The wallet holds 10_000¢ of SETTLED purchased credit and is limited to metric a, so it covers its allowed slice in full with a surplus — the distinction from the partial-cover row, where the same limitation applies but the balance runs out inside the slice. Buckets are `[fee_type, billable_metric_id]` sorted by descending amount (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:82-89), so metric a's 6_000 is offered first and matched through `wallet_targets` (:37-41, :117); metric b's key matches neither targets nor types and is skipped. Draw min(6000, 10000, 8000) = 6_000, total 2_000 — metric b's fee, owed in cash — and the wallet keeps 4_000. Note this is a DIFFERENT lookup from the fee-types rows, ORed against it at :121: both fees here are `fee_type: charge`, so a wallet that matched on fee type alone would take 8_000 and leave 0 owed. The per-fee amounts plus prepaid 6_000 exclude that. The 6 March top-up of 50 credits is never paid and stays pending (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138, `remaining_amount_cents` nil at create_service.rb:56-62): it neither joins `available_inbound` (wallet_transaction.rb:80) nor the balance, so the wallet ends at 4_000 rather than 9_000.

12_000¢ of settled purchased credit against an 8_000¢ invoice — enough to drive the total negative by 4_000. It does not. The metric limitation caps the reachable amount at metric a's 6_000¢ bucket (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:108-122, matching through wallet_targets at :37-41), so the draw is min(6000, 12000, 8000) = 6_000 and the invoice clamp `remaining_invoice_amount` (:53, :57) is never the binding constraint. Total 2_000 — metric b's fee, which this wallet may not pay for, owed in CASH while 6_000¢ of purchased credit stays unusable. Alternatives with their numbers: (a) limitation ignored → the invoice clamp takes over, prepaid 8_000, total 0, wallet 4_000; (b) no clamp anywhere → total −4_000 and the wallet drained to 0; (c) the unusable surplus refunded — no credit note, no inbound transaction, the only movement is the 6_000¢ outbound. Because (a) and the truth differ on the wallet as much as the invoice, balance_cents 6_000 and consumed_amount_cents 6_000 are asserted with the total. Both fees are `fee_type: charge`, so nothing but the wallet_targets lookup can tell them apart. The 6 March top-up of 40 credits is never paid and stays pending (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138); if pending credits counted the balance would end at 10_000. prepaid_purchased 6_000 with prepaid_granted absent confirms a purchased-only pool.

Mid-period on the ongoing allocator (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:33-65 via Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob → Customers::RefreshWalletsService — premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8), with a wallet limited to metric a. Unbilled usage: metric a 6_000¢, metric b 2_000¢. Fee keys are `[fee_type, billable_metric_id, target_wallet_code, currency]` (:118-124) — one element wider than the billing allocator's key, which is why this needs its own row rather than reusing the billing derivation. The pool is sorted descending (:98-104) so metric a is offered first with `budgets["EUR"]` = 8_000; the wallet is the only applicable one so it takes all 6_000 (:48-51). Metric b's key has NO applicable wallet (:126-137, targets do not include it), so its 2_000 is dropped — the budget falls but no wallet claims it. `ongoing_balance_cents = 10_000 − 6_000 = 4_000` (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63). Wrong answers: ignoring the metric limitation gives ongoing_usage 8_000 and ongoing_balance 2_000; the last-wallet-absorbs rule (:48) firing for metric b as well would give the same 8_000 — asserting 6_000 exactly excludes both. The 6 March top-up of 50 credits is never paid; it is created `pending` (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138) and Balance::IncreaseService only runs from Wallets::ApplyPaidCreditsService on payment (apply_paid_credits_service.rb:12-20), so `balance_cents` stays 10_000 and the ongoing balance stays 4_000 rather than 9_000 — purchased-but-unsettled credit does not make a wallet look solvent mid-period either. invoices is 2: both `credit` top-up invoices, no billing having run.

The mirror of the metric full-cover row: fees 8_000¢ (metric a 6_000, metric b 2_000) but only 20 credits settled — 2_000¢ against a 6_000¢ allowed slice. The wallet is drained: draw min(6000, 2000, 8000) = 2_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53), so 4_000¢ of metric a's fee plus all 2_000¢ of metric b's are owed in cash, total 6_000. The 6 March top-up is 100 credits — deliberately far more than the shortfall — and it is never paid. It is created `pending` (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138) with `remaining_amount_cents` nil (create_service.rb:56-62), so it is invisible both to `balance_cents` and to `available_inbound` (wallet_transaction.rb:80). If purchased but unsettled credits were spendable, the draw would be min(6000, 12000, 8000) = 6_000, prepaid 6_000 and total 2_000 — a 4_000¢ swing on the customer's bill from credits nobody has paid for. Asserting balance_cents 0 and consumed_amount_cents 2_000 alongside the total pins which of the two Lago does. Metric b's fee is the one the limitation forbids and it is asserted at its full 2_000¢ inside the 6_000 total; both fees are `fee_type: charge`, so only the wallet_targets lookup (:37-41, :117) can distinguish them. invoices is 3 — subscription plus two `credit` invoices, one settled, one pending.

Rate 1.66675, the full five decimals the column allows. 10 credits is `(10 × 1.66675).round(2) × 100` = 16.6675 → 16.67 → 1_667¢ (wallet_credit.rb:26-27, HALF-UP on the third decimal). Truncating gives 16.66 → 1_666¢. Name both: prepaid 1_667 vs 1_666, total 6_333 vs 6_334. This is the amount the customer was invoiced for the top-up, so the rounding decides the price as well as the cover. Fees 8_000¢ (metric a 6_000, metric b 2_000). The wallet is limited to metric a, so the reachable bucket is 6_000 and the draw is min(6000, 1667, 8000) = 1_667 — the whole settled balance. Total 8_000 − 1_667 = 6_333, which contains metric b's untouchable 2_000¢ in full. The 6 March top-up of another 10 credits is never paid, stays pending (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138) and is excluded from the balance and from `available_inbound` (wallet_transaction.rb:80). Had it settled the draw would be min(6000, 3334, 8000) = 3_334 and the total 4_666 — so the row pins rounding, the metric limitation and the settlement boundary with one set of numbers.

Fees 11_000¢ = 5_000 subscription + 6_000 charge. The wallet holds 10_000¢ of SETTLED purchased credit and is limited to `charge`, so "full cover" here means the allowed slice is covered in full and a surplus remains — the discriminator against the partial-cover row below, where the same wallet runs dry mid-slice. `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:108-122) admits only the charge bucket: the subscription key matches neither `types` (["charge"]) nor `targets` (empty), and `unrestricted_wallet` is false because types is non-empty. Draw min(6000, 10000, 11000) = 6_000 → total 5_000, the subscription fee owed in CASH, and the wallet retains 4_000. A wallet ignoring allowed_fee_types would draw 10_000 and leave 1_000 owed; one treating the limitation as an invoice-level discount would reach the same 5_000 total with a 0 balance — balance_cents 4_000 rules both out. The 6 March top-up of 50 credits is never paid: created `pending` (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138), excluded from `available_inbound` (wallet_transaction.rb:80) and from the balance, so it changes nothing. Had it settled the wallet would end at 9_000 with the same invoice. prepaid_purchased 6_000 and no prepaid_granted: every cent came from a purchased inbound (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:83-92). invoices is 3 — subscription plus two `credit` invoices, one settled and one pending.

14_000¢ of settled purchased credit against an 11_000¢ invoice: more than enough to drive the total negative, and more than enough to pay the whole invoice. Neither happens. The limitation clamp fires FIRST — `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:108-122) with types=["subscription"] admits only the 5_000¢ subscription bucket, so the draw is min(5000, 14000, 11000) = 5_000 and `remaining_invoice_amount` (:53) never becomes the binding constraint. Total 6_000 — exactly the charge fee, owed in cash — while 9_000¢ of paid-for credit sits unusable. The alternatives with their numbers: (a) limitation ignored → prepaid 11_000, total 0, wallet 3_000; (b) no clamp anywhere → total −3_000; (c) the unusable surplus refunded via a credit note or expired — neither occurs, the only wallet transaction is the 5_000¢ outbound. Because (a) and the truth differ in the wallet as much as in the invoice, balance_cents 9_000 and consumed_amount_cents 5_000 are asserted alongside the total. The 6 March top-up of 50 credits is never paid and stays pending (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138); the balance would end at 14_000 rather than 9_000 if pending credits counted. prepaid_purchased 5_000 with prepaid_granted absent: a purchased-only wallet, which is what makes this the paid-settled row rather than the granted one.

Mid-period, on the ongoing allocator (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:33-65, reached from Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob → Customers::RefreshWalletsService), with a `charge`-only wallet — the positive branch of the fee-type filter on this path, complementary to the granted `subscription`-only row which asserts a 0 allocation. The pool contains ONLY the charge fee: it is built from `current_usage_fees` (refresh_wallets_service.rb:52-54) = Invoices::CustomerUsageService output, which produces usage fees, so the plan's 5_000¢ subscription fee — the fee this wallet may not pay for — is absent from the mid-period picture altogether and will be owed in cash at period end with nothing reserved against it. The charge key matches `types` (:126-137), the wallet is the only applicable one, so it absorbs the whole 6_000¢ (:48-51). `ongoing_balance_cents = 10_000 − 6_000 = 4_000` (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63). Wrong answers: 11_000 of usage and −1_000 if the ongoing pool included the subscription fee AND the limitation were ignored; 1_000 if the subscription fee entered the pool but the limitation held. Both are excluded by asserting ongoing_usage_balance_cents 6_000 exactly. The 6 March top-up of 50 credits stays pending (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138) and does not move `balance_cents` off 10_000, so it cannot inflate the ongoing balance either — 9_000 would be the wrong answer there. invoices is 2, both `credit` top-up invoices.

The mirror of the full-cover row: the same 11_000¢ invoice (5_000 subscription + 6_000 charge), the same `charge`-only limitation, but only 20 credits settled — 2_000¢, less than the 6_000¢ allowed slice. The wallet is drained: draw min(6000, 2000, 11000) = 2_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53), so 4_000¢ of the charge fee AND the whole 5_000¢ subscription fee are owed in cash, total 9_000. The 6 March top-up is 100 credits — deliberately more than enough to finish the job — and it is never paid. It is created `pending` with `remaining_amount_cents` nil (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138, create_service.rb:56-62), so it is invisible to both the balance and `available_inbound` (wallet_transaction.rb:80). If purchased-but-unsettled credits were spendable, the draw would be min(6000, 12000, 11000) = 6_000, prepaid 6_000 and total 5_000 — a 4_000¢ difference on the customer's bill. That is the sharpest form of the paid/paid-settled boundary in this slice, and it is why the row bills 12_000¢ of credit and lets only 2_000¢ of it work. Both the settled and the pending top-up appear as `credit` invoices, so invoices is 3. The subscription fee is the fee the limitation forbids and it is asserted at its full 5_000¢ inside a 9_000 total.

Rate 3.4565 — a credit worth more than a euro, and 10 credits land exactly on a half-cent: `(10 × 3.4565).round(2) × 100` = 34.565 → 34.57 → 3_457¢ (wallet_credit.rb:26-27, HALF-UP). Truncating gives 34.56 → 3_456¢. Name both: prepaid 3_457 vs 3_456, total 7_543 vs 7_544. The customer is invoiced 3_457¢ for the top-up, so the rounding decides both what they paid and what they got. Fees 11_000¢ (5_000 subscription + 6_000 charge). The wallet may pay only `subscription` fees, so the reachable bucket is 5_000¢ and the 6_000¢ charge fee is skipped by `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:108-122) and owed in cash in full. Draw min(5000, 3457, 11000) = 3_457, the whole settled balance; total 11_000 − 3_457 = 7_543. The 6 March top-up of another 10 credits is never paid and stays pending (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138), so it neither settles nor raises the balance; had it settled the draw would be min(5000, 6914, 11000) = 5_000 and the total 6_000. Rounding and settlement are therefore pinned by the same three numbers.

This row pins what `paid-settled` MEANS, in both directions, on one wallet. A purchased top-up is created with `status: :pending` and no `remaining_amount_cents` (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138, create_service.rb:56-62), and the balance is NOT touched. Settlement is what makes the credits spendable: paying the `credit` invoice flips its payment_status, Invoices::UpdateService fires Invoices::PrepaidCreditJob (prepaid_credit_job.rb:17-25) → Wallets::ApplyPaidCreditsService (apply_paid_credits_service.rb:12-20) → SettleService (status settled, `remaining_amount_cents = amount_cents`, settle_service.rb:18-25) then Balance::IncreaseService (+10_000¢). So the 100 credits paid on 2 March are worth 10_000¢ of cover. The second top-up, on 6 March, is never paid. Its transaction stays pending, so it is excluded from `available_inbound` (wallet_transaction.rb:80, `inbound.settled`) AND from the balance — an UNSETTLED top-up's credits are NOT spendable, which is the answer to the revenue question: pending credits cannot be spent, so no revenue leaks; the risk lives on the other side, a customer who has been invoiced 5_000¢ of credits they cannot yet use. Arithmetic: 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of fees, fully covered — prepaid 6_000, total 0, payment_status succeeded (calculate_fees_service.rb:64 marks a zero total succeeded, not pending). The wallet keeps 4_000, not the whole balance. If pending credits HAD been spendable the balance would be 15_000 and end at 9_000 with the same invoice numbers, so balance_cents 4_000 is the only assertion that separates the two. prepaid_purchased 6_000 with prepaid_granted absent shows the pool: this wallet has no granted inbound at all. invoices is 3 — subscription plus two `credit` invoices, one settled and one not.

10_000¢ of settled purchased credit against an invoice that a `once` coupon has already cut to 4_000¢ — the configuration where the total could go negative. Lago clamps at zero: every draw is bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53, decremented :57), so exactly 4_000¢ leaves the wallet and 6_000¢ stays. Alternatives, named: total −6_000 if the balance were drained; a credit note or `credit` invoice for the 6_000 surplus (none is created); the wallet emptied to 0. Why the ceiling is 4_000 and not 6_000: prepaid credit is the LAST reducer (calculate_fees_service.rb:57-62 — progressive billing → coupon → tax → credit note → prepaid), and the per-fee cap is `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` (:77-79) with `sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents = amount_cents − precise_coupons_amount_cents` (fee.rb:238-240) = 6_000 − 2_000. Credits before the coupon would have drawn 6_000 and left the wallet at 4_000; both numbers are asserted so the order is pinned, not just the totals. The coupon is spent HERE and not on the top-up invoice: the `credit` invoice is issued first in time, but Invoices::PaidCreditService computes its totals directly (:80-91) and never runs the coupon or prepaid stages, so a `frequency: once` coupon survives to the period invoice. The 6 March top-up of 20 credits is never paid, stays pending and does not raise the balance; had it settled the balance would end at 8_000 rather than 6_000, which is the assertion that separates settled from purchased-but-unsettled here.

A mid-period read on the ongoing path — Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated, refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService — which is a separate implementation from the billing allocator, not a shared helper. The 100 credits paid on 2 March are settled, so `balance_cents` is 10_000¢. Unbilled usage is 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢, pooled as `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents` (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:90). One wallet, so it is the last applicable and absorbs the whole key (:48-51). `ongoing_balance_cents = balance_cents − ongoing_usage_balance_cents` (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63) = 10_000 − 6_000 = 4_000. The 6 March top-up of 50 credits is the row's real question. It is created pending (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138) and nothing settles it, so `balance_cents` stays 10_000 and the ongoing figure stays 4_000. An implementation that projected PURCHASED but unsettled credits into the ongoing balance — plausible, since the customer has been invoiced for them — would report balance 10_000 with ongoing_balance 9_000, i.e. a wallet that looks solvent on credits nobody has paid for. Asserting all three fields excludes it. invoices is 2: both `credit` top-up invoices. No billing ran, so there is no subscription invoice and no WalletTransactionConsumption — the ongoing path debits nothing.

The same wallet as the row above, with the top-up invoice paid on 2 March. Settling it moves the wallet transaction from pending to settled and raises the balance to 10 credits, so the period invoice now draws 1_000¢ of cover and the customer owes 3_000 − 1_000 = 2_000¢ — the same arithmetic the granted row reaches without a payment, because granted credits are free. Recording a payment through the API is itself premium: POST /payments answers 403 feature_unavailable without both License.premium? and the `manual_payments` premium integration on the organization, which is why this row declares both.

Rate 0.12345, five decimals, so 100 credits is 12.345 currency units — exactly on the half-cent. `WalletCredit` computes `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent)` then × 100 (wallet_credit.rb:26-27); BigDecimal#round is HALF-UP, so 12.345 → 12.35 → 1_235¢. A truncating implementation gives 12.34 → 1_234¢. Name both: prepaid 1_235 vs 1_234 and total 4_765 vs 4_766. The `credit` invoice the customer pays is for 1_235¢, so the rounding is money the customer was actually billed. Fees are 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢. The draw is min(6000, 1235, 6000) = 1_235 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53), the whole settled balance, leaving 4_765 owed and the wallet empty. The 6 March top-up of another 100 credits is never paid, so it neither settles nor raises the balance (create_from_params_service.rb:125-138 creates it `pending`; only Wallets::ApplyPaidCreditsService, driven by the payment, settles it). Had pending credits been spendable the prepaid would be 2_470 and the total 3_530 — the row therefore pins the rounding and the settlement boundary with the same numbers.

The settled twin of the paid row: paying the top-up invoice on 2 March runs Invoices::UpdateService:117 → PrepaidCreditJob → Wallets::ApplyPaidCreditsService, which moves the inbound transaction to settled and raises balance_cents to 10_000¢. Recording a payment through the API is itself premium (POST /payments answers 403 feature_unavailable without both License.premium? and `manual_payments`), so the row declares that integration alongside `events_targeting_wallets` — `apply_golden_organization` (golden_runner.rb:96-100) REPLACES the list, so both must be named together or the charge silently loses accepts_target_wallet. Fees 10_000¢: 60 units → 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_ps_fc_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20), 40 units → 4_000¢ tagged b06_twc_ps_fc_b, and the 0¢ subscription fee. Wallet a holds the whole invoice's worth and still pays only its own bucket, min(6_000, 10_000, 10_000) = 6_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53, gated by :109-114): full cover of the allowed slice with 4_000¢ of surplus that may NOT touch the b-tagged fee. Wallet b pays min(4_000, 1_000, 4_000) = 1_000, so 3_000¢ is owed in cash. The pool breakdown is the extra assertion this source makes possible: 6_000 purchased (wallet a) and 1_000 granted (wallet b) — the tag routed each pool onto its own fee, and a single prepaid_credit figure could not show that (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91). Tag-blind, one 10_000¢ bucket, wallet a at priority 1 pays all of it: prepaid 10_000 with purchased 10_000 and granted nil, total 0, balance 0. Name both: total 3_000 vs 0, balance 4_000 vs 0.

Target beats priority, with the pools proving which wallet actually paid. Three wallets: b06_twc_ps_mp_g at priority 1, granted, unrestricted, 10_000¢; b06_twc_ps_mp_a at priority 20, 100 purchased credits settled on 2 March, 10_000¢; b06_twc_ps_mp_d at priority 30, granted, 500¢. `Wallet.in_application_order` is priority ASC then created_at (wallet.rb:69-71), so g is reached first (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:126 over :34) and is refused BOTH buckets on the tag alone (:109-114) — before priority, fee types, metric targets or the unrestricted case matter. It keeps all 10_000¢. Buckets: 30 units → 3_000¢ tagged a (5/15/10: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 10) and 20 units → 2_000¢ tagged d. a pays its own 3_000¢, d pays min(2_000, 500, remaining) = 500 and empties. Prepaid 3_500 of 5_000¢ of fees, total 1_500 owed in cash next to an untouched priority-1 wallet. The breakdown says the same thing twice: purchased 3_000 can only have come from a and granted 500 from d, so g contributed nothing (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91). Tag-blind, one 5_000¢ bucket and g first in order pays all of it: prepaid 5_000 with granted 5_000 and purchased nil, total 0, g at 5_000¢. Name both: g 10_000 vs 5_000, total 1_500 vs 0.

10_000¢ of settled purchased credits against a 3_000¢ invoice whose only reachable fee is capped at 1_800¢ — the strongest form of "could the total go negative", and it does not. Draws are bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53, decremented at :57) and by the per-fee cap at :77-81, so 1_800¢ leaves the wallet, 8_200¢ stays, and 1_200¢ is still owed in cash. No credit note and no second `credit` invoice appear for the surplus: invoices is 2, the top-up and the period invoice. Fees 5_000¢: 30 units → 3_000¢ tagged b06_twc_ps_nt_a (10/15/5: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 5) and 20 units → 2_000¢ tagged b06_twc_ps_nt_b. The fixed_amount coupon spreads by weight (fee.rb:232-236 via credits/applied_coupon_service.rb:35-37): 2_000 × 3_000/5_000 = 1_200 onto the a fee, 800 onto the b fee, 0 onto the 0¢ subscription fee — caps 1_800 and 1_200. Wallet b is declared with no credits, so `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65) drops it from the allocator and its 1_200¢ is unpayable by anyone; wallet a is refused it by the tag (:109-114) while holding 8_200¢. Named alternatives: prepaid credit applied before the coupon would cap the a fee at 3_000 → prepaid 3_000, total 0, balance 7_000; a tag-blind allocator would pay both caps → the same prepaid 3_000 and total 0; draining the applicable balance → total −7_000. prepaid_purchased 1_800 with no granted figure confirms every cent came from the settled purchase (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91). The coupon is untouched by the top-up invoice because credit invoices never run the coupon or prepaid stages (invoices/paid_credit_service.rb:80-91).

A mid-period read with a SETTLED purchase, so balance_cents is a real 10_000¢ rather than the pending 0 of the paid twin, and the only invoice in the row is the paid top-up. The path is Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService, a SECOND implementation of the tag rule: it re-derives the key at allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-123 and re-implements the refusal at :127-130, so no billing row covers this branch. Current-usage fees keep their grouping (`UsageFilters::WITHOUT_PRESENTATION_FILTER` leaves skip_grouping false — fees/charge_service.rb:493-499), so the pool is two keys: 6_000¢ tagged a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b. Each key's `applicable` list holds one wallet, which is therefore also the last and takes the whole bucket (:47-58): wallet a reserves 6_000, not 10_000, and ongoing_balance = balance − ongoing_usage = 10_000 − 6_000 = 4_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63). Tag-blind, the keys merge into one 10_000¢ pool and wallet a — first in `in_application_order` (customers/refresh_wallets_service.rb:48), room 10_000 — absorbs all of it: ongoing_usage 10_000, ongoing_balance 0. Name both: 6_000 vs 10_000 and 4_000 vs 0. balance_cents stays 10_000 because the ongoing figures are a projection that never debits the wallet, and the current-usage payload is asserted alongside to show the customer still owes the whole 10_000¢. No WalletTransactionConsumption rows are written on this path, so there is no purchased/granted split to read mid-period even though this wallet is entirely purchased.

Settled purchased credits that run out inside their own bucket, next to a granted wallet holding five times the shortfall and forbidden to lend. The 20 purchased credits settle on 2 March (Invoices::UpdateService:117 → PrepaidCreditJob → Wallets::ApplyPaidCreditsService) and are worth 2_000¢ against a 6_000¢ tagged bucket: min(6_000, 2_000, 10_000) = 2_000 and wallet a is emptied (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53). Wallet b pays its own 4_000¢ bucket in full and keeps 6_000¢; `applicable_fee?` returns `wallet.code == target_wallet_code` before it looks at anything else (:109-114), so those 6_000¢ cannot reach a's 4_000¢ remainder, which is owed in cash. Fees 10_000¢ = 60 units tagged a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) + 40 units tagged b + the 0¢ subscription fee. The breakdown splits exactly along the tag: 2_000 purchased from a, 4_000 granted from b (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91). Tag-blind, the buckets merge, b covers the remaining 8_000 and ends at 2_000¢ with total 0 and purchased 2_000 / granted 8_000. Name both: b 6_000 vs 2_000, total 4_000 vs 0. Wallet b is the asserted wallet because a ends at 0 under either behaviour, and `expect.wallet` takes one wallet rather than a list.

The half-cent is charged to the customer and then spent. 50 credits at rate 0.6665 is 50 × 0.6665 = 33.325, and `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) rounds HALF-UP to 33.33 → a top-up invoice of 3_333¢, asserted directly; truncation would bill 3_332¢. Paying it on 2 March settles the transaction (Invoices::UpdateService:117 → PrepaidCreditJob → ApplyPaidCreditsService) so the whole 3_333¢ is spendable, and the same cent then reappears in the period invoice. Fees 8_000¢: 60 units → 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_ps_rn_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20), 20 units → 2_000¢ tagged b06_twc_ps_rn_b, plus the 0¢ subscription fee. Wallet a is confined to its own bucket and holds less than it, so it is drained for 3_333¢ exactly (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53); wallet b pays its own 2_000¢ and keeps 8_000¢ that may not reach a's 2_667¢ remainder (:109-114). Prepaid 5_333 = purchased 3_333 + granted 2_000, total 2_667. Truncation instead of half-up: top-up 3_332, prepaid 5_332, total 2_668. Ignoring the tag: b covers a's shortfall, prepaid 8_000 (purchased 3_333 + granted 4_667), total 0, b at 5_333¢. The pair (total 2_667, wallet b 8_000) separates all three, and the purchased/granted split confirms which wallet each cent came from (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91).

Two metered charges on a taxed invoice: the covered metric bills 60 units at 0.50 = 3_000¢ (+600¢ tax) and the uncovered one 80 units = 4_000¢ (+800¢ tax). The wallet is limited by WalletTarget rather than fee type, so its targets are [["charge", covered_metric_id]] and its allowed_fee_types are empty — a different branch of `applicable_fee?` (target_match, not type_match, allocate:108-120), which is why this cell exists separately from the fee-types one. Bucket keys are [fee_type, billable_metric_id] (allocate:81), so the two charges are separate buckets and the covered one is capped at 3_000 + 600 = 3_600 (allocate:77-79 — the ceiling includes the fee's own tax). The plan is 0¢, so its subscription fee is skipped for having a zero sub-total (allocate:75) and creates no bucket at all. With 5_000¢ spendable, the bucket is binding: 3_600 paid, 4_800¢ (the uncovered charge plus its tax) still owed in cash, and 1_400¢ stranded on the wallet. The uncovered bucket is deliberately the LARGER one, because buckets are consumed largest-first (allocate:89): an implementation that ignored the limitation would spend all 5_000¢ starting on the uncovered charge, giving a total of 3_400¢ and a balance of 0. An implementation using the pre-tax amount as the ceiling would pay 3_000 and leave 5_400¢ owed with 2_000¢ on the wallet. And if the pending 20 purchased credits were spendable the balance would end at 3_400¢. Three distinct wrong answers, all excluded.

Both wallets target the SAME metric, so the only question left is order. Each carries a pending 30-credit purchase (three invoices), leaving 1_200¢ spendable at priority 1 and 4_000¢ at priority 20. The uncovered metric's 4_000¢ charge fee is the fee neither wallet may pay, and total_amount_cents 4_000 is the assertion that it is still owed in cash. Buckets: 4_000 (uncovered) then 3_000 (covered), largest-first (allocate:89); both wallets skip the first. In priority order (wallet.rb:69) the priority-1 wallet pays min(3_000, 1_200, 7_000) = 1_200 and empties, then the priority-20 wallet pays min(1_800, 4_000, 5_800) = 1_800. Declared low-priority-first so creation order disagrees with priority order, and the asserted balance separates every wrong answer: correct order 4_000 - 1_800 = 2_200¢; creation order would drain 3_000 and leave 1_000¢; ignoring the target would let the pair also spend on the 4_000 bucket (total 1_800¢, balance 0); and spending the pending purchased credits would let the priority-1 wallet's 4_200¢ cover the whole covered bucket alone, leaving the second at 7_000¢.

10_000¢ of spendable credit targeted at one metric, against 3_000¢ on that metric and 60¢ on another. After covering its own bucket in full the wallet still holds 7_000¢ — far more than the whole rest of the invoice. Four outcomes are conceivable: (a) the debit stops at the targeted bucket and 60¢ is owed in cash, (b) the excess spills onto the untargeted charge and the invoice reaches 0, (c) the total goes negative, (d) a credit note or refund appears for the excess. The implementation gives (a). Bucket keys carry the billable_metric_id (allocate:81) and `applicable_fee?` matches the wallet's WalletTarget pair ["charge", metric_id] (allocate:108-120), so the other metric's bucket is unreachable no matter how much credit is left. Every debit is also capped by remaining_invoice_amount (allocate:31,53), which is what makes (c) impossible in general, and the prepaid path creates no credit note, so `invoices: 2` — purchase plus period — excludes (d). So 0.60 is invoiced and the invoice stays `pending` while 70.00 of usable credit sits beside it. total_amount_cents 60 (not 0, not -6_940) and balance_cents 7_000 (not 0, and not the 9_000 an implementation that spent the pending purchased credits would leave) are the two numbers that say so.

A mid-period read on the ONGOING path (Customers::RefreshWalletsService -> Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService); nothing is billed, so no prepaid credit is applied and the invoice-time allocator never runs. Unbilled usage is 5_000¢ — 3_000¢ on the targeted metric (60 units) and 2_000¢ on the other (40 units) — under two separate fee keys, because the key carries the billable_metric_id (allocate_ongoing:118-123). The wallet targets only the first, so `applicable_fee?` (allocate_ongoing:126-134) leaves the 2_000¢ key with no applicable wallet at all and it is simply not allocated. For the 3_000¢ key the wallet is the only, hence last, applicable wallet, so it absorbs the whole amount and is allowed to go negative (allocate_ongoing:48-51): ongoing_usage_balance_cents = 3_000, ongoing_balance_cents = 1_200 - 3_000 = -1_800 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:62-63). The row asserts a positive allocation and an exclusion at the same time, so it cannot be passed by an implementation that allocates nothing. Ignore the target and the wallet would absorb all 5_000¢, giving -3_800. Reuse the invoice-time clamp and it would report 1_200 / 0 rather than 3_000 / -1_800. Count the pending 20 purchased credits as money and balance_cents would read 3_200 with ongoing_balance +200. The 2_000¢ of usage the wallet may not cover is asserted through the usage payload, which still reports the full 5_000¢ as owed.

Two wallets, each targeting one metric, each with a pending 30-credit purchase (three invoices) so the spendable balances are 1_200¢ and 5_000¢ rather than 4_200¢ and 8_000¢. Buckets: the second metric's charge 4_000¢ and the first metric's 3_000¢, consumed largest-first (allocate:89); the 0¢ subscription fee makes no bucket (allocate:75). The priority-1 wallet may not touch the 4_000 bucket, so it pays min(3_000, 1_200, 7_000) = 1_200 of the 3_000 bucket — a partial cover of its own metric. The priority-20 wallet then pays its 4_000 bucket in full and stops: the 1_800¢ left on the first metric is not its metric, so 7_000 - 5_200 = 1_800¢ is owed in cash while 1_000¢ of credit sits unusable. That 1_000¢ leftover is what makes the limitation observable at all. Where a wallet's balance is the binding constraint, the invoice total cannot see WHICH fee was paid — so the row is built so the second wallet is stopped by its target, not by its balance. Drop the limitations and the numbers move: the priority-1 wallet's 1_200 lands on the larger bucket, the second wallet then pays 2_800 there plus 2_200 on the other, prepaid becomes 6_200, the total 800¢ and its balance 0. Both asserted values change.

3.5 credits at a rate of 0.33 is 1.155 — a tie at the half cent. `(credit_amount * rate_amount).round(currency.exponent)` (wallet_credit.rb:26) uses BigDecimal's ROUND_HALF_UP, so the purchase invoice and the granted pool are both 116¢, not the 115¢ truncation gives. The credit fee's `units` pins the other direction of the conversion: an invoiceable credit is recomputed from the ROUNDED amount, `amount.fdiv(rate_amount)` (wallet_credit.rb:29-32), so the customer is billed 1.16 / 0.33 = 3.51515 credits rather than the 3.5 requested. The targeted metric is priced at 0.01, so its bucket is 60¢ — smaller than the wallet. The wallet pays min(60, 116, 4_060) = 60 and the untargeted metric's 4_000¢ is owed in cash. The rounding then shows up in the residue: 116 - 60 = 56¢ stranded, or 55¢ under truncation. Ignore the target and the wallet would instead spend all 116¢ on the 4_000¢ bucket (consumed first, allocate:89), giving a total of 3_944¢ and a zero balance — so 4_000 and 56 test the limitation while 56-versus-55 and 3.51515-versus-3.5 test the rounding.

Two fee types on one taxed invoice: a 5_000¢ subscription fee (+1_000¢ tax) and a 3_000¢ charge fee (+600¢ tax), 8_000¢ of fees and 9_600¢ due. The wallet is limited to fee_type `charge`, so `applicable_fee?` matches only the charge bucket (allocate:108-120 — type_match on fee_key.first, with unrestricted_wallet false because types is non-empty). The subscription fee is a fee this wallet may NOT pay, and the assertion that it is still owed in cash is total_amount_cents 6_000 = 5_000 + 1_000: an implementation that ignored limitations would pay all 9_600 and land on 0. The ceiling of the allowed bucket is the number this row exists for. It is `sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents + taxes_precise_amount_cents - precise_credit_notes_amount_cents` (allocate:77-81), i.e. 3_000 + 600 = 3_600 — a wallet may pay the tax on a fee it is allowed to pay. An implementation using the pre-tax amount as the ceiling would pay 3_000 and leave 6_600¢ owed with 7_000¢ on the wallet. With 10_000¢ available the bucket, not the balance, is binding, which is why "full cover" here means the allowed portion is covered whole and 6_400¢ is left stranded on the wallet. balance_cents 6_400 also excludes the pending purchase: if the 20 purchased credits counted, the pool would be 12_000¢ and the leftover 8_400¢. prepaid_granted equal to prepaid_credit says the same thing from the invoice side.

Both wallets are limited to fee_type `charge` and both carry a pending 30-credit purchase, so spendable balances are 1_200¢ (priority 1) and 4_000¢ (priority 20), and there are three invoices. The 5_000¢ subscription fee is the fee neither wallet may pay: it is still owed in cash, which is total_amount_cents 5_000. Only the 3_000¢ charge bucket is payable. In priority order (wallet.rb:69) the priority-1 wallet pays min(3_000, 1_200, 8_000) = 1_200 and empties; the priority-20 wallet pays min(1_800, 4_000, 6_800) = 1_800. Prepaid 3_000¢. The wallets are declared low-priority-first so creation order and priority order disagree, and the asserted balance separates every wrong answer: correct order leaves the second wallet at 4_000 - 1_800 = 2_200¢; consuming in creation order drains 3_000 from it and leaves 1_000¢; ignoring the limitation lets it also spend on the subscription bucket, taking it to 0 with a total of 2_800¢; and treating the pending purchased credits as money would let the priority-1 wallet (4_200¢) cover the whole charge bucket alone and leave the second at 7_000¢.

A wallet holding 10_000¢ of spendable credit, allowed to pay only charge fees, against an invoice of 3_000¢ of charge and 60¢ of subscription. After paying the charge bucket in full it still has 7_000¢ — more than a hundred times what is left owed. Four outcomes are conceivable: (a) the debit stops at the allowed bucket and 60¢ is owed in cash, (b) the excess spills onto the disallowed subscription fee and the invoice reaches 0, (c) the invoice goes negative, (d) a credit note or refund is issued for the excess. The implementation gives (a). `applicable_fee?` (allocate:108-120) rejects the ["subscription", nil] bucket outright, so there is nothing for the excess to spill onto; each debit is additionally capped by remaining_invoice_amount (allocate:31,53), which is why (c) cannot happen even without a limitation; and no credit note is created anywhere in the prepaid path, so `invoices: 2` — purchase plus period — rules out (d). So a customer with 70.00 of usable credit is still invoiced 0.60 and the invoice stays `pending`. That is the whole finding of the row, and the two numbers that carry it are total_amount_cents 60 (not 0, not -6_940) and balance_cents 7_000 (not 0, and not the 9_000 an implementation spending the pending purchased credits would leave).

A mid-period read on the ONGOING path (Customers::RefreshWalletsService -> Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService), not the invoice-time one: nothing is billed, so no prepaid credit is applied. Current usage is charge fees only (customer_usage_service.rb:103,120), 60 units at 0.50 = 3_000¢ under the single key ["charge", metric, nil, EUR]. The priority-1 wallet is limited to fee_type `subscription`, so `applicable_fee?` (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-134) excludes it from that key entirely and the priority-20 unrestricted wallet is the only — and therefore last — applicable wallet: it absorbs the whole 3_000¢. ongoing_balance_cents = 4_000 - 3_000 = 1_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:62-63). The row asserts the UNRESTRICTED wallet on purpose, because that is where the limitation is visible as a positive number rather than as an absence. If limitations were ignored in the ongoing path, both wallets would be applicable and the non-last one would be capped at its room (allocate_ongoing:52-55): the priority-1 wallet would take 1_200 and the asserted wallet only 1_800, leaving ongoing_balance 2_200. And if the pending purchased 30 credits counted as money, balance_cents would read 7_000 and ongoing_balance 4_000. `invoices: 2` is the two purchase invoices; the 3_000¢ of usage is unbilled.

Two disjointly limited wallets: one may pay only charge fees (1_200¢ spendable), the other only subscription fees (7_000¢ spendable). Each also carries a pending 30-credit purchase, so there are three invoices and the spendable balances are NOT 4_200 and 10_000. Buckets are consumed largest first (`ordered = remaining.sort_by { -v }`, allocate:89): subscription 5_000 then charge 3_000. The charge wallet skips the subscription bucket and pays min(3_000, 1_200, 8_000) = 1_200 of the charge fee. The subscription wallet then pays min(5_000, 7_000, 6_800) = 5_000 of the subscription fee and STOPS — the 1_800¢ still owed on the charge fee is a fee it may not pay, so 8_000 - 6_200 = 1_800¢ is owed in cash even though 2_000¢ of credit is sitting on the wallet. That stranded 2_000¢ is what makes the limitation observable. When a wallet's balance is the binding constraint the invoice total is blind to WHICH fee it paid, so this row is built so the limitation, not the balance, stops the second wallet. Ignore limitations and the answer moves: the charge wallet's 1_200 goes to the subscription bucket, the other wallet then pays 3_800 of subscription plus 1_800 of charge = 5_600, giving prepaid 6_800, a total of 1_200¢ and a leftover of 1_400¢. Both asserted numbers change. Priority is deliberately not load-bearing here — the wallets are limited to disjoint fee types, so swapping their priorities gives the same split. The ordering question belongs to the multi-wallet-priority cell.

Same half-cent as the unlimited rounding row, made visible through a limitation. 3.5 credits at 0.33 is 1.155, and `(credit_amount * rate_amount).round(currency.exponent)` (wallet_credit.rb:26) rounds HALF-UP to 1.16 — so both the purchase invoice and the granted pool are 116¢, where truncation would give 115¢. The charge fee is deliberately tiny: 60 units at 0.01 = 60¢, smaller than the wallet. The wallet may pay only charge fees, so it pays min(60, 116, 5_060) = 60 and the 5_000¢ subscription fee is owed in cash. The residue is where the rounding lands: 116 - 60 = 56¢ stranded on the wallet, or 55¢ under the truncating alternative. The limitation is what strands it. Without it the wallet would spend all 116¢ against the 5_000¢ subscription bucket (consumed first, allocate:89), giving a total of 4_944¢ and a balance of 0 — so both the 5_000 total and the 56¢ balance test the limitation, and the 56 versus 55 tests the rounding.

One wallet holding BOTH pools. The 20 purchased credits create an inbound transaction with status `pending` and transaction_status `purchased` (create_from_params_service.rb:129,131) plus a finalized-but-unpaid `credit` invoice of 20 x 1.00 = 2_000¢ — credit fees are never taxed (fees/paid_credit_service.rb:36), so that invoice is exactly 2_000¢ even under a taxed organization. Those credits are worth nothing until Invoices::PrepaidCreditJob:20-21 runs ApplyPaidCreditsService on a SUCCEEDED payment, which never happens here, so `balance_cents` carries only the 50 granted credits = 5_000¢. Three events (10+30+20) give 60 units at 0.50 = 3_000¢ — three, because one event cannot tell sum_agg (60) from max_agg (30) or latest_agg (20). Prepaid credit is the last reducer (calculate_fees_service.rb:62): the single bucket ["charge", metric] has cap 3_000 + 0 tax = 3_000 (allocate:77-81) and the wallet pays min(3_000, 5_000, 3_000) = 3_000 (allocate:53), so the invoice lands at 0 and is stamped `succeeded`. The wallet keeps 5_000 - 3_000 = 2_000¢. Two wrong implementations are excluded by balance_cents alone. If the pending purchased credits were spendable the pool would be 7_000¢ and the balance would end at 4_000¢, not 2_000¢. If wallets were ignored the total would be 3_000¢. And because prepaid_granted_credit_amount_cents (3_000) equals prepaid_credit_amount_cents (3_000), every cent came from the granted pool — the purchased pool moved nothing (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:73-91 builds that split from WalletTransactionConsumption rows, and only a GRANTED inbound gets a remaining_amount_cents to be consumed from, wallet_transactions/create_service.rb:56-62).

Two wallets, each with a pending purchased top-up of 30 credits and a settled grant. That makes three invoices — two `credit` invoices of 3_000¢ each plus the period invoice — and spendable balances of 1_200¢ (priority 1) and 4_000¢ (priority 20), not 4_200¢ and 7_000¢, because a purchased top-up is created `pending` (create_from_params_service.rb:129) and only Invoices::PrepaidCreditJob:20-21 on a succeeded payment turns it into balance. Consumption follows `priority` ascending, not creation order (wallet.rb:69 `order(:priority, :created_at)`, used by applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:114), so the wallets are declared in the wrong order on purpose. The single bucket ["charge", metric] is 3_000¢. The priority-1 wallet pays min(3_000, 1_200, 3_000) = 1_200 and is emptied; the priority-20 wallet then pays min(1_800, 4_000, 1_800) = 1_800 (allocate:53). Total prepaid 3_000¢, invoice 0.
