The row asserts the SECOND wallet, because that is the number the order decides: correct order leaves it at 4_000 - 1_800 = 2_200¢, the wrong order (creation order, or descending priority) drains 3_000 from it and leaves 1_000¢, and an implementation that spent the pending purchased credits would let the priority-1 wallet (4_200¢) absorb the whole invoice and leave the second untouched at 7_000¢. One assertion kills all three. `expect.wallet` takes a single wallet, not a list, so the first wallet's balance is pinned indirectly: prepaid_credit_amount_cents 3_000 minus the second wallet's 1_800 consumption leaves exactly 1_200, which is its whole spendable balance.

10_000¢ of spendable credit against a 3_000¢ invoice. Three outcomes are conceivable and the row does not assume one: (a) the debit is clamped to what is owed, (b) the wallet is drained and the invoice goes to -7_000¢, (c) the excess becomes a credit note or a refund invoice. The implementation gives (a). `remaining_invoice_amount` is seeded from invoice.total_amount_cents (allocate:31) and every debit is min(bucket_remaining, wallet_remaining, remaining_invoice_amount) (allocate:53), so no allocation can exceed what is still owed; refresh_amounts then subtracts exactly that (calculate_fees_service.rb:394-396), landing on 0. Nothing in the prepaid path creates a credit note, so `invoices` stays at 2 — the purchase invoice and the period invoice — and (c) is excluded by the count. (b) is excluded twice over: by the clamp, and by `validates :balance_cents, numericality: {greater_than_or_equal_to: 0}, if: :traceable?` (wallet.rb:54), which would reject a wallet debited past its balance. The leftover balance is the load-bearing number: 10_000 - 3_000 = 7_000¢. An implementation spending the still-pending 20 purchased credits would leave 9_000¢, and one that drained the wallet on full cover would leave 0.

A mid-period read, and a different code path from every other row in this slice: no invoice is billed, so Credits::AllocatePrepaidCreditsByWalletsService never runs. The number comes from Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob -> Customers::RefreshWalletsService -> Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService, and it is the ONGOING path. Current usage is 60 units at 0.50 = 3_000¢ and consists of charge fees only (customer_usage_service.rb:103,120 — the subscription fee is not part of current usage at all). The single unrestricted wallet is the last applicable wallet for that fee key, so it absorbs the whole amount and is explicitly allowed to go negative (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:48-51): ongoing_usage_balance_cents = 3_000 and ongoing_balance_cents = balance_cents - ongoing_usage = 1_200 - 3_000 = -1_800 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:62-63). That negative is the point. The invoice-time path clamps at the balance, so an implementation that reused it here would report 1_200 / 0 instead of 3_000 / -1_800. And the pending purchased 20 credits are still not money: were they counted, balance_cents would read 3_200 and ongoing_balance_cents +200 rather than -1_800. `invoices: 1` is the purchase invoice alone — the 3_000¢ of usage is unbilled, which is exactly what makes it "ongoing".

PAID credits are sold, so buying them issues a separate invoice of type `credit` for the top-up — two invoices where the granted row has one. But the purchase is not money yet: the wallet transaction is created PENDING and the balance only rises once that top-up invoice is settled. So the period invoice gets 0¢ of cover and the customer owes the full 3_000¢, even though a wallet with 10 credits appears to exist. The paired row below settles the top-up and gets the 1_000¢ of cover; the two together pin the boundary between credits bought and credits usable.

3.5 credits at a rate of 0.33 is 1.155 — exactly half a cent. WalletCredit rounds the MONEY, not the credits: `@amount = (credit_amount * rate_amount).round(currency.exponent)` (wallet_credit.rb:26) with BigDecimal's default ROUND_HALF_UP gives 1.16, so amount_cents = 116. Truncating or rounding half-down would give 115, and that one cent is visible three times in this row: the purchase invoice is 116¢ not 115¢, the granted pool is 116¢ not 115¢, and the period invoice ends at 3_000 - 116 = 2_884¢ rather than 2_885¢. The credit fee's `units` pins the second half of the conversion. An invoiceable credit is re-derived FROM the rounded amount — `amount.fdiv(wallet.rate_amount)` (wallet_credit.rb:29-32) — so the customer is billed for 1.16 / 0.33 = 3.51515 credits, not the 3.5 they asked for. An implementation that kept the requested 3.5 would put 3.5 here and would then disagree with its own 116¢ price. The purchased 116¢ stays pending (create_from_params_service.rb:129) and the granted 116¢ is what the invoice draws on, which is why prepaid_credit_amount_cents equals prepaid_granted_credit_amount_cents. Both are 116, so 2_884¢ is still owed in cash.

`source: paid` means the purchase is PENDING: the 40 purchased credits create an inbound transaction with status pending (wallet_transactions/create_from_params_service.rb:129) and a finalized-but-unpaid `credit` invoice of 40 × 1.00 = 4_000¢ — credit fees are never taxed (fees/paid_credit_service.rb:36). Pending credits are excluded from `balance_cents` (wallet_transaction.rb:80, inbound.settled), so the wallet's spendable pool is only the 100 granted credits = 10_000¢. A row funded ONLY with pending paid credits would assert 0 prepaid and would pass under an implementation that ignored wallets entirely, so both pools are funded and the row asserts that the granted one moved while the purchased one did not. Two tagged charge fees (fees/charge_service.rb:496-499): 60 units → 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_p_fc_a (10/30/20, so sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 40 units → 4_000¢ tagged b06_twc_p_fc_b, plus the 0¢ subscription fee = 10_000¢. Wallet a may only pay its own bucket (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:83-85, :109-114): min(6_000, 10_000, 10_000) = 6_000, full cover of the allowed slice with 4_000¢ left over. Wallet b pays min(4_000, 1_000, 4_000) = 1_000. Prepaid 7_000, total 3_000 owed in cash — wallet a's 4_000¢ surplus is forbidden from covering it. Three implementations are excluded by the pair (total 3_000, balance 4_000). If the pending purchase were spendable the pool would be 14_000¢, wallet a would still pay only its 6_000¢ bucket and end at 8_000¢. If the tag were ignored there would be one 10_000¢ bucket, wallet a (priority 1) would pay all of it and end at 0 with total 0. If credits were applied before taxes or coupons nothing would move here (neither exists), which is why fees_amount and taxes are asserted too. prepaid_granted 7_000 = prepaid_credit proves the purchased pool contributed nothing (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91).

Target beats priority, and the wallet that proves it is the one that never moves. Three wallets: b06_twc_p_mp_g at priority 1 holding 10_000¢ and unrestricted, b06_twc_p_mp_a at priority 20 holding 10_000¢ spendable (its 30 purchased credits are pending and excluded from balance_cents), b06_twc_p_mp_d at priority 30 holding 500¢. `Wallet.in_application_order` is priority ASC then created_at (wallet.rb:69-71), so the allocator reaches g FIRST (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:126 over :34). Both charge fees carry a tag — 30 units → 3_000¢ tagged a (5/15/10: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 10) and 20 units → 2_000¢ tagged d — so `applicable_fee?` (:109-114) refuses g for both of them, on the tag alone, before priority or the unrestricted case is consulted. g contributes NOTHING and keeps all 10_000¢. a pays its own 3_000¢, d pays min(2_000, 500, remaining) = 500 and is emptied. Prepaid 3_500, fees 5_000, total 1_500 owed in cash while the priority-1 wallet sits untouched. That last figure is the whole assertion. Tag-blind, the buckets merge into one 5_000¢ pool and g, first in order and unrestricted, pays all of it: prepaid 5_000, total 0, g at 5_000¢. Name both: g 10_000 vs 5_000, total 1_500 vs 0. prepaid_granted 3_500 = prepaid_credit, so a's pending purchase contributed nothing (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:74-91), and the `credit` invoice for it stays pending at 3_000¢ — invoices 2.

Over-funded wallet, tag-confined fee, and a coupon in front of it: the case where the total could go negative. It cannot. 100 granted credits = 10_000¢ are spendable and the 40 purchased ones are pending (create_from_params_service.rb:129), and the wallet still leaves 8_200¢ untouched while 1_200¢ stays owed in cash. No `credit` invoice for the surplus and no credit note is issued — the only credit invoice is the 4_000¢ top-up, which is why invoices is 2 and its payment_status is asserted pending. Fees 5_000¢: 30 units → 3_000¢ tagged b06_twc_p_nt_a (10/15/5: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 5) and 20 units → 2_000¢ tagged b06_twc_p_nt_b, plus the 0¢ subscription fee. The fixed_amount coupon spreads by weight, `credit × (amount_cents − precise_coupons) / invoice.sub_total` (fee.rb:232-236 through credits/applied_coupon_service.rb:35-37): 1_200 onto the a fee, 800 onto the b fee. Caps become `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:77-79) = 1_800 and 1_200. Wallet b has no credits at all, so `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65) removes it from the allocator and its 1_200¢ cannot be paid by anybody; wallet a is refused it by the tag (:109-114). Prepaid 1_800, total 1_200, balance 10_000 − 1_800 = 8_200. The named alternatives: credits applied before the coupon would cap the a fee at 3_000, giving prepaid 3_000, total 0 and balance 7_000; a tag-blind allocator would pay both caps for the same prepaid 3_000 and total 0; draining the applicable balance would give total −7_000. The coupon survives the top-up invoice because credit invoices never run the coupon or prepaid stages (invoices/paid_credit_service.rb:80-91), even though the coupon is applied before the wallet is created (golden_runner.rb:58-60).

A mid-period read on the OTHER implementation of the rule — no billing runs, so the only invoice in the row is the pending 4_000¢ top-up. Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService re-derives the tag at allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-123 and re-implements the refusal at :127-130; current-usage fees are grouped exactly as billed ones because `UsageFilters::WITHOUT_PRESENTATION_FILTER` leaves skip_grouping false (fees/charge_service.rb:493-499). The pool is `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents` per key (:88): 6_000¢ tagged a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b. Each bucket's `applicable` list holds exactly one wallet, so it is also the last one and takes the whole bucket (:47-58): wallet a reserves 6_000 and not the 4_000 that belongs to b, so ongoing_balance = 10_000 − 6_000 = 4_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63). `balance_cents` is 10_000, not 14_000: the 40 purchased credits are pending and excluded (create_from_params_service.rb:129; wallet_transaction.rb:80) — and if they were counted the ongoing balance would read 8_000 instead of 4_000, which is the second thing this row separates. Tag-blind, the keys merge into one 10_000¢ pool and wallet a, first in `in_application_order` with room 10_000, absorbs all of it: ongoing_usage 10_000 and ongoing_balance 0. Name all three: ongoing_usage 6_000 vs 10_000, ongoing_balance 4_000 vs 0 vs 8_000. The current-usage payload is asserted alongside because the customer still owes the whole 10_000¢ — the ongoing figures are a projection that never debits the wallet, and no WalletTransactionConsumption rows exist on this path, so there is no granted/purchased split to read.

Partial cover under the tag: the targeted wallet runs dry INSIDE its own bucket while a wallet holding five times the shortfall is forbidden to finish it. Wallet a's 60 purchased credits are pending and unspendable (create_from_params_service.rb:129; wallet_transaction.rb:80), so its pool is the 20 granted credits = 2_000¢ against its own 6_000¢ bucket: min(6_000, 2_000, 10_000) = 2_000 and it is emptied (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53). Wallet b pays its own 4_000¢ bucket in full — min(4_000, 10_000, 8_000) = 4_000 — and keeps 6_000¢ that it may NOT put against a's 4_000¢ remainder, because `applicable_fee?` returns `wallet.code == target_wallet_code` before it considers targets, types or the unrestricted case (:109-114). Fees 10_000¢ = 60 units tagged a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) + 40 units tagged b + the 0¢ subscription fee; prepaid 6_000; 4_000¢ still owed in cash. Wallet b is the asserted wallet because a ends at 0 under both behaviours. Tag-blind, the two buckets merge into one 10_000¢ pool, a pays 2_000, b pays the remaining 8_000 and ends at 2_000¢ with total 0. Name both: b 6_000 vs 2_000, total 4_000 vs 0. Index 1 is the target wallet, and a wallet with an active threshold rule is deliberately allowed to absorb everything and go negative so its rule can refill it (:48-51, threshold_wallet? at :139-141), so it takes the remaining 4_000. Its credits_ongoing_balance is therefore −40, not −60, and the rule asks for 10 − (−40) = 50 credits = 5_000¢ granted (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150). An implementation that let the threshold wallet swallow the whole 6_000 regardless of the cascade would ask for 70 credits: name both, target-wallet balance 1_000 vs 3_000 at the end. At billing the draw is again in priority order and the amounts are chosen so the order CHANGES the split: purchased first takes min(6_000, 2_000, 6_000) = 2_000, then the target wallet takes min(4_000, 5_000, 4_000) = 4_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53-57). Total prepaid 6_000, total 0, and the breakdown is 2_000 purchased / 4_000 granted. Creation order first would draw 5_000 from the target wallet and 1_000 from the purchased one — 5_000 granted / 1_000 purchased, and the target wallet emptied instead of holding 1_000. No re-arm: 1_000¢ left is credits_ongoing_balance 10, above threshold 0 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20).

A target rule over-funds by construction here, which is the cleanest way to ask what Lago does when a wallet is worth more than the invoice. target_ongoing_balance 100 against 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of unbilled usage: at the 6 March refresh credits_ongoing_balance is −60, so the gap is 100 − (−60) = 160 credits = 16_000¢ of granted credit (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150), against an invoice that will owe only 4_000¢. Lago CLAMPS and leaves the surplus in the wallet. Every draw is bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53, decremented at :57), so exactly 4_000¢ leaves and 12_000¢ stays. The three alternatives, named: (a) total −12_000 if the applicable balance were drained, (b) a `credit` invoice or credit note for the 12_000 surplus — none is issued, invoices stays 1, (c) the wallet drained to 0. None happens. The 4_000 ceiling is the row's second half, and it is what the coupon is for. Prepaid credit is the LAST reducer (calculate_fees_service.rb:53-62: progressive billing → coupon → tax → credit note → prepaid) and the per-fee cap is `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:77-79) where `sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents = amount_cents − precise_coupons_amount_cents`: 6_000 − 2_000 = 4_000, which equals invoice.total so `reconcile_remaining_amounts` (:93-106) adds nothing. Credits applied BEFORE the coupon would have taken 6_000 and left 10_000 — name both, prepaid 4_000 vs 6_000 and wallet 12_000 vs 10_000. A third fact only a target rule can show: the top-up is sized against GROSS unbilled usage. Ongoing usage is pooled as `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents` (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:90) with no coupon subtracted, so the rule funds 16_000¢ for an invoice that will only ever need 4_000 — it over-funds by exactly the coupon. A rule that netted the pending coupon would have asked for 140 credits and ended on 10_000¢. No re-arm: 12_000¢ left is credits_ongoing_balance 120, above threshold_credits 0 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20).

A mid-period read with NO invoice anywhere, and for a target rule it is the only surface on which the method's defining claim is directly visible: after the rule fires, ongoing_balance_cents equals the target. `perform_wallet_refresh` runs Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8, hence `premium: true`) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService, a reimplementation of the billing allocator rather than the same code (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:33-65). The refresh runs twice and the two passes are the row. Pass one: balance 0, unbilled usage 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ (pooled as `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents`, :90), so ongoing_usage_balance_cents 6_000, ongoing_balance_cents −6_000, credits_ongoing_balance −60 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:62-68) — a single threshold wallet is allowed to go negative (:48-51). Persisting that changes the wallet's ongoing columns, which is what arms the rule: `state_changed` is exactly `saved_change_to_ongoing_usage_balance_cents? || saved_change_to_ongoing_balance_cents?` (update_ongoing_service.rb:18-19) and the rule is skipped outright without it (threshold_top_up_service.rb:18). −60 is not above threshold_credits 0, so the rule asks for 25 − (−60) = 85 credits = 8_500¢ granted. Wallets::Balance::IncreaseService then re-enqueues the refresh (increase_service.rb:36), and pass two reports ongoing_usage 6_000 against a balance of 8_500 → ongoing_balance 2_500 = 25 credits, which IS above threshold 0, so the rule stops (:20). It converges after exactly one top-up. The alternatives, named: a rule sizing the gap against `balance_cents` (0) would grant 25 credits and leave balance 2_500 with ongoing_balance 2_500 − 6_000 = −3_500; a rule that clamped the ongoing balance at zero would never see −60 and would grant 25 credits as well. So balance_cents 8_500 vs 2_500 and ongoing_balance_cents +2_500 vs −3_500 are the discriminating pair, and asserting both is what makes this a target row rather than a restatement of the granted one. invoices is 0 and consumed_amount_cents is 0: a GRANTED target top-up raises no invoice (create_from_params_service.rb:145-173) and the ongoing figures are a projection that never debits the wallet.

A target rule is sized WHEN IT FIRES, against the usage visible at that instant — so the way to make a target rule under-cover is to let usage grow after the top-up. 12 units (2+6+4) exist at the 4 March refresh: ongoing_usage_balance_cents 1_200, balance 0, credits_ongoing_balance −12 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:54-68). target_ongoing_balance is 0, so the gap is 0 − (−12) = 12 credits = 1_200¢ (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150) — a target of zero means "fund exactly the unbilled usage", which is the sharpest statement of what the method measures. grants_target_top_up is true, so the credits are GRANTED: settled immediately, no invoice (create_from_params_service.rb:145-173), which is why invoices stays 1. Then 60 more units (10/30/20 — sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) arrive with no refresh between, so the period invoice is 72 units × 1.00 = 7_200¢ against a 1_200¢ wallet: prepaid is min(7_200, 1_200, 7_200) = 1_200 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53) and 6_000¢ stays owed in cash. Two wrong implementations, both named: a rule measuring the gap against `balance_cents` (0) would top up 0 − 0 = 0 credits, prepaid 0 and total 7_200; a rule evaluated at billing time instead of at the refresh would see 72 units and top up 7_200¢, prepaid 7_200 and total 0. The re-arm after billing is a provable no-op rather than an omission: the wallet is drained to 0 and the synchronous refresh (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:39) reports credits_ongoing_balance 0, which is NOT above threshold_credits 0, so threshold_top_up_service.rb:23 runs — but compute_target_top_up_amount returns 0.0 when ongoing_balance >= target (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:139-141), and CreateFromParamsService creates nothing for a zero amount (:115, :146). balance_cents 0 and consumed 1_200 therefore also assert that no second top-up appeared.

A target rule rounds TWICE, and the two roundings are in different units. First, the ongoing balance the gap is measured against is computed in CREDITS by float division and stored in a decimal(30,5) column: `ongoing_balance_cents.to_f.fdiv(100).fdiv(rate_amount)` (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:66-68). 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of unbilled usage against a 0¢ balance gives −6_000¢, and −60 / 0.3333 = −180.018001800180…, stored as −180.01800. Second, the credits the rule asks for are converted back to money by `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27), a HALF-UP round of the currency amount and not a truncation. target_ongoing_balance 9.982 is chosen so the gap is exact: 9.982 − (−180.018) = 190.00000 credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:143). 190 × 0.3333 = 63.327, which HALF-UP is 63.33 → 6_333¢ of granted credits. TRUNCATING would give 63.32 → 6_332¢. Name both: the top-up is 6_333 vs 6_332 and the wallet ends on 333¢ vs 332¢. A third wrong answer, the rule measuring its gap against `balance_cents` (0) rather than the ongoing balance: 9.982 × 0.3333 = 3.32700 → 3.33 → 333¢ of top-up, prepaid 333 and total 5_667. Three events 10/30/20 so sum 60 is distinguishable from max 30 and latest 20. The invoice is 6_000¢ and the wallet holds 6_333¢, so prepaid is min(6_000, 6_333, 6_000) = 6_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53) and the residue is 333¢ — the rounding survives into the asserted balance rather than being absorbed by the invoice. No re-arm: 333¢ is credits_ongoing_balance 9.991, above threshold_credits 0 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20).

A `method: target` rule tops up TO `target_ongoing_balance` and derives the amount as a gap against CREDITS_ONGOING_BALANCE — balance MINUS unbilled usage (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150 via compute_granted_credits :104-112) — so under this limitation the tag decides the SIZE of the top-up. The wallet declares no credits of its own; every credit here is sized by the rule. Two tagged charge fees (fees/charge_service.rb:496-499): 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_tm_fc_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b06_twc_tm_fc_b. At the 10 March refresh the ongoing allocator gives wallet a only its own bucket (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-130), so ongoing_usage 6_000, ongoing_balance = 0 − 6_000 = −1_000 × 6 = −6_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63) and credits_ongoing_balance −60 ≤ threshold 0 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20-21). The rule asks for 40 − (−60) = 100 credits = 10_000¢, granted because `grants_target_top_up` is true, so it settles at once and raises no invoice (create_from_params_service.rb:145-173) — invoices stays 1. The cascade re-refresh reads (10_000 − 6_000)/100 = 40 credits, not > 0 is false, so it stops after exactly one top-up. At billing wallet a pays only its own bucket, min(6_000, 10_000, 10_000) = 6_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53 gated by :109-114) — full cover of the allowed slice, 4_000¢ of surplus — and wallet b pays min(4_000, 1_000, 4_000) = 1_000, leaving 3_000¢ in cash that a's surplus is forbidden to touch. Two wrong implementations, both named: a rule measuring the gap against `balance_cents` (0) would ask for 40 credits, so prepaid would be 4_000 + 1_000 = 5_000 and the total 5_000 with balance 0. A tag-blind allocator would absorb all 10_000¢ mid-period, ask for 140 credits, then pay the whole merged bucket: prepaid 10_000 and total 0 — and its residual balance would ALSO be 4_000, because a target rule always lands the ongoing balance on the target. That is why this row asserts prepaid and the total rather than resting on the balance.

Target beats priority, and here it also decides how large a target top-up is. Three wallets: b06_twc_tm_mp_g at priority 1, granted, unrestricted, 10_000¢; b06_twc_tm_mp_a at priority 20 with no credits and a target rule; b06_twc_tm_mp_d at priority 30 with 500¢. Both charge fees carry a tag — 3_000¢ to a (5/15/10: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 10) and 2_000¢ to d — so g is applicable to NEITHER, mid-period (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:127-130) and at billing (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:109-114), even though `Wallet.in_application_order` reaches it first (wallet.rb:69-71). At the 10 March refresh wallet a sees only its own 3_000¢, so credits_ongoing_balance = −30 ≤ 0 and the target rule asks for 70 − (−30) = 100 credits = 10_000¢ granted (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150 via compute_granted_credits :104-112); the re-refresh reads 70 credits, not below the target, and stops. Wallet d absorbs its own 2_000¢ with no rule to fire; g's allocation is 0. At billing a pays its own 3_000¢ (balance 7_000), d pays min(2_000, 500, remaining) = 500 and empties, and g pays NOTHING while holding twice the invoice. Prepaid 3_500 of 5_000¢, total 1_500 in cash. g's untouched 10_000¢ is the assertion: tag-blind, one 5_000¢ bucket and g first in order pays all of it — prepaid 5_000, total 0, g at 5_000¢ — and a's rule would have been sized against 5_000¢ of usage instead of 3_000¢, asking for 120 credits. Name both: g 10_000 vs 5_000, total 1_500 vs 0.

A target rule that overshoots the invoice, and the total still does not go negative. At the 10 March refresh wallet a sees only its own tagged 3_000¢ (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb: 118-130), so credits_ongoing_balance = −30 ≤ threshold 0 and the rule asks for 70 − (−30) = 100 credits = 10_000¢, granted, no invoice (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150; create_from_params_service.rb:145-173) — invoices stays 1. The re-refresh reads 70 credits, not below the target, so there is exactly one top-up. Coupons do not enter the ongoing pool, which is `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents` (:88). Fees 5_000¢: 3_000¢ tagged b06_twc_tm_nt_a (10/15/5: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 5) and 2_000¢ tagged b06_twc_tm_nt_b. The fixed_amount coupon spreads BY WEIGHT (fee.rb:232-236 through credits/applied_coupon_service.rb:35-37): 2_000 × 3_000/5_000 = 1_200 onto the a fee and 800 onto the b fee, so the per-fee caps are `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` = 1_800 and 1_200 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:77-79). Wallet b holds no credits, so `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65) drops it from the allocator and its 1_200¢ is unpayable by anyone; wallet a is refused it by the tag (:109-114) while holding 8_200¢. Draws are bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (:53, :57), so prepaid is 1_800 and the total clamps at 1_200 instead of −7_000, with no credit note and no `credit` invoice for the surplus. Named alternatives: credits before the coupon would cap the a fee at 3_000 → prepaid 3_000, total 0, balance 7_000; a tag-blind allocator would size the rule against 5_000¢ of usage (120 credits = 12_000¢) and pay both caps → total 0 and balance 9_000; a rule measuring the gap against `balance_cents` would ask for 70 credits = 7_000¢ → prepaid still 1_800 but balance 5_200. The post-billing refresh leaves 82 credits above the target, so nothing re-arms.

The mid-period read where the tag sizes the top-up and NOTHING else can show it. No invoice exists (invoices 0) and no billing code runs: Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService → RefreshOngoingUsageService → UpdateOngoingService, whose after_commit is the only caller of Wallets::ThresholdTopUpService (update_ongoing_service.rb:26). Current-usage fees keep their grouping (fees/charge_service.rb:493-499), so the pool is 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_tm_ob_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b06_twc_tm_ob_b, and `applicable_fee?` (:127-130) gives each key exactly one wallet. Wallet a therefore measures its gap against its OWN bucket: ongoing_balance = 0 − 6_000 = −6_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63), credits_ongoing_balance −60 ≤ 0, and the target rule asks for 40 − (−60) = 100 credits = 10_000¢ granted (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150 via compute_granted_credits :104-112). Balance::IncreaseService re-enqueues the refresh (increase_service.rb:36) and the second pass reads 40 credits, not below the target, so it terminates after one top-up. The trap this row has to dodge: a target rule always lands the ongoing balance ON the target, so ongoing_balance_cents is 4_000 whether or not the tag is honoured. Tag-blind the wallet would absorb all 10_000¢, ask for 140 credits and end at 14_000¢ with ongoing_usage 10_000 — identical ongoing_balance. The separating figures are therefore balance_cents 10_000 vs 14_000 and ongoing_usage_balance_cents 6_000 vs 10_000; a rule measuring the gap against `balance_cents` would instead ask for 40 credits and report balance 4_000 with ongoing_balance −2_000. The current-usage payload is asserted alongside because the customer still owes the whole 10_000¢: the ongoing figures are a projection that never debits the wallet, and no WalletTransactionConsumption rows exist on this path.

A target rule is sized WHEN IT FIRES, against the usage visible at that instant and — under this limitation — only the usage TAGGED FOR IT. Only 10 a-tagged units (1_000¢) exist at the 4 March refresh: wallet a is given its own bucket alone (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-130), so ongoing_balance = 0 − 1_000 = −1_000 and credits_ongoing_balance = −10 ≤ threshold 0 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20-21). The gap is 10 − (−10) = 20 credits = 2_000¢ (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150), granted so it settles at once with no invoice — invoices stays 1. The re-refresh reads (2_000 − 1_000)/100 = 10 credits, which is not below the target, so it stops. Then 50 more a-tagged units and 40 b-tagged units arrive with no refresh between, so at billing the fees are 6_000¢ tagged a (10/30/20 across the two batches: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20), 4_000¢ tagged b and the 0¢ subscription fee. Wallet a is confined to its own bucket and holds a third of it: min(6_000, 2_000, 10_000) = 2_000 and it empties (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53). Wallet b pays its own 4_000¢ in full and keeps 6_000¢ that `applicable_fee?` (:109-114) forbids it from putting against a's remainder, so 4_000¢ is owed in CASH. Wallet b is the asserted wallet: a ends at 0 under every variant, and its rule re-arms after billing — the synchronous refresh at applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:39 sees balance 0 and no usage, so credits_ongoing_balance 0 is below the target of 10 and a fresh 10-credit grant lands after the invoice is final. Named alternatives: a rule measuring the gap against `balance_cents` would ask for 10 credits, prepaid 5_000 and total 5_000; a tag-blind allocator merges the buckets so b covers a's shortfall, prepaid 10_000, total 0 and b at 2_000¢. Name both: b 6_000 vs 2_000, total 4_000 vs 0.

A target top-up whose credit amount is a half-cent, and the numbers are chosen so the gap itself is exact. Charge rate 1.333 makes 50 units cost 66.65 → 6_665¢, and wallet a's rate is 0.6665, so at the 4 March refresh — where the allocator gives a only its own tagged bucket (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-130) — credits_ongoing_balance = −6_665/100/0.6665 = −100.00000 exactly (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63-68, a decimal(30,5) column). The target rule asks for 50 − (−100) = 150 credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:138-150), and `(150 × 0.6665).round(2) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) is 99.975 → HALF-UP 99.98 → 9_998¢. Truncation or half-even would give 99.97 → 9_997¢: both numbers are named, and the row carries the single cent into the invoice total. The re-refresh reads (9_998 − 6_665)/100/0.6665 = 50.0075 credits, above the target of 50, so exactly one top-up occurs; the grant settles immediately and raises no invoice, so invoices is 1. 50 more a-tagged units and 20 b-tagged units then arrive with no refresh, so the fees are 100 × 1.333 = 133.30 → 13_330¢ tagged a (events 10/25/15 twice: sum 50 per batch ≠ max 25 ≠ latest 15), 20 × 1.333 = 26.66 → 2_666¢ tagged b, and the 0¢ subscription fee: 15_996¢. Wallet a is drained for its whole 9_998¢ against its own bucket (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53) and wallet b pays its own 2_666¢, keeping 7_334¢ that the tag forbids it from lending (:109-114). Prepaid 12_664, total 3_332. Truncating the top-up: prepaid 12_663 and total 3_333. Ignoring the tag: a's rule would have been sized against the whole 15_996¢ pool (≈290 credits, ≈19_329¢) and would then have paid the entire merged bucket, total 0 with b untouched at 10_000¢. Wallet b is asserted rather than a because a ends at 0 in every variant and its rule re-arms after billing (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:39).

Same shape as the fee-types full-cover row but discriminating on METRIC rather than fee kind — separate rows because they are separate branches of `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:105-121: `targets` from wallet_targets versus `types` from allowed_fee_types). Two charges, each with three events so sum is distinguishable from max and latest: 10/30/20 → 60 units → 6_000¢ on the covered metric, 5/15/10 → 30 units → 3_000¢ on the other, 9_000¢ of fees. Mid-period the pool has two keys, [charge, cov_id] = 6_000 and [charge, oth_id] = 3_000. The wallet's targets are [["charge", cov_id]] and its types are empty, so for the `oth` key there is no target match, no type match, and `unrestricted_wallet` is false because targets is non-empty (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137) — `applicable` is empty for it and it is dropped. For the `cov` key the threshold wallet absorbs the whole 6_000 rather than being capped at its balance (:48-51, `balance: threshold ? 0` at :74), so ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000, −10 credits ≤ 20, and the rule fires once for a flat 40 granted credits → 9_000¢; the cascade refresh sees 3_000 (30 credits > 20) and stops. At billing the buckets sort descending, so `cov` (6_000) is drawn first: min(6000, 9000, 9000) = 6_000, and the `oth` bucket is then skipped by the same target mismatch. Prepaid 6_000, total 3_000 — the whole `oth` charge fee, owed in cash: the fee this wallet may not pay for. Balance ends 3_000, consumed 6_000, and the post-billing refresh leaves it there (April usage 0, 30 credits > 20). Counterfactuals: ignoring wallet_targets at billing → prepaid 9_000, total 0, balance 0; ignoring them mid-period → ongoing_usage 9_000, ongoing_balance −4_000, two top-ups and a 13_000¢ balance before billing. Without the threshold top-up at all the wallet would have held 5_000: prepaid 5_000, total 4_000, balance 0.

Two wallets limited to the SAME metric, declared in the wrong order so only `Wallet.in_application_order` (priority ASC then created_at, wallet.rb:69-71) yields the asserted numbers. Fees 9_000¢: 60 units (10/30/20) × 1.00 on `cov`, 30 units (5/15/10) × 1.00 on `oth`. The purchased wallet's 60 paid credits stay pending until its `credit` invoice is paid on 2 March (hence `manual_payments`), giving it 6_000¢; the threshold wallet holds 20 granted credits = 2_000¢ and a rule granting 60 more below 10 credits. Mid-period the pool has [charge, cov_id] = 6_000 and [charge, oth_id] = 3_000. Neither wallet is applicable to `oth` (targets is [["charge", cov_id]], types empty, so no match and `unrestricted_wallet` false — allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137), so those 3_000¢ are dropped. For `cov` both wallets are applicable, and the threshold wallet is both first and allowed to absorb the whole remaining amount rather than only its balance's worth (:48-51, `balance: threshold ? 0` at :74): it takes 6_000, the purchased wallet takes 0 (`break if remaining <= 0`, :46). Its ongoing balance is 2_000 − 6_000 = −4_000, −40 credits ≤ 10, so the rule fires once for a flat 60 granted credits → 8_000¢, and the cascade refresh sees 2_000 (20 credits > 10) and stops. At billing `cov` (6_000) is drawn first. Wallet 1 (priority 1, 8_000¢) takes min(6000, 8000, 9000) = 6_000, zeroing that bucket; `oth` is inapplicable to it. Wallet 2 then finds `cov` at 0 (`next if remaining_amount <= 0`, :44) and `oth` inapplicable, so it contributes nothing and is dropped (`next if total_amount_cents <= 0`, :64). Prepaid 6_000, total 3_000 — the whole `oth` fee, the fee neither wallet may pay for, owed in cash. Balances end 2_000 (threshold, consumed 6_000) and 6_000 (purchased, consumed 0). Both wallets are pinned without an `expect.wallets` list because one pool is purely granted and the other purely purchased, so prepaid_granted 6_000 with prepaid_credit 6_000 means the purchased wallet contributed nothing and still holds 6_000 (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:83-92). Creation order instead of priority would report prepaid_granted nil and prepaid_purchased 6_000, with wallet[b06_thr_bm_thr] at 8_000 and consumed 0 — every asserted number differs.

A wallet holding 25_000¢ against a 9_000¢ invoice that still leaves 3_000¢ owed in cash: the METRIC limitation, not the balance, decides what credits may touch, so no amount of over-refill can drive the total to zero, let alone negative. Fees 9_000¢ — 60 units (10/30/20) × 1.00 on `cov`, 30 units (5/15/10) × 1.00 on `oth`. The rule is asleep at creation (no subscription, ongoing_balance_cents 5_000, 50 credits > 20). On 10 March the `oth` key is dropped as inapplicable (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137) and the threshold wallet absorbs all 6_000¢ of `cov` (:48-51): ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000, −10 credits ≤ 20, and the rule fires once for a flat 200 granted credits — `compute_granted_credits` returns the rule's amount verbatim for a non-target rule (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111), so nothing scales it to the 1_000¢ actually missing. Balance 25_000; the cascade refresh sees 19_000 (190 credits > 20) and stops. At billing the `cov` bucket draws min(6000, 25000, 9000) = 6_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53) and `oth` is skipped by the target mismatch (:105-121). Total 3_000¢ of cash while 19_000¢ of credit sits unusable in the same wallet. Named alternatives, none of which happens: (a) total −16_000 if the balance were drained against the whole invoice, (b) total 0 with the limitation ignored, since 25_000 ≥ 9_000, leaving the wallet at 16_000, (c) a `credit` invoice or credit note for the 19_000 surplus — invoices stays 1 because the top-up is granted and raises no invoice, (d) the wallet emptied to 0.

A mid-period read where the metric limitation PARTIALLY narrows what the wallet reserves against — the middle case between b06/threshold-rule/none/ongoing-balance (absorbs everything) and b06/threshold-rule/fee-types/ongoing-balance (absorbs nothing). The timeline stops at the refresh, so no invoice exists and invoices is 0; the path is Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService → RefreshOngoingUsageService → UpdateOngoingService, whose after_commit is the only caller of Wallets::ThresholdTopUpService (update_ongoing_service.rb:26). Unbilled usage is 9_000¢ in two keys: `cov` 60 units (10/30/20) × 1.00 = 6_000 and `oth` 30 units (5/15/10) × 1.00 = 3_000. The wallet is limited to `oth`, so `applicable_fee?` (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137) leaves `applicable` empty for the `cov` key — dropped, not reassigned — while for `oth` the threshold wallet absorbs the whole 3_000 (:48-51, `balance: threshold ? 0` at :74). First pass: ongoing_usage 3_000, ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 3_000 = 2_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63), credits_ongoing_balance 20 ≤ 30 — note it takes only 2_000¢ of reachable usage to arm a wallet still holding 5_000¢, because the threshold is read against the ONGOING balance and not the settled one. The rule fires for a flat 40 granted credits, and the state asserted is after Wallets::Balance::IncreaseService re-enqueues the refresh (increase_service.rb:36): balance 9_000, ongoing_usage 3_000 again, ongoing_balance 6_000 — and 60 credits > 30, so exactly one top-up. The wrong implementation to name is the one that ignores wallet_targets on the ongoing path: ongoing_usage 9_000, ongoing_balance −4_000, the rule fires, balance 9_000, ongoing_balance 0, which is still ≤ 30 so it fires AGAIN — balance 13_000, ongoing_usage 9_000, ongoing_balance 4_000. All three asserted numbers differ (9_000 vs 13_000, 3_000 vs 9_000, 6_000 vs 4_000). The 6_000¢ of `cov` usage is the fee this wallet may not pay for; it is excluded from the wallet's ongoing reservation and will be owed in cash at period end.

Partial cover twice over, on the metric axis: the wallet runs dry half-way through the metric it is allowed to pay, and the other metric is untouched. Fees 9_000¢ — 60 units (10/30/20) × 1.00 on the covered metric, 30 units (5/15/10) × 1.00 on the other. No mid-period refresh, so the rule is still asleep when the invoice is built: `perform_billing` runs Clock::SubscriptionsBillerJob, never Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob, and credits_ongoing_balance is still the 30 set at wallet creation, 30 > 10 at threshold_top_up_service.rb:20. The wallet therefore has only its 30 granted credits = 3_000¢. The `oth` bucket is skipped outright by `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:105-121) — targets is [["charge", cov_id]], so no target match, no type match, `unrestricted_wallet` false — and the `cov` bucket (drawn first, buckets sort descending at :88) takes min(6000, 3000, 9000) = 3_000, emptying the wallet. Total 6_000¢ = the 3_000 of `cov` charge the credits could not reach plus the whole 3_000 of `oth`; both halves are cash and payment_status is pending. Only after the credits are consumed does the refresh run (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:34-39: DecreaseService with `skip_refresh: true`, then Customers::RefreshWalletsService), by which time the balance is 0 and the new April period has no usage: ongoing_balance_cents = 0, 0 credits ≤ 10, and the rule fires for a flat 40 granted credits. The wallet ends at 4_000¢ — more than the 3_000 it spent — while 6_000¢ went out as cash, because the top-up is sized by the rule and not by the shortfall (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111). Named counterfactuals: refreshing (and topping up) before applying credits → prepaid 6_000, total 3_000, balance 1_000; ignoring wallet_targets → prepaid 3_000 still, the wallet being the binding constraint, but drawn off the `oth` bucket first, which is why the per-fee split is asserted — the totals alone cannot tell the two apart.

Two half-cent conversions on a metric-limited wallet. `(credit_amount × rate_amount) .round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) is HALF-UP on the currency amount: at rate 0.1115 the initial grant is 10 × 0.1115 = 1.115 → 1.12 → 112¢ and the threshold top-up is 70 × 0.1115 = 7.805 → 7.81 → 781¢, so the balance after the top-up is 112 + 781 = 893¢. Truncating gives 111 + 780 = 891¢ — name both. Fees 900¢: 60 units (10/30/20, so sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) × 0.10 = 600¢ on `cov` and 30 units (5/15/10) × 0.10 = 300¢ on `oth`. The rule is asleep at creation: no subscription, so ongoing_balance_cents = 112 and credits_ongoing_balance = 1.12 ÷ 0.1115 = 10.04484 > 5 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20). On 10 March the `oth` key is dropped (targets is [["charge", cov_id]], so no match and `unrestricted_wallet` false — allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137) and the threshold wallet absorbs all 600¢ of `cov` (:48-51): ongoing_balance_cents = 112 − 600 = −488, −43.76682 credits ≤ 5, one top-up of 70 granted credits. The cascade refresh sees 893 − 600 = 293, i.e. 26.27803 credits > 5, and stops. At billing `cov` (600) is drawn first and takes min(600, 893, 900) = 600 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53); `oth` is skipped by the same target mismatch (:105-121), so 300¢ stays cash — the fee this wallet may not pay for. Balance ends 893 − 600 = 293¢ against the truncating implementation's 291¢, the one asserted number that separates them, since prepaid, total and the per-fee split are identical under both.

Under a limitation "full cover" means the wallet fully covers the slice it is ALLOWED to pay and keeps a surplus, while the rest stays cash. The invoice holds two fees: a 5_000¢ subscription fee and a 6_000¢ charge fee (60 units from 10/30/20 × 1.00), 11_000¢ total. Mid-period the ongoing pool contains only the charge bucket — `current_usage_fees` is Invoices::CustomerUsageService output, charge fees only, a subscription fee is not usage (refresh_wallets_service.rb:52-54) — and the wallet allows fee_type `charge`, so `applicable_fee?` (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137) matches and the threshold wallet absorbs all 6_000¢ (:48-51). ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000, −10 credits ≤ 20, so the rule fires once for a flat 40 granted credits → balance 9_000¢; the cascade refresh sees 3_000 (30 credits > 20) and stops. At billing the buckets are [charge, bm] = 6_000 and [subscription, nil] = 5_000, sorted descending (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:88). The wallet's allowed_fee_types is ["charge"], so for the subscription bucket `applicable_fee?` (:105-121) finds no type match, no target match, and `unrestricted_wallet` false because types is non-empty — the bucket is SKIPPED ENTIRELY, not merely reduced. The charge bucket draws min(6000, 9000, 11000) = 6_000. So prepaid is 6_000 and total is 5_000 — exactly the subscription fee, still owed in cash, which is the fee this wallet may not pay for and the reason payment_status is pending despite a wallet that could have covered the lot. Counterfactuals, named: ignoring allowed_fee_types at billing → prepaid 9_000, total 2_000, balance 0; ignoring it mid-period changes nothing here because the pool is charges only, which is why the fee-types/ongoing-balance row uses the opposite limitation. Without the threshold top-up the wallet would have held 5_000: prepaid 5_000, total 6_000, balance 0.

Granted-and-auto-refilled versus purchased, both limited to fee_type `charge`, declared in the wrong order so that only `Wallet.in_application_order` (priority ASC then created_at, wallet.rb:69-71) produces the asserted numbers. Fees 11_000¢ (5_000 subscription + 6_000 charge, 60 units from 10/30/20 × 1.00). The purchased wallet's 60 paid credits are pending until its `credit` invoice is paid on 2 March (hence `manual_payments`), after which it holds 6_000¢; the threshold wallet holds 20 granted credits = 2_000¢ and a rule granting 60 more below 10 credits. Mid-period the pool is the 6_000¢ charge bucket only (a subscription fee is not usage, refresh_wallets_service.rb:52-54) and both wallets are applicable, but the threshold wallet is first AND absorbs the whole remaining amount rather than only its balance's worth (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:48-51, `balance: threshold ? 0` at :74), so it takes 6_000 and the purchased wallet takes 0 (`break if remaining <= 0`, :46). Its ongoing balance is 2_000 − 6_000 = −4_000, −40 credits ≤ 10, so the rule fires once for a flat 60 granted credits → 8_000¢; the cascade refresh sees 2_000 (20 credits > 10) and stops. At billing the buckets are charge 6_000 and subscription 5_000. Wallet 1 (priority 1, 8_000¢): the subscription bucket is skipped by `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:105-121) since allowed_fee_types is ["charge"], and the charge bucket draws min(6000, 8000, 11000) = 6_000, zeroing it. Wallet 2 (priority 20) then finds the charge bucket at 0 (`next if remaining_amount <= 0`, :44) and the subscription bucket inapplicable, contributes nothing and is dropped (`next if total_amount_cents <= 0`, :64). Prepaid 6_000, total 5_000 — the subscription fee, still cash, the fee neither wallet may pay for. Balances end 2_000 (threshold, consumed 6_000) and 6_000 (purchased, consumed 0). Both wallets are pinned without an `expect.wallets` list: one pool is purely granted and the other purely purchased, so prepaid_granted 6_000 alongside prepaid_credit 6_000 means the purchased wallet contributed nothing and still holds 6_000 (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:83-92). Creation order instead of priority would report prepaid_granted nil and prepaid_purchased 6_000, with wallet[b06_thr_fm_thr] still at 8_000 and consumed 0 — every asserted number differs.

The sharpest form of "negative total" under a limitation: a wallet holding 25_000¢ against an 11_000¢ invoice that STILL leaves 5_000¢ owed in cash, because the limitation and not the balance decides what credits may touch. Fees 11_000¢ (5_000 subscription + 6_000 charge, 60 units from 10/30/20 × 1.00). The rule is asleep at creation (no subscription, so ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 and 50 credits > 20). On 10 March the pool is the 6_000¢ charge bucket, which the wallet may pay, so the threshold wallet absorbs it all (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:48-51): ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000, −10 credits ≤ 20, and the rule fires once for a flat 200 granted credits — `compute_granted_credits` returns the rule's amount verbatim for a non-target rule (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111), so nothing scales it to the 1_000¢ actually missing. Balance 25_000; the cascade refresh sees 19_000 (190 credits > 20) and stops. At billing the charge bucket draws min(6000, 25000, 11000) = 6_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53) and the subscription bucket is skipped outright by `applicable_fee?` (:105-121). So the total does not merely fail to go negative — it does not even reach zero: 5_000¢ of subscription fee is cash while 19_000¢ of credit sits unusable in the same wallet, and payment_status is pending. Named alternatives, none of which happens: (a) total −14_000 if the balance were drained against the whole invoice, (b) total 0 with the limitation ignored, since 25_000 ≥ 11_000, and the wallet at 14_000, (c) a `credit` invoice or credit note for the 19_000 surplus — invoices stays 1, (d) the wallet emptied to 0.

The row where the fee-type limitation DISARMS the threshold rule. A threshold rule has exactly one trigger — the ongoing-balance recompute (update_ongoing_service.rb:26) — and the ongoing balance only moves if the wallet is allowed to absorb the usage. This wallet may pay only `subscription` fees, and the mid-period pool is built from `current_usage_fees` (refresh_wallets_service.rb:52-54), i.e. Invoices::CustomerUsageService output, which is CHARGE fees only: a subscription fee is not usage and never appears there. So `applicable_fee?` (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:126-137) is asked whether a wallet with types=["subscription"] matches a fee_key whose fee_type is "charge": no type match, no target match, and `unrestricted_wallet` is false because types is non-empty. `applicable` is EMPTY for the only key in the pool, the loop at :45-61 allocates nothing, and the 6_000¢ of charge usage (60 units from 10/30/20 × 1.00) is simply dropped rather than forced onto some wallet. ongoing_usage_balance_cents is 0 and ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 0 = 5_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63). credits_ongoing_balance is therefore 50, and 50 > 20, so threshold_top_up_service.rb:20 returns and the rule never fires: balance stays at its initial 50 granted credits. The wrong answer, and the one a reader expects, is an implementation that ignores allowed_fee_types on the ongoing path — ongoing_usage 6_000, ongoing_balance −1_000, the rule fires for 40 granted credits and balance ends 9_000. Name all three: balance 5_000 vs 9_000, ongoing_usage 0 vs 6_000, ongoing_balance 5_000 vs −1_000. The 6_000¢ of charge usage is the fee this wallet may not pay for and it will be owed in cash at period end; the wallet reserves nothing against it, which is why `depleted_ongoing_balance` never fires here. invoices is 0: the top-up is granted so it raises no `credit` invoice, and the timeline stops before billing.

Partial cover TWICE over: the wallet runs dry part-way through the slice it is allowed to pay, AND the slice it is not allowed to pay is untouched. Fees 11_000¢ (5_000 subscription + 6_000 charge, 60 units from 10/30/20 × 1.00). No mid-period refresh, so as in b06/threshold-rule/none/partial-cover the rule is still asleep when the invoice is built (`perform_billing` runs Clock::SubscriptionsBillerJob, never Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob, and credits_ongoing_balance is still the 30 set at wallet creation, 30 > 10 at threshold_top_up_service.rb:20). The wallet therefore has only its 30 granted credits = 3_000¢. The subscription bucket is skipped outright by `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:105-121) because allowed_fee_types is ["charge"], and the charge bucket draws min(6000, 3000, 11000) = 3_000 (:53) — the wallet is emptied without finishing the charge fee. Total owed 8_000¢ = the whole 5_000 subscription fee plus the 3_000 of charge fee the credits could not reach; both halves are cash. Only after the credits are consumed is the wallet refreshed (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:34-39: DecreaseService with `skip_refresh: true`, then Customers::RefreshWalletsService). Balance is then 0 and the new April period has no usage, so ongoing_balance_cents = 0, 0 credits ≤ 10, and the rule fires for a flat 40 granted credits: the wallet ends at 4_000¢, richer than it started, while 8_000¢ went out as cash. Named counterfactuals: a refresh (and so a top-up) before applying credits → prepaid 6_000, total 5_000, balance 1_000; ignoring allowed_fee_types → prepaid 3_000 still (the wallet is the binding constraint) but drawn off the subscription bucket first, so prepaid stays 3_000 while total stays 8_000 — which is why this row also asserts the per-fee split, the only place the two differ is which fee remains payable.

Two half-cent conversions on a fee-type-limited wallet. `(credit_amount × rate_amount) .round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) is HALF-UP on the currency amount: at rate 0.2225 the initial grant is 10 × 0.2225 = 2.225 → 2.23 → 223¢ and the threshold top-up is 70 × 0.2225 = 15.575 → 15.58 → 1_558¢, so the balance after the top-up is 223 + 1_558 = 1_781¢. Truncating gives 222 + 1_557 = 1_779¢ — name both. Fees 5_600¢: a 5_000¢ subscription fee plus 60 units (10/30/20, so sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) × 0.10 = 600¢ of charge. The rule is asleep at creation: no subscription yet, so ongoing_balance_cents = 223 and credits_ongoing_balance = 2.23 ÷ 0.2225 = 10.02247 > 5 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20). On 10 March the pool is the 600¢ charge bucket, which this wallet may pay, so the threshold wallet absorbs all of it (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:48-51): ongoing_balance_cents = 223 − 600 = −377, −16.94382 credits ≤ 5, one top-up of 70 granted credits. The cascade refresh sees 1_781 − 600 = 1_181, i.e. 53.07865 credits > 5, and stops. At billing the buckets sort descending, so subscription 5_000 is tried FIRST and skipped — allowed_fee_types is ["charge"], so `applicable_fee?` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:105-121) finds no match and `unrestricted_wallet` is false — and only then does the charge bucket draw min(600, 1781, 5600) = 600. Total 5_000 is the subscription fee, still owed in cash: the fee this wallet may not pay for. Balance ends 1_781 − 600 = 1_181¢ against the truncating implementation's 1_179¢, the one asserted number that separates them, since prepaid, total and the per-fee split are identical under both.

A threshold rule is NOT fired by a scheduler: its only call site is `Wallets::Balance::UpdateOngoingService` (update_ongoing_service.rb:26), reached whenever the wallet's ongoing balance is recomputed. `perform_wallet_refresh` (Clock:: RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob → Customers::RefreshWalletJob → Customers::RefreshWalletsService) is therefore the verb that arms it, and the rule itself only exists at all with a premium licence (recurring_transaction_rules/create_service.rb:16 returns early otherwise), hence `premium: true`. Three events 10/30/20 so sum 60 is distinguishable from max 30 and latest 20: 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of fees. Wallet starts at 50 granted credits = 5_000¢. At wallet creation the customer has no subscription, so the ongoing pool is empty, ongoing_balance_cents = balance_cents = 5_000 and credits_ongoing_balance = 50 > 20: the guard at threshold_top_up_service.rb:20 returns and the rule does NOT fire on creation. On 10 March the refresh allocates the 6_000¢ of unbilled usage to the wallet — a wallet with an active threshold rule is deliberately allowed to go negative rather than being capped at its balance (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:48-51, `balance: threshold ? 0` at :74) — so ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63) and credits_ongoing_balance = −10 ≤ 20. The rule fires for a flat 40 granted credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111: a non-target rule returns `granted_credits` unchanged, it does NOT top up to the threshold), so the balance becomes 9_000¢. The cascade re-refresh then sees 9_000 − 6_000 = 3_000, i.e. 30 credits > 20, and stops: exactly ONE top-up, which is why 40 and not 20 was chosen — 20 would land the ongoing balance on 20 credits and `>` (not `>=`) would fire a second time. At billing the wallet holds 9_000¢ against a 6_000¢ invoice, so the draw is min(6000, 9000, 6000) = 6_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53), the total clamps to 0 and payment_status is succeeded. Balance ends 3_000, consumed 6_000, and the post-billing refresh leaves it there (April usage is 0, 30 credits > 20). Without the threshold top-up the wallet would have had only 5_000¢: prepaid 5_000, total 1_000, balance 0. Name both — total 0 vs 1_000, prepaid 6_000 vs 5_000, balance 3_000 vs 0. prepaid_granted is the whole 6_000 because both inbounds are grants; no `credit` invoice is issued for either, so invoices stays 1.

Two wallets, declared in the WRONG order on purpose: the purchased one (priority 20, 60 paid credits = 6_000¢, settled by paying its `credit` invoice on 2 March) comes first in the YAML, the threshold one (priority 1, 20 granted credits = 2_000¢ plus a rule that grants 60 more) second. Consumption follows `Wallet.in_application_order` — priority ASC then created_at (wallet.rb:69-71) — so the threshold wallet is drawn first. Mid-period the threshold wallet also absorbs the WHOLE unbilled pool, not just its own balance's worth: `wallet_meta` reports `balance: 0` for it and the loop takes `remaining` outright (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:48-51, :68-75), so of the 6_000¢ of usage it takes 6_000 and the purchased wallet takes 0 (`break if remaining <= 0`, :46). Its ongoing balance is 2_000 − 6_000 = −4_000, i.e. −40 credits ≤ 10, so the rule fires for a flat 60 granted credits and the balance becomes 8_000¢; the cascade refresh then sees 8_000 − 6_000 = 2_000 (20 credits > 10) and stops. At billing the invoice is 6_000¢ and the threshold wallet holds 8_000¢, so it pays the entire invoice: min(6000, 8000, 6000) = 6_000, `remaining_invoice_amount` drops to 0 and the purchased wallet is skipped on `next if remaining_amount <= 0` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:44). Balances end 2_000 (threshold, consumed 6_000) and 6_000 (purchased, consumed 0). Both wallets are pinned without an `expect.wallets` list, because one pool is purely granted and the other purely purchased, so the breakdown at applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:83-92 maps one-to-one: prepaid_granted 6_000 with prepaid_credit 6_000 means the purchased wallet contributed nothing and still holds its 6_000. The counterfactual is different in every asserted number: consuming in declaration/creation order would report prepaid_granted nil and prepaid_purchased 6_000, with wallet[b06_thr_nm_thr].balance_cents still 8_000 and consumed 0, and the purchased wallet drained to 0. invoices is 2 — the purchased top-up's `credit` invoice plus the period invoice; paying an invoice through POST /payments is itself premium, hence `manual_payments`.

A threshold rule that grossly over-refills — 200 granted credits on a wallet already holding 50, against an invoice whose payable ceiling is 4_500¢ — which is the case where the total could go negative. It does NOT. Lago clamps at zero and leaves the surplus in the wallet: every draw is bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53, decremented at :57), so exactly 4_500¢ leaves the wallet and 20_500¢ stays. The three alternatives, named: (a) total −20_500 if the whole balance were drained against the invoice, (b) a `credit` invoice or a credit note for the 20_500 surplus — none is issued and invoices stays 1, (c) the wallet emptied to 0. Getting there: 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of fees. The rule is asleep at creation (ongoing pool empty, 50 credits > 20). On 10 March the refresh hands the wallet all 6_000¢ of unbilled usage, so ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000, −10 credits ≤ 20, and the rule fires once for 200 granted credits → balance 25_000¢; the cascade refresh sees 25_000 − 6_000 = 19_000 (190 credits > 20) and stops. Note the top-up is sized by the RULE, not by the deficit: `compute_granted_credits` returns `granted_credits` verbatim for a non-target rule (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111), so nothing scales it down to the 1_000¢ actually missing. The 4_500 ceiling is the row's second half. Prepaid credit is the LAST reducer (calculate_fees_service.rb:57-62: coupon → tax → credit note → prepaid) and the per-fee cap is `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` (:77-79), where `sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents = amount_cents − precise_coupons_amount_cents` (fee.rb:238-240): 6_000 − 1_500 = 4_500, which equals invoice.total exactly so `reconcile_remaining_amounts` (:93-106) adds nothing. Credits applied BEFORE the coupon would have taken 6_000 and left 19_000 — name both: prepaid 4_500 vs 6_000, wallet 20_500 vs 19_000. The coupon is `frequency: once` and is still unspent when the period invoice is built because the threshold top-up is granted, so it raises no invoice for the coupon to be consumed on.

A mid-period read, and the only row in this slice where the threshold rule's effect is observed WITHOUT an invoice existing at all: the timeline stops at the refresh, so no billing code runs and invoices is 0. The path is Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → Wallets::Balance::AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService → RefreshOngoingUsageService → UpdateOngoingService, whose after_commit is the one and only caller of Wallets::ThresholdTopUpService (update_ongoing_service.rb:26). 60 units (10/30/20) × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of unbilled usage, pooled as `fee.amount_cents + fee.taxes_amount_cents` (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:88). First pass: balance 5_000, ongoing_usage 6_000, ongoing_balance_cents = 5_000 − 6_000 = −1_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63) — the wallet is allowed NEGATIVE, and `depleted_ongoing_balance` flips true (:41-45). credits_ongoing_balance −10 ≤ 20 so the rule fires for a flat 40 granted credits. Wallets::Balance::IncreaseService then re-enqueues the refresh (increase_service.rb:36), which is the state asserted: balance 9_000, ongoing_usage 6_000 again, ongoing_balance 3_000 — and 30 credits > 20, so the loop terminates after exactly one top-up. The plausible wrong answers, all named: no top-up at all → balance 5_000 and ongoing_balance −1_000; a top-up sized to the deficit rather than the rule's flat 40 → balance 6_000 and ongoing_balance 0; a clamp of ongoing usage at the balance → ongoing_usage 5_000 and ongoing_balance 0. Honest limitation of this row: with a single wallet the threshold special-case and the ordinary "last applicable wallet absorbs the overflow" branch coincide (`meta[:threshold] || index == applicable.length - 1`, :48), so it does not distinguish them — the two-wallet form in b06/threshold-rule/none/multi-wallet-priority is what separates a threshold wallet from a merely-last one. Note too that there is no granted/purchased breakdown on this path: ongoing usage is allocated against `balance_cents` as a single pool and no WalletTransactionConsumption rows are written.

The same wallet and the same rule as the row above with ONE step removed — no mid-period `perform_wallet_refresh` — and that single omission moves 1_000¢ from credits to cash. This is the row that pins WHEN a threshold rule fires relative to the invoice it would have paid. 60 units × 1.00 = 6_000¢ of fees. Nothing recomputes the ongoing balance between the events and the billing run: `perform_billing` runs Clock::SubscriptionsBillerJob, not Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob, so credits_ongoing_balance is still the 50 it was set to at wallet creation and the rule is still asleep. The invoice therefore draws against the 5_000¢ actually in the wallet: min(6000, 5000, 6000) = 5_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53), leaving 1_000¢ owed in cash and payment_status pending rather than succeeded. Only AFTER the credits are consumed does the wallet get refreshed: Credits:: AppliedPrepaidCreditsService calls Wallets::Balance::DecreaseService with `skip_refresh: true` and then Customers::RefreshWalletsService itself (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:34-39). At that point the balance is 0 and the new April period has no usage, so ongoing_balance_cents = 0 − 0 = 0, credits_ongoing_balance 0 ≤ 20, and the rule fires for 40 granted credits — 4_000¢ that arrive one step too late to reduce the invoice that emptied the wallet. The next cascade refresh sees 40 credits > 20 and stops. The wrong implementation to name is the one that refreshes (and so tops up) BEFORE applying credits: it would report prepaid 6_000, total 0 and balance 3_000 — the full-cover row's numbers — instead of prepaid 5_000, total 1_000 and balance 4_000. Note also that the wallet ends RICHER than the invoice was short (4_000 in the wallet, 1_000 owed in cash): the top-up is a flat 40 credits, not a top-up to the invoice's shortfall.

Two credit→cents conversions on one wallet, both landing exactly on a half-cent, so the whole row moves if the rounding mode changes. `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) is a HALF-UP round of the currency amount, not a truncation. At rate 0.3335 the initial grant is 10 × 0.3335 = 3.335 → 3.34 → 334¢ and the threshold top-up is 70 × 0.3335 = 23.345 → 23.35 → 2_335¢, so the balance after the top-up is 334 + 2_335 = 2_669¢. Truncating instead of rounding gives 333 + 2_334 = 2_667¢ — name both. Fees: 60 units (10/30/20, so sum 60 is distinguishable from max 30 and latest 20) × 0.10 = 6.00 → 600¢, deliberately small enough that the top-up over-covers it. The rule stays asleep at wallet creation: with no subscription the ongoing pool is empty, so ongoing_balance_cents = 334 and credits_ongoing_balance = 3.34 ÷ 0.3335 = 10.01499 > 5 (threshold_top_up_service.rb:20). On 10 March the refresh gives the wallet the 600¢ of unbilled usage — a threshold wallet is not capped at its balance (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:48-51) — so ongoing_balance_cents = 334 − 600 = −266, i.e. −7.97601 credits ≤ 5, and the rule fires once for a flat 70 granted credits. The cascade refresh then sees 2_669 − 600 = 2_069, i.e. 62.03898 credits > 5, and stops. At billing the draw is min(600, 2669, 600) = 600 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service .rb:53) so the total clamps to 0, and the outbound is sized by `WalletCredit.from_amount_cents` (wallet_credit.rb:8-11) which carries the 600¢ through unrounded. Balance ends 2_669 − 600 = 2_069¢, and the truncating implementation would print 2_067¢ — the single asserted number that separates the two, since prepaid and total are identical under both.

The tag decides how much unbilled usage the wallet can SEE, and therefore how often its threshold rule fires — the interaction no `limitation: none` row can express. A threshold rule has one call site, `Wallets::Balance::UpdateOngoingService`'s after_commit (update_ongoing_service.rb:26), so `perform_wallet_refresh` is the verb that arms it, and the rule needs a premium licence (recurring_transaction_rules/create_service.rb:16). Two tagged charge fees (fees/charge_service.rb:496-499): 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_th_fc_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b06_twc_th_fc_b. At the 10 March refresh the ongoing allocator gives wallet a ONLY its own bucket — each key's `applicable` list holds the one wallet whose code matches (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-130), and a wallet with an active threshold rule absorbs its whole applicable pool with no room check (:47-58, `balance: threshold ? 0` at :74). So ongoing_usage is 6_000, ongoing_balance = 2_000 − 6_000 = −1_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63) and credits_ongoing_balance −10 ≤ 0: the rule fires ONCE for a flat 80 granted credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111 — a non-target rule returns granted_credits unchanged), balance 10_000¢. The cascade re-refresh then reads 10_000 − 6_000 = 3_000, i.e. 40 credits > 0, and stops. At billing wallet a pays only its own bucket, min(6_000, 10_000, 10_000) = 6_000 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53 gated by :109-114) — full cover of the allowed slice with 4_000¢ of surplus — and wallet b pays min(4_000, 1_000, 4_000) = 1_000. Prepaid 7_000, total 3_000 owed in cash that wallet a's surplus may not touch. The post-billing refresh (applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:39) sees April usage 0 and 40 credits > 0, so nothing re-arms. Tag-blind, the wallet would absorb the entire 10_000¢ pool: credits_ongoing_balance −80 fires 80, the re-refresh lands on exactly 0 credits which is NOT > 0 so it fires a SECOND time, and the wallet reaches 18_000¢, pays the whole merged bucket and ends at 8_000¢ with total 0. Name both: total 3_000 vs 0, balance 4_000 vs 8_000, one top-up vs two.

Target beats priority on both code paths at once. Three wallets: b06_twc_th_mp_g at priority 1, unrestricted, 10_000¢; b06_twc_th_mp_a at priority 20 with 20 granted credits and a threshold rule; b06_twc_th_mp_d at priority 30 with 500¢. Both charge fees carry a tag — 3_000¢ to a (5/15/10: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 10) and 2_000¢ to d — so g is applicable to NEITHER, mid-period (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:127-130) and at billing (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:109-114), even though `Wallet.in_application_order` reaches it first (wallet.rb:69-71). At the 10 March refresh wallet a sees only its own 3_000¢: ongoing_balance = 2_000 − 3_000 = −1_000, credits_ongoing_balance −10 ≤ 0, so its rule fires once for a flat 80 granted credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111) and the balance becomes 10_000¢; the cascade re-refresh reads 70 credits > 0 and stops. Wallet d absorbs its own 2_000¢ and goes ongoing-negative with no rule to fire; g's allocation is 0. At billing a pays its own 3_000¢ (balance 7_000), d pays min(2_000, 500, remaining) = 500 and empties, g pays NOTHING and keeps 10_000¢. Prepaid 3_500 of 5_000¢ of fees, total 1_500 owed in cash. g's balance is the whole assertion: tag-blind, one 5_000¢ bucket and g first in order pays all of it, prepaid 5_000, total 0, g at 5_000¢ — and mid-period a would have absorbed 5_000 instead of 3_000, still one top-up, ending at 10_000. Name both: g 10_000 vs 5_000, total 1_500 vs 0.

An auto-refilled wallet ends up holding three times the invoice while 1_200¢ stays unpaid — the total never goes negative and the surplus is never refunded. The rule fires at the 10 March refresh on the wallet's OWN bucket only: ongoing_usage 3_000 (its tagged fee, not the 5_000 of total usage — allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-130), ongoing_balance = 2_000 − 3_000 = −1_000, credits_ongoing_balance −10 ≤ 0, one flat 80-credit grant (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111 via update_ongoing_service.rb:26) → balance 10_000¢, and the cascade re-refresh reads 70 credits > 0 and stops. Granted credits raise no invoice, so invoices is 1. Fees 5_000¢: 3_000¢ tagged b06_twc_th_nt_a (10/15/5: sum 30 ≠ max 15 ≠ latest 5) and 2_000¢ tagged b06_twc_th_nt_b. The fixed_amount coupon spreads BY WEIGHT (fee.rb:232-236 through credits/applied_coupon_service.rb:35-37): 2_000 × 3_000/5_000 = 1_200 onto the a fee and 800 onto the b fee, so the caps are `sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes_precise − precise_credit_notes` = 1_800 and 1_200 (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:77-79). Wallet b holds no credits, so `with_positive_balance` (wallet.rb:65) drops it and its 1_200¢ can be paid by nobody — wallet a is refused it by the tag (:109-114) while sitting on 8_200¢. Every draw is also bounded by `remaining_invoice_amount` (:53, :57), so prepaid is 1_800 and the total clamps at 1_200 rather than −7_000. The named alternatives: credits applied before the coupon would cap the a fee at 3_000 → prepaid 3_000, total 0, balance 7_000; a tag-blind allocator would pay both caps → the same 3_000 and 0, and mid-period would have absorbed 5_000 of usage instead of 3_000; a wallet drained to 0 or a credit note for the surplus — neither happens. The post-billing refresh leaves 82 credits > 0, so the rule does not re-arm and 8_200 is stable.

The purest form of the interaction: no invoice exists at all (invoices 0), so the only thing under test is how much unbilled usage the tag lets the wallet see and what its rule does about it. The path is Clock::RefreshWalletsOngoingBalanceJob (premium-gated at refresh_wallets_ongoing_balance_job.rb:8) → Customers::RefreshWalletsService → AllocateOngoingUsageByWalletsService → RefreshOngoingUsageService → UpdateOngoingService, whose after_commit is the one and only caller of Wallets::ThresholdTopUpService (update_ongoing_service.rb:26). Current-usage fees keep their grouping (fees/charge_service.rb:493-499 — `UsageFilters::WITHOUT_PRESENTATION_FILTER` leaves skip_grouping false), so the pool is 6_000¢ tagged b06_twc_th_ob_a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20) and 4_000¢ tagged b06_twc_th_ob_b. `applicable_fee?` (:127-130) gives each key exactly one wallet, so wallet a absorbs 6_000 and not the 4_000 that belongs to b: ongoing_balance = 2_000 − 6_000 = −1_000 (refresh_ongoing_usage_service.rb:63), credits_ongoing_balance −10 ≤ 0, and the rule fires ONCE for a flat 80 granted credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111). Balance::IncreaseService re-enqueues the refresh (increase_service.rb:36), which is the state asserted: balance 10_000, ongoing_usage 6_000 again, ongoing_balance 4_000 — and 40 credits > 0 terminates the loop. Tag-blind, wallet a is applicable to both keys and, having an active threshold rule, absorbs everything with no room check (:47-58, `balance: threshold ? 0` at :74): ongoing_usage 10_000, credits_ongoing_balance −80, one grant to 10_000¢, then a re-refresh landing on exactly 0 credits which is NOT > 0, so a SECOND grant to 18_000¢. Name all three figures: balance 10_000 vs 18_000, ongoing_usage 6_000 vs 10_000, ongoing_balance 4_000 vs 8_000. The current-usage payload is asserted alongside because the customer still owes the whole 10_000¢ — the wallet has only reserved the part the tag allows, and no WalletTransactionConsumption rows are written on this path.

A threshold rule is sized WHEN IT FIRES, so the way to make it under-cover is to let usage grow afterwards. Wallet a is created with no credits of its own — every credit in this row comes from the rule. Only 10 units (1_000¢, tagged a) exist at the 4 March refresh: ongoing_usage 1_000, ongoing_balance = 0 − 1_000 = −1_000, credits_ongoing_balance −10 ≤ 0, so the rule fires for a flat 20 granted credits = 2_000¢ (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111; the only call site is update_ongoing_service.rb:26). Granted credits settle immediately and raise no invoice (create_from_params_service.rb:145-173), which is why invoices stays 1. The cascade re-refresh reads 2_000 − 1_000 = 1_000, 10 credits > 0, and stops. Then 50 more a-tagged units and 40 b-tagged units arrive with no refresh between, so at billing the fees are 6_000¢ tagged a (10/30/20 across the two batches: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20), 4_000¢ tagged b and the 0¢ subscription fee. Wallet a is confined to its own bucket and holds a third of it: min(6_000, 2_000, 10_000) = 2_000 and it empties (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53). Wallet b pays its own 4_000¢ in full and keeps 6_000¢ that `applicable_fee?` (:109-114) forbids it from putting against a's 4_000¢ remainder, so that remainder is owed in CASH. Wallet b is the asserted wallet for two reasons: a ends at 0 under either behaviour, and a's rule RE-ARMS after billing — the synchronous refresh at applied_prepaid_credits_service.rb:39 sees a drained wallet with 0 credits ongoing, which is not > 0, so a fresh 20-credit grant lands after the invoice is already computed. It cannot change any invoice figure, but it does make a's balance unassertable. Tag-blind, the buckets merge, b covers the remaining 8_000¢ and ends at 2_000¢ with total 0. Name both: b 6_000 vs 2_000, total 4_000 vs 0.

Two half-up rounds at rate 0.6665, both landing in the same wallet, and the cent they produce decides the invoice total. `(credit_amount × rate_amount).round(currency.exponent) × 100` (wallet_credit.rb:26-27) turns the 10 granted credits into 6.665 → 6.67 → 667¢ and the rule's 50 credits into 33.325 → 33.33 → 3_333¢, a spendable pool of exactly 4_000¢; truncation would give 666 + 3_332 = 3_998¢. The rule is sized at the 4 March refresh, when only 10 a-tagged units (1_000¢) exist: wallet a is given only its own bucket (allocate_ongoing_usage_by_wallets_service.rb:118-130), so ongoing_balance = 667 − 1_000 = −333 and credits_ongoing_balance = −333/100/0.6665 = −4.996 ≤ 0. The rule fires once for a flat 50 granted credits (recurring_transaction_rule.rb:104-111, called from update_ongoing_service.rb:26) and the cascade re-refresh reads (4_000 − 1_000)/100/0.6665 = 45.01 credits > 0, so it stops. 50 more a-tagged units and 20 b-tagged units then arrive with no refresh, so the fees are 6_000¢ tagged a (10/30/20: sum 60 ≠ max 30 ≠ latest 20), 2_000¢ tagged b and the 0¢ subscription fee. Wallet a is drained for its whole 4_000¢ against its own bucket (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:53) and wallet b pays its own 2_000¢, keeping 8_000¢ it may not lend (:109-114). Prepaid 6_000, total 2_000. Truncation instead of half-up: prepaid 5_998 and total 2_002 — a two-cent difference carried from the wallet arithmetic to the invoice. Tag-blind: b covers a's 2_000¢ shortfall, prepaid 8_000, total 0, b at 6_000¢.
