Two fixed charges differing in units and price, rebuilt: 40_000¢ + 60_000¢ = 100_000¢, the same as the finalized b19/fixed_charge/unequal/invoice, because a refresh re-runs the producers and nothing about a fixed charge is gated on finalization (calculate_fees_service.rb:44 vs :364-379). The per-fee assertion is the whole row. A rebuild reads each charge's units from its own `FixedChargeEvent` and its price from the charge's `properties`, i.e. from two records that a destroy-and-rebuild must re-pair correctly; with two charges present the pairing can go wrong without changing the fee COUNT. Units swapped reads 20_000¢ / 120_000¢ (total 140_000¢), one charge's properties applied to both reads 80_000¢ or 180_000¢, and either charge lost reads 40_000¢ or 60_000¢ with `fees_count` 2. Only 4 units at 40_000¢ against add-on A and 2 units at 60_000¢ against add-on B is the correct rebuild, and `Fee#item_code` being the add-on's code (fee.rb:121) is what lets the row say which is which. The three finalizing-gated reducers are asserted as 0 so the draft cannot pass having allocated one.

12_000¢ of wallet balance against a 5_000¢ invoice: the pool of invoice runs out inside the first wallet, so allocation decides not how much each pays but whether the second is touched at all. The priority-1 wallet is taken first (`Wallet.in_application_order` is `order(:priority, :created_at)`, wallet.rb:69-71) and covers the whole 5_000¢, which drives `remaining_invoice_amount` and the bucket's `ordered_remaining_amounts` entry to zero. The priority-2 wallet then hits `next if remaining_amount <= 0` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:44) on the only bucket there is, accumulates no transactions, and is dropped by `next if total_amount_cents <= 0` (:68) — no wallet transaction, no partial consumption, balance untouched at 4_000¢. That 4_000¢ is the entire assertion, because the invoice is identical under every allocation: 5_000¢ of prepaid credit and nothing due whichever wallet paid. Reverse the order and the low-priority wallet would be drained to 0¢ and the other left at 7_000¢. Split the invoice pro rata by balance and it would read 1_667¢. Only the untouched 4_000¢ is priority-ordered consumption with a hard stop.

The capped pair forecast: 12_000¢ of wallet against a 5_000¢ invoice, where the first wallet alone covers everything and the second must not be touched. Both surfaces run the same allocator on the same balances: priority-1 pays 5_000¢, the bucket and `remaining_invoice_amount` fall to zero, and the priority-2 wallet is skipped at `next if remaining_amount <= 0` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:44). Preview: 5_000¢ of prepaid credit, nothing due — identical to the invoice, which is the parity claim. The failure this specifically excludes is a preview that clamps to the WALLET total rather than to the invoice. `transaction_amount` takes the min of three quantities and the invoice is the binding one here; a preview that dropped `remaining_invoice_amount` from that min would quote 12_000¢ of credit against a 5_000¢ invoice and a negative total. `total_amount_cents: 0` on the preview is what rules that out. The `expect.wallet` is again the only order-bearing assertion, and it reads the state after the real billing: 4_000¢ untouched. A preview that had actually created wallet transactions would leave it at 4_000¢ too but the priority-1 wallet at −2_000¢ worth of double spending, which is why the invoice's own `prepaid_credit_amount_cents` is asserted alongside: 5_000¢, spent once.

The capped pair: the priority-1 wallet alone covers every invoice in sight, so the priority-2 wallet is the control — it must be untouched by the finalized period AND by the regenerated draft. March, finalized out of grace: priority 1 pays the whole 5_000¢ and the low-priority wallet is skipped before any transaction is built (`next if remaining_amount <= 0` and `next if total_amount_cents <= 0`, allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:44, :68), leaving 3_000¢ on the first wallet and 4_000¢ on the second. April is generated as a draft and rebuilt by refresh: 5_000¢ of fees, 0¢ of prepaid credit, 5_000¢ due — the finalizing gate (calculate_fees_service.rb:375-379). 4_000¢ on the low-priority wallet at the end of all that excludes three separate wrong behaviours: consumption in reverse priority order in March (it would read 0¢), pro-rata sharing (1_667¢), and a refresh that allocated April (the first wallet's 3_000¢ would go, then 2_000¢ off this one → 2_000¢). The finalized invoice's own 5_000¢ of prepaid credit is asserted alongside so a total that never moved cannot be mistaken for a wallet that was correctly spared.

Two identically configured wallets, neither of which can settle the invoice alone: 3_000¢ each against 5_000¢ due. The question is whether the allocator moves on to the SECOND wallet once the first is empty, or stops. `Credits::AllocatePrepaidCreditsByWalletsService` walks `Wallet.in_application_order` and, per wallet, tries each fee bucket with `transaction_amount = [remaining_amount, remaining_wallet_balance, remaining_invoice_amount].min` (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:40-66). The single `["subscription", nil]` bucket starts at 5_000¢: the first wallet is bounded by its own 3_000¢ balance, the second by the 2_000¢ of invoice that is left — 5_000¢ of prepaid credit and nothing due. Both wallets hold granted credits, so all 5_000¢ lands in `prepaid_granted_credit_amount_cents` and none in the purchased column, which is the second half of the assertion: it says the credits were sourced from wallets and not from a mis-classified top-up. A one-wallet implementation reads 3_000¢ of prepaid credit and 2_000¢ still due — the loud difference this row is sized for. Deliberately NO `expect.wallet`: both wallets share priority 1 and are created inside the same frozen `travel_to`, so `order(:priority, :created_at)` (wallet.rb:69-71) has nothing left to break the tie and which of the two ends at 1_000¢ is not determined. The invoice-level totals are order-independent, which is exactly why they are the whole assertion here; the ordered cases are b19/prepaid_credit/unequal/invoice and .../capped/invoice.

Two 3_000¢ wallets and a 5_000¢ invoice, forecast before either is spent. The arithmetic is the one derived in b19/prepaid_credit/equal/invoice: the first wallet is bounded by its balance, the second by the remaining invoice, 5_000¢ of prepaid credit and nothing due. The preview is not a reimplementation here — `PreviewService#create_applied_prepaid_credits` calls the very same `Credits::AllocatePrepaidCreditsByWalletsService` (preview_service.rb:368-377) — but it feeds it an UNSAVED invoice, so the service takes the `invoice.persisted? ? invoice.fees.includes(:charge) : invoice.fees` branch (allocate_prepaid_credits_by_wallets_service.rb:73) and reads `sub_total_excluding_taxes` and `taxes_precise_amount_cents` off in-memory fees. That is the divergence risk this cell exists to close: same allocator, different input, and a preview that quoted 3_000¢ of credit against an invoice that applies 5_000¢ would be a forecast the customer could not reconcile. No wallet is spent by the preview — it returns the transactions rather than creating them — so the subsequent real billing starts from full balances and lands on the same numbers. And no `expect.wallet`, for the same reason as the invoice sibling: at equal priority and identical creation instants the tie-break in `order(:priority, :created_at)` is undetermined, so which wallet keeps the last 1_000¢ is not a fact this row may assert.

Two equal wallets, one period settled and the next held open as a draft. March, finalized by hand out of its grace period: 3_000¢ + 2_000¢ from the two wallets settles the 5_000¢ plan, leaving 1_000¢ of credit between them (which of the two holds it is undetermined — equal priority, identical creation instant — so no wallet is asserted). April is the cell. The draft reads 5_000¢ of fees and 0¢ of prepaid credit: `should_create_applied_prepaid_credit?` begins `return false if not_in_finalizing_process?` (calculate_fees_service.rb:375-379), and the refresh must reproduce it rather than allocating. That gate is not cosmetic here — it is the only thing stopping a draft from burning the surviving 1_000¢ of wallet credit that a later refresh, or a plan change, would have to hand back. `Invoices::VoidService` does recredit outbound wallet transactions, but a REFRESH does not, so credit spent on a draft would simply be gone. A refresh that allocated would show 4_000¢ due and both wallets at zero. 5_000¢ due with 0¢ of prepaid credit is the correct, deliberate answer, and asserting the field as 0 rather than omitting it is what makes the row able to say so.

Two wallets holding 13_000¢ between them against a 5_000¢ invoice, so the invoice settles either way and the only question is whose credits were spent. `Wallet.in_application_order` sorts by ascending priority, not by creation, so the 30-credit wallet at priority 1 goes first despite being declared second. It contributes its whole 3_000¢ and the priority-2 wallet covers the remaining 2_000¢, ending at 8_000¢. That 8_000¢ is the entire assertion. Had priority been ignored and the larger wallet gone first it would have paid the whole 5_000¢ and ended at 5_000¢, with the small wallet untouched — same invoice, same prepaid_credit_amount_cents, same zero due. Only the balance of the wallet that did NOT go first distinguishes the two, which is why the row selects it by code rather than asserting the invoice alone.

The priority-ordered pair of b19/prepaid_credit/unequal/invoice, forecast: 3_000¢ at priority 1 and 10_000¢ at priority 2 against a 5_000¢ invoice. The priority-1 wallet contributes its whole 3_000¢ and the priority-2 wallet the remaining 2_000¢, ending at 8_000¢. The row makes two separate claims, because the surface can only carry one of them. (1) The preview total: 5_000¢ of prepaid credit, nothing due. This is what the customer is shown and it must match the invoice to the cent — same allocator (preview_service.rb:368-377 → `Credits::AllocatePrepaidCreditsByWalletsService`), unsaved fees. (2) WHICH wallet paid is NOT visible on a preview at all: the service returns a wallet → amount hash and the preview keeps only `sum { |_k, v| v }`, creating no wallet transaction and moving no balance. So the aggregate is order-blind — 5_000¢ whether priority is honoured or ignored — and the ordering claim can only be made against the real wallet after the real billing. Hence the `expect.wallet` on the priority-2 wallet: 8_000¢ if priority decided the order, 5_000¢ if the larger wallet had gone first and paid the whole invoice. Recording that blind spot is part of the cell's value: a preview cannot be used to check wallet ordering, and a row that asserted only the preview would look like it covered this and cover nothing.

The priority-ordered pair, with the surviving wallet asserted after a regeneration. March, finalized out of grace: priority 1 gives its whole 3_000¢, priority 2 the remaining 2_000¢ → 8_000¢ left on the priority-2 wallet (wallet.rb:69-71; reversed, it would read 5_000¢ and the small wallet would still be full). April's invoice is a draft and stays one through the refresh: 5_000¢ of fees, 0¢ of prepaid credit (calculate_fees_service.rb:375-379), 5_000¢ due. The wallet assertion is doing double duty and that is why this row is the strongest of the three prepaid regenerated cells. 8_000¢ says (a) March consumed in priority order, and (b) the April draft consumed nothing at all — had the refresh allocated, the priority-1 wallet is already empty so the whole 5_000¢ would have come off this wallet and it would read 3_000¢. One number separates three behaviours: correct, ignored-priority, and a draft that spends.

Two subscriptions on the SAME plan for the same customer, landing on ONE invoice with two subscription fees: 6_000¢ + 6_000¢ = 12_000¢. That they consolidate is the structural claim, and it comes from `Subscriptions::OrganizationBillingService#call`, which groups billable subscriptions `group_by(&:customer_id)` and then splits only by payment method, currency, billing entity, `consolidate_invoice` and purchase order number before handing the whole group to ONE `BillSubscriptionJob` (:15-44, :532-560). Both subscriptions here are calendar/monthly/EUR on the same billing entity with `consolidate_invoice` at its default, so nothing splits them and `invoices: 1` is an assertion in its own right — two invoices of 6_000¢ would be a different behaviour with the same total. `CalculateFeesService` then loops over the invoice's `invoice_subscriptions` (calculate_fees_service.rb:20-47) and calls `create_subscription_fee` once per subscription, so the count of fees is the count of subscriptions. A wrong implementation that billed the customer once — deduplicating by plan, or keying the fee on the plan rather than the subscription — reads 6_000¢ and `fees_count` 1. The two fee expectations are identical because they must be: `Fee#item_code` for a subscription fee is `subscription.plan.code` (fee.rb:123) and both fees share the plan, the period and the type, so they collide on every `FEE_MATCH_KEYS` field (F67) and are only assertable while interchangeable. The unequal sibling puts them on different plans, which is what makes the split nameable there.

Two subscriptions on one plan, previewed together: 6_000¢ + 6_000¢ = 12_000¢, the same invoice b19/subscription_fee/equal/invoice finalizes. The preview has to be ASKED for both, which is why the step carries an explicit `subscriptions.external_ids` — the runner otherwise previews only the last subscription it created, and a one-subscription preview would quote 6_000¢ against a 12_000¢ invoice while looking correct in isolation. With both named, `Invoices::PreviewService` loops `subscriptions.each { add_subscription_fee ... }` (preview_service.rb:43-49) and builds one fee per subscription. Two guards have to pass for that to be reachable at all, and they are the reason this cell is not simply implied by the invoice: `currencies_aligned?` (:84-93) rejects a mixed-currency set and `billing_times_aligned?` (:95-103) rejects subscriptions whose `end_of_period` differ. Both subscriptions here are calendar/monthly/EUR started on the same day, so both guards pass; a preview that refused the pair would fail the row rather than silently forecasting half of it. `fees_count: 2` on both surfaces is what says the two fees stayed two — the totals alone cannot distinguish two 6_000¢ fees from one 12_000¢ fee, and `Fee#item_code` is the plan's code for both so the per-fee amounts are not separately matchable (F67).

Two subscriptions on one plan, consolidated onto one draft and rebuilt: 6_000¢ + 6_000¢ = 12_000¢, unchanged from the finalized b19/subscription_fee/equal/invoice because subscription fees are producers (calculate_fees_service.rb:42) and only the three reducers are gated on finalization (:364-379). A refresh is where a consolidated invoice is most exposed, and that is the point of the cell. `Invoices::RefreshDraftService` destroys the draft's fees and re-runs `CalculateFeesService`, which rebuilds one subscription fee per `invoice_subscription` — so the rebuild depends on the invoice still carrying BOTH `invoice_subscriptions`, a join a refresh does not recreate. A rebuild that saw one of them reads 6_000¢ with `fees_count` 1; one that appended rather than replaced reads 24_000¢ with `fees_count` 4. Both are excluded by the count together with the total. The two fee expectations are identical, which is what makes them matchable: `Fee#item_code` is the plan's code for a subscription fee (fee.rb:123) and both fees share plan, type and period, so they collide on every `FEE_MATCH_KEYS` field (F67). The three withheld reducers are asserted as 0 rather than omitted, so a draft that allocated one cannot slip through.

Two subscriptions on DIFFERENT plans, consolidated onto one invoice: 6_000¢ + 15_000¢ = 21_000¢. Different plans is what makes the per-fee split assertable — `Fee#item_code` for a subscription fee is `subscription.plan.code` (fee.rb:123), so the two fees differ on a `GoldenRunner::FEE_MATCH_KEYS` field and each expectation matches exactly one fee (unlike the equal sibling, F67). And the amounts are deliberately far apart, so a fee built against the wrong subscription's plan reads 12_000¢ or 30_000¢ rather than the correct 21_000¢. They still share one invoice because `Subscriptions::OrganizationBillingService` groups by customer and then splits only on payment method, currency, billing entity, `consolidate_invoice` and purchase order number (:15-44, :532-560) — the PLAN is not a splitting criterion, only the plan's currency is, and both are EUR. Both are calendar/monthly so both are billable on 1 April. `invoices: 1` therefore asserts the consolidation and `fees_count: 2` asserts that consolidation did not collapse the two subscriptions into one line. The failure this excludes is the invoice-level one that a same-plan row cannot see: a fee keyed on the invoice's first subscription would bill 6_000¢ twice (12_000¢) and look perfectly consistent doing it.

Two subscriptions on different plans, previewed together: 6_000¢ + 15_000¢ = 21_000¢, matching b19/subscription_fee/unequal/invoice. This is the one preview cell in the block where the per-fee split IS assertable, because the two fees carry different plan codes as `item_code` (fee.rb:123) and so are separable by `GoldenRunner::FEE_MATCH_KEYS`. That makes the row able to say more than the total: it pins each fee to its own subscription's plan, which is exactly the pairing `PreviewService#add_subscription_fee` could get wrong while still summing to a plausible number — building both fees from `first_subscription` reads 12_000¢, from the last 30_000¢, and mixing the plan of one with the boundaries of the other would show up as a wrong per-fee amount rather than a wrong total. Both subscriptions must be named in the step, or the runner previews only the last one created (15_000¢ against a 21_000¢ invoice). With both named, `currencies_aligned?` passes because both plans are EUR and `billing_times_aligned?` passes because both are calendar/monthly with the same `end_of_period` (preview_service.rb:84-103) — a mixed pair would be refused outright, and a preview refusing the multiplicity is a different finding from one mis-summing it.

Two subscriptions on different plans, consolidated onto one draft and rebuilt: 6_000¢ + 15_000¢ = 21_000¢, the same as the finalized b19/subscription_fee/unequal/invoice — producers are not gated on finalization (calculate_fees_service.rb:42 vs :364-379). Because the plans differ, `Fee#item_code` differs (fee.rb:123) and the rebuild's PAIRING is assertable, not just its total. `CalculateFeesService` walks the invoice's `invoice_subscriptions` and builds a subscription fee from each one's own subscription and boundaries (:20-47), so a refresh that re-resolved both fees from the same invoice_subscription would read 12_000¢ or 30_000¢, and one that kept the fees rather than replacing them would read 42_000¢ with `fees_count` 4. 6_000¢ against plan A and 15_000¢ against plan B is the only correct rebuild, and the amounts are far enough apart that no swap lands on 21_000¢. `invoices: 1` still asserts the consolidation itself, which the grace period does not change: `Subscriptions::OrganizationBillingService` groups by customer and never splits on plan (:15-44, :532-560). The three finalizing-gated reducers are asserted as 0 per the draft rule.

Two taxes at the same rate, both applied at the same level: do the rates ADD, or does one overwrite the other? They add, and the mechanism is a loop rather than a lookup. `Fees::ApplyTaxesService` iterates `applicable_taxes`, builds one `Fee::AppliedTax` per tax, and accumulates `applied_taxes_amount_cents += tax_amount_cents` and `applied_taxes_rate += tax.rate` (apply_taxes_service.rb:24-52). Both taxes here are created with `applied_to_organization: true`, so both become billing-entity taxes and both fall out of the final branch of `applicable_taxes` (:81-82) — the only branch that can return more than one tax from more than one source. 10_000¢ of subscription fee, 10% + 10% = 20% → 2_000¢ of tax, 12_000¢ due, and the fee's own `taxes_rate` reads 20.0 because that column is the SUM of the applied rates, not a single tax's. The failure this row is sized to catch is a last-one-wins implementation: 1_000¢ of tax, 11_000¢ due, `taxes_rate` 10.0 — half the VAT collected, on an invoice that still looks internally consistent. Asserting the fee's `taxes_rate` as well as the amount is what separates "one tax at 20%" from "two taxes at 10%", which the amounts alone cannot. Note the rounding is sum-then-round (`fee.taxes_amount_cents = applied_taxes_amount_cents.round` at :46-48, over unrounded per-tax floats), so on a base with a fractional half-cent per tax the two orders would differ by 1¢; 10_000¢ at 10% is exact in both, which keeps this row about additivity alone.

Two 10% taxes at the same level, forecast. The invoice arithmetic is derived in b19/tax/equal/invoice: the rates add to 20%, so 10_000¢ of fee carries 2_000¢ of tax. The preview must reach it through `PreviewService#apply_taxes`, which calls the same `Fees::ApplyTaxesService` per fee and then `Invoices::ApplyTaxesService` on the invoice (preview_service.rb:379-388) — so the per-tax loop and the `applied_taxes_rate +=` accumulation are shared, and what is NOT shared is the surrounding total arithmetic: `sub_total_including_taxes = sub_total_excluding_taxes + taxes` and `total = sub_total_including_taxes − credit_notes` are recomputed inline at preview_service.rb:310-316 rather than by `Invoices::ComputeTaxesAndTotalsService`. That is why all four totals are asserted on the preview and not just the tax: the risk is not that the two taxes fail to add on this surface but that the second one adds into the fee and then fails to reach the invoice header, which shows up as a 12_000¢ fee-level total under an 11_000¢ invoice-level one. A single-tax implementation reads 1_000¢ / 11_000¢ on both lines.

Tax is the one reducer a draft DOES carry, so this is the cell where a regeneration has to reproduce a non-zero amount rather than a zero. `Invoices::RefreshDraftService` rebuilds the draft by destroying its fees and re-running `CalculateFeesService`, and only the three finalizing-gated reducers drop out (calculate_fees_service.rb:364-379); `Invoices::ComputeTaxesAndTotalsService` runs unconditionally at :57. So both 10% taxes are re-resolved from the billing entity, re-summed by `Fees::ApplyTaxesService` (apply_taxes_service.rb:24-52) and the draft reads 2_000¢ of tax on 10_000¢ of fee — 20.0 on the fee's `taxes_rate` — exactly what the finalized twin b19/tax/equal/invoice reads. The two failure modes a refresh could introduce are both excluded here. One is a re-run that resolves only one of the two taxes (1_000¢, `taxes_rate` 10.0). The other is a re-run that re-applies taxes onto fees that already carry them — `Fees::ApplyTaxesService` opens with `return result if fee.applied_taxes.any?` (:18), which is a no-op on a REBUILT fee but a double-taxation guard on a reused one; had the refresh kept the fees and re-applied, the row would read 4_000¢ and 40.0. The three withheld reducers are asserted as 0 rather than omitted, so this row cannot pass by finding a draft that quietly allocated something.

Two taxes that do NOT add, because they are attached at different levels and the levels are ordered. This is the tax feature's version of "something decides which one goes first": for coupons it is a sort, for wallets a priority, and for taxes it is the guard chain in `Fees::ApplyTaxesService#applicable_taxes` (apply_taxes_service.rb:64-83), where the FIRST level that has any tax returns and every level below it is never consulted. A subscription fee reaches `if (fee.charge? || fee.subscription? || ...) && plan.taxes.any? → return plan.taxes` (:77-79) before `return customer.taxes if customer.taxes.any?` (:80). So the plan's 20% applies alone: 10_000¢ × 20% = 2_000¢, 12_000¢ due, fee `taxes_rate` 20.0. Both taxes are created with `applied_to_organization: false` so the billing-entity fallback at :81-82 cannot smuggle either of them back in. Three counterfactuals, all distinguishable on these numbers. Additive (the naive reading of "the customer has two taxes"): 25% → 2_500¢ and 12_500¢. Customer-wins: 5% → 500¢ and 10_500¢. Both levels merged and de-duplicated: still 25%. The rates are deliberately 20 and 5 rather than two equal rates, because with equal rates the precedence and the additive answers would differ only by a factor of two and a plan-vs-customer mix-up would be invisible. b19/tax/equal/invoice is the control: at the SAME level two taxes really do add, so this row records precedence, not a refusal to stack.

Precedence, forecast. A plan tax of 20% and a customer tax of 5%, and the plan's wins outright: `applicable_taxes` returns `plan.taxes` and never reaches `customer.taxes` (apply_taxes_service.rb:77-80), so 10_000¢ carries 2_000¢ and not 2_500¢. The reason this cell is worth a row of its own rather than being assumed from b19/tax/unequal/invoice is that a preview resolves the fee's associations differently. Its subscription fee is built by `Fees::SubscriptionService` with `context: :preview` and is never saved, and `Fees::ApplyTaxesService` is then called as `call(fee:)` with no `plan:` argument — so `plan` falls back to `fee.subscription&.plan` (apply_taxes_service.rb:11) rather than being handed down as it is from `CalculateFeesService`. If that fallback resolved to nil the guard `plan.taxes.any?` would raise, and if it resolved to an override plan without the tax the chain would fall through to the CUSTOMER's 5% and the preview would quote 10_500¢ against a 12_000¢ invoice. Asserting 2_000¢ on both surfaces is what pins the fallback to the same plan the invoice used. Counterfactuals on the preview line: additive 2_500¢ / 12_500¢, customer-wins 500¢ / 10_500¢, no tax at all 0¢ / 10_000¢ (the shape `apply_zero_tax` produces when provider taxation is misdetected, preview_service.rb:410-413).

Precedence, re-resolved from scratch. The plan's 20% wins over the customer's 5% because `applicable_taxes` returns at the plan level and never reads the customer's (apply_taxes_service.rb:77-80), so the draft reads 2_000¢ of tax and 12_000¢ due. This is the cell where a refresh is genuinely at risk rather than merely re-derived, because the refresh path is the one thing that RE-RUNS the precedence chain against whatever the records say now. `Customers::ApplyTaxesService` and `Taxes::UpdateService`/`DestroyService` are among the services that flag drafts `ready_to_be_refreshed` precisely so that a tax change is picked up, and `Invoices::RefreshDraftService` destroys the fees and rebuilds them — new `Fee` records with empty `applied_taxes`, so the chain is walked again from the top rather than reusing the resolution the original build made. A rebuild that lost the plan level would fall through to the customer's 5% and read 500¢ / 10_500¢; one that merged both levels would read 2_500¢ / 12_500¢ with `taxes_rate` 25.0. The fee's `taxes_rate` is asserted alongside the amount because the amounts alone cannot separate "one tax at 20%" from any other combination summing to 20. b19/tax/unequal/preview forecasts the same 2_000¢ and b19/tax/unequal/invoice finalizes it, so the three surfaces of this cell are pinned to one number.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the row that says a grace period is no protection against this one. Identical to b20/charge-replaced/paid_advance_fee/invoice except for a 5-day grace period, and the point is which invoices it reaches. The March period invoice is held open as a draft — 5_000¢, one subscription fee, and no charge fee at all because `create_charges_fees` excludes a pay-in-advance charge on a non-recurring metric (calculate_fees_service.rb:130-132). THE ADVANCE INVOICES ARE FINALIZED ANYWAY: Invoices::CreatePayInAdvanceChargeService calls Invoices::TransitionToFinalStatusService directly (:46) and never consults `grace_period?`, which only Invoices::SubscriptionService does (subscription_service.rb:177,193). So `status: finalized` is asserted on both of them rather than assumed. That is the whole content of this surface. The 5_000¢ the charge replacement wrongly billed on 18 March — 0¢ is what the cache would have produced, see the /invoice row's derivation — was taken on a finalized, customer-facing invoice five days before the period even closed, and the only invoice the grace period does hold open is the one that has nothing to do with it. There is no window in which the mistake could have been corrected before it was issued. THE NUMBERS THE ROW SEPARATES ARE STILL 5_000¢ AND 0¢ on index 2, and it separates them here with `status: finalized` attached, which is the thing the /invoice row cannot say.

CHARACTERIZATION. Replacing a charge record makes Lago forget how much of the period's peak usage the customer has already paid for, and it bills them for it a second time. The charge pays in advance and is invoiceable, so each event raises its own invoice (b03/standard/sum_agg/invoiceable is the uncomplicated version of that). 5 MARCH, +100. No cached aggregation yet, so SumService#compute_pay_in_advance_aggregation returns the event's own value 100 and writes `current_aggregation: 100, max_aggregation: 100` against THIS charge's id (create_pay_in_advance_service.rb:212-226). ApplyPayInAdvanceChargeModelService prices the delta as `amount_from_aggregation - amount_excluding_persisted_event` = 100 x 1.00 - 40... no: 100 x 1.00 - 0 x 1.00 = 100.00 → 10_000¢, units 100. That invoice is the positive evidence the state exists. 8 MARCH, -60. The cache is found: `current_aggregation` 100 - 60 = 40, `old_max` 100, and 40 is NOT greater than 100, so the delta is 0 and the cache is rewritten as `current 40, max 100` (:161-172). The fee is 40 x 1.00 - 40 x 1.00 = 0, and `display_applied_units_for_zero_invoice?` holds (40 <= 100) so the units shown are the applied -60, floored to 0 (apply_pay_in_advance_charge_model_service.rb:112-125). A 0¢ invoice is still raised, because Invoices::CreatePayInAdvanceChargeService returns early only on `fees.none?` (:16) and a 0¢ fee is a fee. THIS EVENT IS THE WHOLE POINT: it is what puts current below max, the one thing the cache carries that cannot be recomputed from the event stream. 12 MARCH, the churn. One id-less `update_plan` charges entry for the same metric: `Plans::UpdateService#process_charges` creates a charge (update_service.rb:230-235) and `sanitize_charges` discards the old one (:241-248). New charge_id, same plan, same subscription, same metric — and every CachedAggregation row still points at the dead id. 18 MARCH, +50. `find_cached_aggregation` scopes on `charge_id: charge.id` (aggregations/base_service.rb:230-243), which now matches nothing, so the service takes its no-cache branch and returns the raw 50 as the delta. The period sum is still 90 (aggregation reads events by metric, not by charge), so the fee is 90 x 1.00 - 40 x 1.00 = 50.00 → 5_000¢. THE NUMBER IF THE CACHE HAD BEEN FOUND IS 0¢. current would be 40 + 50 = 90 against a max of 100, 90 is not greater than 100, the delta is 0 and the fee is 90 x 1.00 - 90 x 1.00 = 0 — correct, because the customer already paid for a peak of 100 and 90 is still under it. So the row's two readings are 5_000¢ and 0¢ on the same event, and the customer pays 15_000¢ for a period whose peak usage cost 10_000¢. The 1 April period invoice carries only the 5_000¢ subscription fee: `create_charges_fees` skips the charge entirely via `.where.not(pay_in_advance: true, billable_metric: {recurring: false})` (calculate_fees_service.rb:130-132), so nothing there re-bills or corrects the advance fees.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the row that pins this surface as STRUCTURALLY BLIND to the whole column. The preview is taken on 25 March, a week after the replacement has already over-billed 5_000¢. It is a projection of March (`billing_time` = `end_of_periods.first + 1.day`, preview_service.rb:141-151), so it is a forecast of the very period the advance fees belong to. `Invoices::PreviewService#add_charge_fees` filters the plan's charges with the same two clauses CalculateFeesService uses — `.where(invoiceable: true)` and `.where.not(pay_in_advance: true, billable_metric: {recurring: false})` (preview_service.rb:184-192) — so a pay-in-advance charge on a non-recurring metric is excluded from the preview altogether. The quote is the 5_000¢ subscription fee and nothing else, and fees_count 1 is asserted to say so. THE PREVIEWED NUMBERS ARE THE SAME WHETHER THE CACHE WAS FOUND OR LOST — 5_000¢ either way — and that coincidence is the finding rather than a defect in the row. A customer who has been billed 15_000¢ in advance for a period worth 10_000¢ can ask Lago what this period will cost and be told 5_000¢, with no mention of the 15_000¢ already taken and no way for the answer to reflect the error. Every other surface in this block at least reports the wrong number; this one reports nothing. THE DISCRIMINATING ASSERTIONS ARE THEREFORE THE INVOICES BESIDE IT: index 0 at 10_000¢ is the positive evidence the cache existed, and index 2 at 5_000¢ with 50 units is the over-charge that a found cache would have priced at 0¢. Without them the preview block alone would guard nothing, which is exactly the trap this block's `observed_via` axis exists to expose.

CHARACTERIZATION. A refresh is the last chance to notice, and it does not take it. Identical to b20/charge-replaced/paid_advance_fee/draft plus one step: the March draft is refreshed on 2 April, after the replacement and after every advance invoice has been issued. Invoices::RefreshDraftService rebuilds the draft's fees from current configuration, and the configuration now says the charge pays in advance on a non-recurring metric — so `create_charges_fees` skips it exactly as it did the first time (calculate_fees_service.rb:130-132). The refreshed draft comes back with the same single 5_000¢ subscription fee, and fees_count 1 is asserted precisely to say no charge fee appeared. THE TWO READINGS THE ROW SEPARATES ARE NOT ON THE DRAFT. The draft is 5_000¢ whether or not the cache was found; what differs is index 2, still 5_000¢ where a found cache gives 0¢, and it is still finalized after the refresh. So the value of this surface is the negative result: nothing in the refresh path consults CachedAggregation, nothing reconciles the advance fees against the period's actual peak, and a 5_000¢ over-charge survives every recomputation Lago will ever perform on this period. Contrast b20/plan-override/paid_advance_fee/regenerated, where a refresh actively DELETES a 100_000¢ fixed-charge fee it decides is already paid. The same refresh, on the metric-charge side of `paid_advance_fee`, does not even look.

CHARACTERIZATION. The churn that rewrites `charge_id` and nothing else, on the surface where the lost credit costs money — and with usage AFTER the replacement, so the new charge is demonstrably the one doing the billing. 100 units cross the 5_000¢ threshold on 5 March and the threshold invoice takes 10_000¢ against the OLD charge id. The 10 March `update_plan` sends one id-less charges entry for the same metric: `Plans::UpdateService#process_charges` creates a charge for it (update_service.rb:230-235) and `sanitize_charges` discards the one the array did not name (:241-248), so the charge record is replaced while the plan, the subscription and the metric are untouched. 50 more units arrive on the 15th and are billed by the new charge, which is what makes the 15_000¢ below evidence that the replacement is live rather than a no-op. The March draft therefore bills 150 x 1.00 = 15_000¢ (aggregation queries events by metric, not by charge id) and Credits::ProgressiveBillingService caps the credit at `invoice.fees.charge.where(charge_id: progressive_billing_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id))` (progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33). Across the replacement that join matches nothing, the cap is 0, `amount_to_credit` > `total_charges_amount`, and the whole 10_000¢ becomes a credit note with `amount_to_credit` set to 0. A DRAFT MAY NOT SPEND A CREDIT NOTE (`should_create_credit_note_credit?` is false while not finalizing, calculate_fees_service.rb:364), so credit_notes_amount_cents is 0 and the draft asks for 15_000¢ on a period where 10_000¢ has already been collected. THE NUMBER IF THE STATE HAD BEEN FOUND IS 5_000¢: 15_000 of fees less a 10_000 progressive credit, which is what b05 gets when nothing is reconfigured. 15_000 vs 5_000, and progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 0 vs 10_000. Companion of b20/hns/charge-replaced/progressive_billing_credit/invoice, where the same diverted note is spent on the spot and the total is accidentally right. One rewritten column, two surfaces, and only the draft shows the money.

CHARACTERIZATION. `Invoices::PreviewService` keeps its own copy of the charge_id cap, so it is exposed to a charge replacement exactly as the invoice pipeline is — and it is the surface where the loss cannot be disguised. The threshold invoice takes 10_000¢ on 5 March; the charge is replaced on the 10th by one id-less `update_plan` charges entry (update_service.rb:230-248); the preview is taken on the 25th, after the replacement and before the period closes, as a projection of March (`billing_time` = `end_of_periods.first + 1.day`, preview_service.rb:141-151). `apply_progressive_billing_credits` reuses the read-only Subscriptions::ProgressiveBilledAmount, which still finds the threshold invoice because it joins on subscription and boundaries only, then filters with `billed_charge_ids = progressive_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id)` and `next 0 unless billed_charge_ids.include?(fee.charge_id)` (:346-352). The previewed fee belongs to the NEW charge, so the include? is false, `creditable_amount_cents` is 0, `amount_cents = [10_000, 0].min` is 0 and the guard `next unless amount_cents.positive?` drops the credit. A preview may not mint the credit note that hides the loss on a finalized invoice (:344-345), so the quote is the whole period again: 10_000¢ on a period that has already paid 10_000¢. THE NUMBER IF THE STATE HAD BEEN FOUND IS 0 with a 10_000¢ credit, which is what b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/preview asserts through the same preview code. THE INVOICE ASSERTED BESIDE IT DISAGREES WITH THE PREVIEW: 10_000¢ of fees, credit 0, a 10_000¢ credit note, total 0. Same rewritten column, two disguises, and the total alone can tell neither.

CHARACTERIZATION. A draft that was right becomes wrong when a charge record is swapped under it, with no plan clone and no new subscription to blame. The threshold invoice takes 10_000¢ on 5 March; the grace period is raised on the 6th, after it (Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 finalizes drafts when a period is shortened); the March invoice is drafted on 1 April WHILE THE ORIGINAL CHARGE IS STILL THERE, so its charge fee carries the same charge_id as the threshold fee, the cap at progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33 matches, 10_000¢ is credited and the draft sits at 0¢. The replacement lands on 2 April — one id-less `update_plan` charges entry, so `process_charges` creates a new charge and `sanitize_charges` discards the old (update_service.rb:230-248) — and the draft is refreshed on the 3rd. RefreshDraftService then destroys `invoice.credits.progressive_billing_invoice_kind` and zeroes progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents, rebuilds the charge fee from the NEW charge, and re-runs ProgressiveBillingService, which now finds `total_charges_amount` 0. `to_credit_amount` is back to the full 10_000¢ because the credit that netted it down was just destroyed, so the whole amount goes into CreditNotes::CreateFromProgressiveBillingInvoice. THE DRAFT GOES FROM 0¢ TO 10_000¢ and a 10_000¢ credit note appears that it may not spend. The customer has paid 10_000¢ and is shown 10_000¢ more. THE CONTROL IS b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/regenerated — identical shape, identical refresh, charge_id rewritten by an upgrade instead, and there the draft comes back at 0. So the refresh is not the cause; the refresh is only when the rewritten id is first consulted. And b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/regenerated is the same outcome reached by rewriting three columns instead of one, which together name `charge_id` as the sole cause. The credit note carries `select: {index: -1}` because without a selector expect.credit_note asserts the payload captured at CREATION by a `create_credit_note` step this row does not have.

CHARACTERIZATION. The same 2_000¢ of phantom tax, and this surface proves it is not the finalization stage that produces it. Identical to b20/filter-changed/progressive_billing_credit/invoice except that the grace period is raised to 5 days on 6 March — after the threshold invoice is finalized, because Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 issues existing drafts when the period is shortened rather than lengthened. The draft reads exactly what the finalized invoice reads. That is the finding, not an accident of duplication: everything the gate at calculate_fees_service.rb:364-379 withholds is asserted at 0 here (coupons, credit notes, prepaid credit), so the 2_000¢ cannot be a withheld reducer waiting to cancel it. Progressive billing runs at :53, ahead of the gate, and the tax stage runs unconditionally — so the mis-distribution and the tax it inflates both happen on a draft, and the number the customer will be charged is already visible five days before it is issued. THE CONTROL IS THE SAME TWO NUMBERS WITHOUT THE FILTER EDIT: credit 10_000¢, tax 0, total 0. And the counterfactual that this row's assertions rule out is a lost CAP rather than a lost distribution: had charge_id moved too, as it does under an override, the credit would be 0, a 10_000¢ credit note would be minted, the gate would withhold it and the draft would read 12_000¢ — which is b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/draft.

CHARACTERIZATION — a customer who has already paid 12_000¢ for a period worth 12_000¢ is invoiced 2_000¢ more, and the invoice says it credited every cent. Setup: one filter, `region: [eu]`, priced identically to the charge itself at 1.00, so PRICE never changes anywhere in this row and only IDENTITY does. 100 eu units cross the 5_000¢ threshold on 5 March: the threshold invoice bills 10_000¢ + 20% = 12_000¢, and its single charge fee carries charge_filter_id = the eu filter. On 10 March the filter's values are widened to `region: [eu, us]`. ChargeFilters::CreateOrUpdateBatchService resolves entries by their `values`, not by id (create_or_update_batch_service.rb:63-77): `{region: [eu, us]}` matches nothing already on the charge, so a NEW filter is inserted and the old eu filter is discarded at :77. The charge itself is untouched — same record, same id, same 1.00 — and the 100 eu units still match, now through a filter with a different UUID. The April invoice then splits in two:
  * THE CAP FINDS THE MONEY. progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33 matches on charge_id only, which
    the edit never touched, so total_charges_amount = 10_000¢, `amount_to_credit` 10_000 is not
    greater than it, no credit note is minted, and progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents reads
    the full 10_000¢. sub_total_excluding_taxes = 10_000 − 10_000 = 0.
  * THE DISTRIBUTION DOES NOT. apply_credit_to_fees (:70-76) requires
    `f.charge_filter_id == progressive_fee.charge_filter_id`; the threshold fee points at the
    discarded filter and the April fee at the new one, so the loop matches nothing and the April
    fee's precise_coupons_amount_cents stays 0.
Tax is computed from the FEES, not from the invoice sub-total: Invoices::ApplyTaxesService#compute_tax_amount_cents sums `fee.sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents` (apply_taxes_service.rb:78-82), and that is `amount_cents − precise_coupons_amount_cents` (fee.rb:238-239) = 10_000 − 0 = 10_000. So 20% of 10_000 = 2_000¢ of tax on an invoice whose own taxable sub-total is ZERO, and total = 0 + 2_000 = 2_000¢. THE CONTROL NUMBER IS 0. Leave the filter alone and the distribution matches, the fee's taxable base is clamped to 0, tax is 0 and the invoice settles at 0 — which is what b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/invoice shows with the same shape and no tax, and what b17/pb-coupon-tax/invoice shows with a tax. The 2_000¢ here is the entire content of the row. Both invoices are asserted because a broken setup is otherwise indistinguishable: if the threshold invoice had never been raised there would be no credit to distribute, the April invoice would read fees 10_000 / credit 0 / tax 2_000 / total 12_000, and the credit assertion is what separates that from this.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the only cell in this block where preview and invoice AGREE on a wrong number — which is exactly what identifies the cause. Invoices::PreviewService has no fee-level distribution at all: apply_progressive_billing_credits (preview_service.rb:330-358) adds the credit to invoice.progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents and stops there, so a previewed fee is ALWAYS taxed on its undiscounted amount. On every other progressive-billing row that makes the preview disagree with the invoice — b17/pb-coupon-tax records the pair at 2_600¢ against 714¢ — because the invoice clamps the fee's taxable base and the preview does not. Here the filter edit removes the invoice's clamp too, and the two land on the same 2_000¢. The agreement is the diagnosis: it says the invoice's tax has stopped being a function of what was credited and has become a function of the gross fee, which is precisely what a preview does when it has nothing to distribute. The cap behaves identically on both sides for the same reason it does on the invoice — the preview keeps its own copy of it, keyed on charge_id (`billed_charge_ids.include?(fee.charge_id)`, :346-352) — so both report the full 10_000¢ credited and a 0 sub-total. THE CONTROL: without the filter edit these two rows would differ, invoice 0¢ against preview 2_000¢. Asserting both surfaces in one row is what turns "the preview is wrong" into "the invoice has become as wrong as the preview", and the threshold invoice's 12_000¢ is what proves there was a credit to mis-distribute rather than none to begin with.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the sharpest form of this column: here the draft is built CORRECTLY first and the refresh breaks it. The order is the point. The April 1 draft is computed while the eu filter still exists, so its charge fee carries the same charge_filter_id as the threshold fee, apply_credit_to_fees matches, the fee's taxable base is clamped to 0 and the draft settles at 0¢. Only then, on 2 April, is the filter widened; on the 3rd the draft is refreshed. RefreshDraftService destroys the fees, the applied taxes and `invoice.credits.progressive_billing_invoice_kind`, zeroes progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents and re-runs CalculateFeesService against the charge as it stands now. `to_credit_amount` is therefore back to the full 10_000¢ (the credit that had netted it down is gone, and no credit note was ever minted), the cap still matches on charge_id, the distribution now does not, and the draft comes back at 2_000¢. So a refresh MOVES a draft from 0¢ to 2_000¢ with no configuration change the invoice can show: the charge is the same record at the same price and the fee's units and amount are identical. Only a UUID moved. `PUT /invoices/:id/refresh` is used rather than the clock job on purpose — Charges::UpdateService does not set ready_to_be_refreshed (unlike Plans::UpdateService), so Clock::RefreshDraftInvoicesJob would never pick this draft up and the row would assert the UNREFRESHED 0¢ while claiming to test a refresh. The endpoint ignores the flag, which is what makes this cell reachable at all — and finalization ignores it too (RefreshDraftAndFinalizeService passes context: :finalize without consulting it), so the 2_000¢ arrives with or without the explicit refresh. This row makes the mechanism visible while the invoice is still a draft.

CHARACTERIZATION. A charge REPLACEMENT loses a progressive-billing credit exactly the way a plan override does, and it is the churn that isolates the cause: no plan is cloned and no plan_id moves, only `charge_id`. `Plans::UpdateService#process_charges` (update_service.rb:230-235) creates a charge for a payload entry carrying no `id`, and `sanitize_charges` (:241-248) then discards every charge the array did not name — so ONE `update_plan` body with a single id-less entry for the same metric replaces the charge record while leaving the plan, the subscription and the metric untouched. 100 units cross the 5_000¢ threshold on 5 March and 10_000¢ is collected on a progressive_billing invoice whose charge fee carries the OLD charge_id. The 10 March replacement mints a new charge; the period invoice bills the same 100 units through it (aggregation queries events by metric code, not by charge id) so fees are again 10_000¢. `Credits::ProgressiveBillingService` then caps the credit at `invoice.fees.charge.where(charge_id: progressive_billing_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id))` (progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33) — which matches NOTHING across the replacement, so the cap is 0, `amount_to_credit > total_charges_amount` holds, and the whole 10_000¢ is diverted into CreditNotes::CreateFromProgressiveBillingInvoice with `amount_to_credit` set to 0. Hence progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 0 and a 10_000¢ credit note. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 10_000 and credit_notes_amount_cents 0 — which is what b05 gets when nothing is reconfigured. The total is 0 either way, which is the trap: only the two fields above tell a credit from a numbered, separately-spendable credit note. Companion of b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/invoice: same symptom, one rewritten column instead of three, so the two together name `charge_id` as the sole cause.

CHARACTERIZATION. Deleting a billable metric takes the metric-limited coupon with it, and neither the invoice nor the coupon says so. March is the control. The plan bills 5_000¢ and 100 units bill 100 x 1.00 = 10_000¢, so fees are 15_000¢. `Credits::AppliedCouponService#billable_metric_related_fees` (applied_coupon_service.rb:120-125) scopes the discountable fees to `invoice.fees.joins(charge: :billable_metric).where(billable_metric: {id: ...coupon_targets})` — an INNER JOIN through `charge`, so the subscription fee is never a candidate and the base is the 10_000¢ charge fee alone. The fixed 2_000¢ therefore comes off a 10_000¢ base, not a 15_000¢ one: coupons 2_000, sub-total 13_000. On 10 April `BillableMetrics::DestroyService` discards the metric AND `metric.charges.update_all(deleted_at:)` (destroy_service.rb:29). Charge carries `default_scope -> { kept }` (models/charge.rb:62), so April's invoice has no charge fee at all — fees_count 1 at 5_000¢ — and the coupon's join finds nothing. `fees.any?` is false, so AppliedCouponService returns at :22 BEFORE creating any Credit: coupons_amount_cents 0, and `frequency_duration_remaining` is not even decremented, so the coupon sits at full life on a customer it can never discount again. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 3_000¢. A reader who assumes a fixed-amount coupon falls back to the whole invoice when its limitation no longer resolves would expect 5_000 − 2_000; a reader who assumes the discarded charge still bills its accrued usage (it does not — see F05) would expect fees 15_000 again. Both are named here, and both are wrong. fees_count is asserted on both invoices because it is the only field that distinguishes "the charge was deleted" from "the period simply had no usage", and sub_total is asserted beside the coupon because the coupon is the sole difference between it and fees_amount_cents.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the surface that separates the deletion from the clock. A 30-day grace period holds March's invoice as a DRAFT, so the 1 April run produces fees 15_000¢ (5_000¢ plan + 100 x 1.00) and NO coupon: a draft carries no coupon, no credit note and no prepaid credit, all three gated on `not_in_finalizing_process?` (calculate_fees_service.rb:364-379). So coupons_amount_cents is 0 both before and after the churn, and what this row pins is the FEE the coupon is anchored to — the only thing `billable_metric_related_fees` can join to (applied_coupon_service.rb:120-125). On 5 April the metric is deleted. `BillableMetrics::DestroyService` is one of the four writers that flag drafts for recomputation: `Invoice.where(id: draft_invoice_ids).update_all(ready_to_be_refreshed: true)` over `Invoice.draft.joins(plans: [:billable_metrics])` (destroy_service.rb:23-31). That flag is the ONLY thing Clock::RefreshDraftInvoicesJob consults, so the 6 April refresh recomputes the draft and the charge fee — whose charge was discarded in the same transaction — is gone: fees_count 1, fees_amount_cents 5_000, total 5_000. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 15_000¢ WITH TWO FEES, and it is not hypothetical — it is what `Charges::UpdateService` produces for the same shape of change, because it does not set the flag (see the B18 rows). So this row is simultaneously the evidence that the deletion reaches an open invoice and the evidence that a charge edit does not. The finalized reading of the same churn is b20/hns/metric-deleted/coupon_application/invoice, where the coupon is live and drops from 2_000¢ to 0¢; here it was never applied at all, which is why `invoices: 1` and `status: draft` are asserted — a row that accidentally finalized would be measuring that other cell.

CHARACTERIZATION. March is the positive evidence that the coupon existed and worked; April is what the deletion leaves of it, held open so the two reducers can be told apart. MARCH, finalized. 5_000¢ plan + 100 x 1.00 = 15_000¢ of fees. `Credits::AppliedCouponService#billable_metric_related_fees` (applied_coupon_service.rb:120-125) scopes the discountable fees to `invoice.fees.joins(charge: :billable_metric)` — an INNER JOIN through `charge`, so the subscription fee is never a candidate and the 2_000¢ comes off the 10_000¢ charge fee, not off 15_000¢. coupons 2_000, sub-total 13_000. Without this invoice the row could not tell a coupon that stopped working from a coupon that never applied. APRIL, draft. The grace period is raised on 5 April — after March finalized, so Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 has no draft to issue. 100 more units arrive on the 10th, which is the whole point: the period the churn affects contains usage a live metric bills at 10_000¢, so the row cannot pass identically either way. On the 20th `BillableMetrics::DestroyService` discards the metric and its charges (:29), and the `kept` default scope (models/charge.rb:62) then empties `subscription.plan.charges`: fees_count 1, 5_000¢. THE NUMBER IF THE METRIC HAD SURVIVED IS 15_000¢ WITH TWO FEES. coupons_amount_cents is 0 EITHER WAY, because a draft withholds coupons entirely (`not_in_finalizing_process?`, calculate_fees_service.rb:364-379) — so what this row pins on the draft surface is the FEE the coupon is anchored to, the only thing `billable_metric_related_fees` can join to, and the difference is 5_000 vs 15_000 rather than 0 vs 2_000. The finalized sibling b20/metric-deleted/coupon_application/invoice is where the coupon itself moves, from 2_000¢ to 0¢, and where `frequency_duration_remaining` is shown never to decrement because AppliedCouponService returns at :22 on `fees.any?` being false. The two rows are the same deletion read through the two halves of the gate.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the row that says this cell's own axis is invisible on this surface. March finalized at 13_000¢ is the positive evidence: a metric-limited coupon takes 2_000¢ off the 10_000¢ charge fee (applied_coupon_service.rb:120-125). April is previewed on the 25th, five days after the metric is deleted; the projection is April, because `Invoices::PreviewService#billing_time` is `end_of_periods.first + 1.day` for a persisted subscription (preview_service.rb:141-151). THE COUPON IS 0¢ ON THE PREVIEW BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER THE CHURN, and that coincidence is the finding rather than a defect in the row. `Coupons::PreviewService#fees` returns `Fee.none` for any `limited_billable_metrics?` coupon and the loop then `next`s on `fees.none?` (coupons/preview_service.rb:27,76-86), so a metric-limited coupon is never applied to a preview at all — the churn cannot move a number that is structurally zero. That is F71, and pinning it here is what stops a future reader from taking the 0 as evidence that the deletion broke the coupon. WHAT DOES MOVE, AND WHAT THIS ROW THEREFORE GUARDS, IS THE FEE: 5_000¢ previewed against the 15_000¢ a live metric would have carried, because `add_charge_fees` reads `subscription.plan.charges` under the `kept` default scope (preview_service.rb:184-192) and the discarded charge is gone from it. The two invoices asserted beside it are where the coupon axis is real — 2_000¢ in March, 0¢ in April once `billable_metric_related_fees` joins to nothing — so the row reads as the divergence it is: the invoice loses 2_000¢ of discount it was applying, and the preview cannot report either the discount or its loss.

CHARACTERIZATION. The same silence, with the period invoice held open — which is what says the silence is not a timing artefact. Identical to b20/metric-deleted/paid_advance_fee/invoice except for a 5-day grace period. The 5 March advance invoice is FINALIZED regardless, because Invoices::CreatePayInAdvanceChargeService calls TransitionToFinalStatusService directly (:46) and only Invoices::SubscriptionService consults `grace_period?` (subscription_service.rb:177,193) — asserted here rather than assumed. The March period invoice is a draft, and it carries the 5_000¢ subscription fee and nothing else. THE READING THIS SURFACE ADDS is that the 200 unbilled units do not turn up on the open invoice either. One might reasonably expect a period held open past the churn to sweep up usage the advance path dropped; it does not, because `create_charges_fees` excludes the charge on two independent grounds — `.where.not(pay_in_advance: true, billable_metric: {recurring: false})` and the `kept` default scope that has removed it from `subscription.plan.charges` altogether (calculate_fees_service.rb:130-132, models/charge.rb:62). fees_count 1 is the assertion. THE NUMBER IF THE STATE HAD BEEN FOUND IS STILL 20_000¢ on a third invoice, so this row and its /invoice sibling separate the same two readings — 15_000¢ collected versus 35_000¢ owed — and this one adds that no open invoice ever gets the chance to correct it.

CHARACTERIZATION. Deleting a metric does not stop its pay-in-advance events arriving — it stops them being billed, silently, with no invoice, no fee and no error. 5 MARCH, +100. The charge pays in advance and is invoiceable, so the event raises its own invoice at once: 100 units x 1.00 = 10_000¢, and a CachedAggregation row against this charge's id holding `current 100, max 100` (create_pay_in_advance_service.rb:212-226). That invoice is the positive evidence the machinery worked before the churn — without it a row asserting silence afterwards would pass on a subscription that never billed anything at all. 12 MARCH. `BillableMetrics::DestroyService` discards the metric and `metric.charges.update_all(deleted_at:)` (destroy_service.rb:29). 18 MARCH, +200. `Events::PostProcessService#handle_pay_in_advance` returns before enqueueing anything: its `charges` lookup is `subscription.plan.charges.pay_in_advance.joins(:billable_metric).where(billable_metric: {code:})` (:136-146), and both `Charge` and `BillableMetric` carry a `kept` default scope, so it comes back empty and `return unless charges.any?` (:131) fires. No Fees::CreatePayInAdvanceService call, no fee, no invoice — hence `invoices: 2`, which is the assertion that carries the whole finding. THE NUMBER IF THE STATE HAD BEEN FOUND IS 20_000¢ ON A THIRD INVOICE. With the metric alive the cache is found, `current_aggregation` 100 + 200 = 300 exceeds `max_aggregation` 100, so the delta is 300 - 100 = 200 and the fee is 300 x 1.00 - 100 x 1.00 = 200.00 → 20_000¢ (sum_service.rb:161-168). So the two readings of this row are three invoices totalling 35_000¢ and two totalling 15_000¢: 200 units of usage the customer consumed and was never asked to pay for. A deleted metric legitimately stops BILLING. What it should not do is keep accepting events for a charge that no longer exists while the period invoice reports nothing unusual: the 1 April invoice is a clean 5_000¢ subscription fee, fees_count 1, with no trace that 200 units went past. Compare b20/charge-replaced/paid_advance_fee/invoice, where the same lost `charge_id` on the same cache costs the customer 5_000¢ EXTRA. One column, two churns, opposite directions of error — which is why the invoice count and the per-fee units are both asserted here rather than the total alone.

CHARACTERIZATION. What the customer is quoted while 200 units of their usage are going unbilled: the same 5_000¢ they would be quoted if everything were working. The preview is taken on 25 March, after the deletion and after the dropped events, as a projection of March (`billing_time` = `end_of_periods.first + 1.day`, preview_service.rb:141-151). `add_charge_fees` excludes the charge twice over — `.where.not(pay_in_advance: true, billable_metric: {recurring: false})` (preview_service.rb:184-192) would have excluded it even while the metric lived, and the `kept` default scope (models/charge.rb:62) has now removed it from `subscription.plan.charges` entirely. So the quote is the 5_000¢ subscription fee, fees_count 1. THE PREVIEWED NUMBERS DO NOT MOVE WITH THE CHURN — 5_000¢ before the deletion and 5_000¢ after — and saying so is the point of the row rather than a weakness in it. `paid_advance_fee` is not a state this surface can observe at all: preview never quotes an in-advance charge on a non-recurring metric, so it can neither report the 200 units that were dropped nor the 20_000¢ they were worth. Any future row that reads a healthy preview here as evidence the advance path is healthy is reading a constant. THE DISCRIMINATING ASSERTIONS ARE THE INVOICES BESIDE IT: index 0 at 10_000¢ proves the advance path worked before the churn, and `invoices: 2` proves the 18 March event raised nothing — where the control b20/metric-deleted/paid_advance_fee/regenerated has three invoices and a 20_000¢ one among them.

THE CONTROL FOR THIS WHOLE COLUMN, and the row that turns the two rows above from a symptom into a trigger. Here the churn lands AFTER the events, so the cache is found every time, and every number is the one the /invoice and /draft rows say is missing. The order is deliberately reversed. 100 units on 5 March raise a 10_000¢ advance invoice and write `current 100, max 100`; the grace period is raised on the 6th, after that invoice is finalized; 200 units on 18 March find the cache — `find_cached_aggregation` scopes on `charge_id: charge.id` (aggregations/base_service.rb:230-243) and the charge is still the same record — so `current_aggregation` 300 exceeds `max_aggregation` 100, the delta is 200 and the fee is 300 x 1.00 - 100 x 1.00 = 200.00 → 20_000¢ (sum_service.rb:161-168). THAT 20_000¢ INVOICE IS THE NUMBER b20/metric-deleted/paid_advance_fee/invoice DOES NOT HAVE, on an identical setup whose only difference is that the deletion had not happened yet. The March draft is then raised on 1 April at 5_000¢, the metric is deleted on the 2nd — `BillableMetrics::DestroyService` collects `Invoice.draft.joins(plans: [:billable_metrics])` at :23 BEFORE discarding the charges at :29, which is the only reason the draft gets flagged at all — and `perform_invoices_refresh` on the 3rd recomputes it, because that flag is the sole thing Clock::RefreshDraftInvoicesJob consults. THE REFRESH CHANGES NOTHING, and that is the second thing this row establishes. The draft comes back with the same single 5_000¢ subscription fee: the deletion cannot claw back the two advance invoices, and the refresh does not try. So the 35_000¢ collected here is correct and stays correct, while the 15_000¢ collected by the /invoice row for the same 300 units stays wrong. Same code, same amounts, one step reordered. `invoices: 3` against the siblings' `invoices: 2` is the load-bearing assertion — the count is what says the missing money is a missing INVOICE and not a mispriced one.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the surface where the diverted credit cannot be spent at all. Identical to b20/metric-deleted/progressive_billing_credit/invoice except for a 5-day grace period, which is safe to declare in `setup` here because the threshold invoice is not raised by Invoices::SubscriptionService and is finalized regardless — asserted, not assumed, by `status: finalized` on it. The deletion diverts the same 10_000¢ into a credit note, but a draft may not consume one: `should_create_credit_note_credit?` returns false while `not_in_finalizing_process?` (calculate_fees_service.rb:364-379). So credit_notes_amount_cents is 0 and the draft asks for the 8_000¢ subscription fee in full on top of the 10_000¢ already collected, while the whole 10_000¢ note sits unspent at `balance_amount_cents: 10000`. THE NUMBER IF THE STATE HAD BEEN FOUND IS 14_000¢ — with the metric alive the draft carries 8_000 + 16_000 = 24_000¢ of fees and progressive billing is the one reducer a draft still applies (it runs at :53, ahead of the gate), so 10_000¢ is credited and the draft reads 14_000¢. Here it reads 8_000¢: a smaller number reached by deleting 16_000¢ of billable usage and refusing the 10_000¢ that was supposed to offset it. Pairs with the /invoice row exactly as lead 1's two rows pair: on the finalized surface the note is spent on the spot and the invoice settles at 0, so the loss is invisible in the total; hold the same invoice open and the customer is shown a bill on money they have already paid.

CHARACTERIZATION. Deleting the metric deletes the fee the progressive credit was collected against, so the money comes back as a credit note LARGER than the invoice it lands on — and the remainder is left sitting on the customer as a separate refundable document. 100 units cross the 5_000¢ threshold on 5 March and the threshold invoice takes the whole accrued 10_000¢. 60 more units arrive on the 8th with no `perform_usage_update`, so no second threshold invoice is raised and March now holds 160 units the period is due to bill. On 10 March `BillableMetrics::DestroyService` discards the metric and, in the same transaction, `metric.charges.update_all(deleted_at:)` (destroy_service.rb:29). `Charge` carries `default_scope -> { kept }` (models/charge.rb:62), so `subscription.plan.charges` is empty when CalculateFeesService builds the March invoice: fees_count 1, the 8_000¢ subscription fee alone. Credits::ProgressiveBillingService then caps the credit at `invoice.fees.charge.where(charge_id: progressive_billing_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id))` (progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33). `invoice.fees.charge` is EMPTY, so the cap is 0, `amount_to_credit` (10_000) > `total_charges_amount` (0), and the entire 10_000¢ is handed to CreditNotes::CreateFromProgressiveBillingInvoice with `amount_to_credit` set to 0 — progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 0. The note is then spent at stage :62 up to what the invoice can absorb: credit_notes 8_000 on a 8_000¢ invoice, total 0, and 2_000¢ of credit-note balance left over. THE NUMBER IF THE STATE HAD BEEN FOUND IS 14_000¢, not 0. With the metric alive the same period bills 8_000 + 160 x 1.00 = 24_000¢, the cap is the 16_000¢ charge fee, 10_000 <= 16_000 so no note is minted at all, and the invoice settles at 24_000 - 10_000 = 14_000¢ with progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 10_000 and credit_notes_amount_cents 0. Every asserted field moves, which is what makes the row a guard rather than a decoration: fees 8_000 vs 24_000, credit 0 vs 10_000, notes 8_000 vs 0, total 0 vs 14_000. The threshold invoice is asserted `finalized` beside it because ProgressiveBilledAmount only reads invoices that are finalized or failed (progressive_billed_amount.rb:28-38) — a threshold invoice held back as a draft would make every line above true for the wrong reason.

CHARACTERIZATION. The fourth implementation of the same cap, and the surface on which the diverted credit has nowhere to hide. The preview is taken on 25 March, after the deletion and before the period closes. It is a PROJECTION: `Invoices::PreviewService#billing_time` returns `end_of_periods.first + 1.day` for a persisted subscription (preview_service.rb:141-151), so the previewed period is March, the same period the 1 April run bills. `add_charge_fees` reads `subscription.plan.charges` under the same `kept` default scope (preview_service.rb:184-192), so the previewed invoice carries the 8_000¢ subscription fee and nothing else. `apply_progressive_billing_credits` then reuses the read-only Subscriptions::ProgressiveBilledAmount — which still finds the threshold invoice, because it is scoped by subscription and boundaries and not by any charge — and applies its OWN copy of the cap: `billed_charge_ids = progressive_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id)` and `next 0 unless billed_charge_ids.include?(fee.charge_id)` (:346-352). The subscription fee's `charge_id` is nil, so `creditable_amount_cents` is 0, `amount_cents = [10_000, 0].min` is 0, and `next unless amount_cents.positive?` drops the credit. A preview may not issue a credit note (:344-345 says the excess is simply dropped), so there is no second spelling of the money to make the total look right: the customer is quoted 8_000¢ for a period on which 10_000¢ has already been collected. THE NUMBER IF THE STATE HAD BEEN FOUND IS 14_000¢ — with the metric alive the preview carries 8_000 + 16_000 = 24_000¢, the charge fee's id IS in `billed_charge_ids`, creditable is 16_000 and the credit is min(10_000, 16_000) = 10_000. So the previewed total moves 14_000 -> 8_000 and the credit 10_000 -> 0. THE INVOICE IS ASSERTED BESIDE IT AND DISAGREES: same fees, but a 8_000¢ credit note application brings it to 0. Same lost state, two disguises — the invoice hides it in a credit note and settles at zero, the preview shows a bill for a period already paid for. That contrast is why `observed_via` is an axis, and why a row asserting only the finalized total would have called this cell healthy. ONE live charge is load-bearing for a different reason too: F72 500s the preview on any plan with two or more untaxed charges, so this row could not have used a surviving second metric.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the only row in this column where the loss can be watched happening, because the draft is correct first and wrong afterwards. The order is deliberately the reverse of the /invoice and /draft rows. The threshold invoice takes 10_000¢ on 5 March; the grace period is raised on the 6th, AFTER it, because Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 finalizes existing drafts when a period is shortened and a grace period declared in `setup` would have put a later reading at risk; 60 more units land on the 8th; and the March invoice is drafted on 1 April WHILE THE METRIC IS STILL ALIVE. At that point it is right: 8_000¢ + 160 x 1.00 = 24_000¢ of fees, the charge_id cap matches the threshold fee, 10_000¢ is credited, and the draft reads 14_000¢ with no credit note anywhere. On 2 April the metric is deleted. `BillableMetrics::DestroyService` is one of the four writers that flag open drafts — it collects `Invoice.draft.joins(plans: [:billable_metrics])` at :23, BEFORE discarding the charges at :29, which is the only reason the flag is set at all — and that flag is the sole thing `Clock::RefreshDraftInvoicesJob` consults, so `perform_invoices_refresh` on the 3rd is what makes this the regenerated surface rather than an endpoint call that ignores it. RefreshDraftService then loses the money in three steps: `reset_invoice_values` destroys `invoice.credits.progressive_billing_invoice_kind` and zeroes progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents; CalculateFeesService rebuilds fees from `subscription.plan.charges`, which the `kept` default scope has just emptied; and ProgressiveBillingService re-runs against an invoice with no charge fees, so the cap is 0, the threshold invoice's `to_credit_amount` is back to the full 10_000¢ now that the credit which netted it down is gone, and the whole amount is diverted into a credit note the draft may not spend. THE DRAFT GOES FROM 14_000¢ TO 8_000¢ AND A 10_000¢ CREDIT NOTE APPEARS. Correct settlement for a customer who paid 10_000¢ and owes 8_000¢ is a 2_000¢ refund; what they get is an 8_000¢ bill and a separate 10_000¢ document. fees_count 1 is asserted with the amount because a charge fee rebuilt at 0¢ and a charge fee not rebuilt at all are different bugs and only the count separates them.

CHARACTERIZATION. The cancelled commitment is visible five days before the invoice is issued, which is the useful half of this cell: a producer is not gated, so a draft is a truthful preview of the loss rather than an artefact of withheld reducers. Identical to b20/plan-override/commitment_progress/invoice except the grace period is raised to 5 days on 2 April — after the March invoice has finalized, since Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 issues existing drafts when the period is shortened, not lengthened. March stays finalized at 10_000¢ with its three fees; April is held open. The April draft reads 5_000¢. The commitment true-up is created at calculate_fees_service.rb:46, in the producer phase, ABOVE the `not_in_finalizing_process?` gate at :364-379 — so unlike a coupon or a credit note it would appear on a draft if it existed. It does not appear, and coupons_amount_cents / credit_notes_amount_cents are asserted at 0 to say that no withheld reducer is standing in for it: 5_000¢ is the whole of what the period holds. THE CONTROL NUMBER IS 10_000¢ — three fees, as March has. b12's thirty-six cells cover this commitment in every interval and billing time and cannot see this, because none of them holds an invoice open or reconfigures the plan underneath one.

CHARACTERIZATION — a plan override silently cancels the minimum commitment, and the customer's floor drops from 10_000¢ to whatever they happen to use. March is the control, and it is the positive evidence this block requires: 2_000¢ plan + 30 units x 1.00 = 5_000¢ of billable content against a 10_000¢ floor, so Commitments::Minimum::InArrears::CalculateTrueUpFeeService raises a 5_000¢ commitment fee (calculate_true_up_fee_service.rb:37-41, `commitment_amount_cents - fees_total_amount_cents`) and the invoice reads 10_000¢ across three fees. The period is whole, so the proration coefficient is 31/31 = 1 and the floor is the full 10_000¢. On 10 April the subscription is updated with `plan_overrides` carrying nothing but a name — no price change is needed, because the override itself is the churn. Subscriptions::UpdateService takes the `handle_plan_override` branch, Plans::OverrideService dups the plan (so amount_cents 2_000 and the 1.00 charge both survive: `plan.dup`, then Charges::OverrideService per charge) and repoints the subscription at the clone. The commitment is NOT dup'd. It is a separate record, rebuilt only from `params[:minimum_commitment]` (override_service.rb:64-72), and the request carried none — so `subscription.plan.minimum_commitment` is nil from 10 April on. April therefore bills 2_000 + 3_000 = 5_000¢ and stops. `should_create_minimum_commitment_true_up_fee?` calls the calculator, which returns 0 for a nil commitment (`return 0 if !minimum_commitment`), and the guard at :257 drops the fee. THE TWO NUMBERS ARE 5_000¢ AND 10_000¢, and fees_count is asserted with them because the amount alone cannot say WHY: April spending its way up to 10_000¢ of usage would also read 10_000¢, with two fees rather than three. March's three fees and April's two are what name the missing one. The counterfactual is not hypothetical — it is what the customer signed. Every subsequent period on this subscription has no floor, and nothing on the plan anyone reads says so.

CHARACTERIZATION. The quote agrees with the invoice, and both are 5_000¢ below the floor the customer contracted for. Invoices::PreviewService reimplements the whole pipeline, and it reaches the commitment through the same single reference the invoice does: `add_commitment_fee` opens with `return unless subscription.plan.minimum_commitment` (preview_service.rb:259-260). The override on 10 April left the subscription on a clone with no commitment, so the guard fires and the previewed April invoice carries the subscription fee and the charge fee only — 2_000 + 3_000 = 5_000¢, two fees, no true-up, and the 1 May invoice confirms it. That agreement matters because preview and invoice differ constantly elsewhere in this block (b20/filter-changed/progressive_billing_credit/preview, b17/pb-coupon-tax/preview). Here they do not, and the reason is structural: a commitment is not a reducer with two implementations to drift apart — it is one nil check on the plan, made twice. THE CONTROL NUMBER IS 10_000¢ WITH THREE FEES, asserted on the March invoice in this same row. Without the override the preview would quote the true-up too, because a preview applies producers unconditionally; with it, neither surface can see the commitment and the customer is quoted the reduced amount as though it were correct. The charge deliberately has usage in the previewed period: Invoices::PreviewService dies on a plan whose charge has no usage (three nils in one path), so a zero-usage April would fail this row with a 500 rather than a disagreement.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the version of this cell in which the money is watched leaving. The order is deliberately the reverse of the other three rows: the April draft is built on 1 May while the commitment is still on the plan, so it is created holding 2_000 + 3_000 + a 5_000¢ true-up = 10_000¢. The override lands on 2 May, the refresh on the 3rd. RefreshDraftService destroys the fees and re-runs CalculateFeesService against the plan the subscription now points at — the clone, which has no commitment — and rebuilds the draft as 2_000 + 3_000 = 5_000¢. The subscription fee and the charge fee both come back UNCHANGED, because Plans::OverrideService dup'd the plan's amount_cents and Charges::OverrideService dup'd the 1.00 charge; only the commitment, which is rebuilt from params rather than dup'd, is gone. So this row asserts a 5_000¢ swing produced by a refresh whose configuration diff is a plan NAME. THE CONTROL IS 10_000¢ WITH THREE FEES, which is both what the draft held before the refresh and what March still reads — and March is asserted here for exactly that reason: it is the same machinery, on the same subscription, producing the true-up correctly, which is what rules out "the commitment was never configured" as an explanation for April. Note what does NOT need to be true for this to bite: nothing flagged the draft. Plans::UpdateService sets ready_to_be_refreshed and Subscriptions::UpdateService does not, so the clock job would leave this draft alone and it would finalize on 6 May through RefreshDraftAndFinalizeService, which calls the same service with context: :finalize WITHOUT consulting the flag.
