The 5_000¢ arrives either way; the explicit refresh only makes it observable while the invoice still exists as a draft.

THE SURFACE THAT CANNOT ANSWER THE QUESTION, stated as such rather than dressed up. Coupons are gated: `should_create_coupon_credit?` returns false while `not_in_finalizing_process?` (calculate_fees_service.rb:367-373), so a draft carries no coupon at all — whether or not the plan join would have found one. The April draft therefore reads 15_000¢ with coupons_amount_cents 0, and that 0 is NOT evidence about the churn. What this row does establish, and why it is worth a cell rather than a footnote:
  * The coupon exists and works on this subscription — March, in the same row, is finalized with
    2_000¢ discounted. Without that assertion a reader cannot tell a gated coupon from an absent
    one, which is precisely the silent-lookup failure mode this block exists to catch.
  * The gating is the ONLY reason for the 0. credit_notes_amount_cents and
    prepaid_credit_amount_cents are asserted at 0 beside it because they are gated by the same
    three lines, and sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents 15_000 says nothing has been taken off
    the fees at all.
  * The churn did not disturb the producers: fees are 15_000¢ before and after the override, so the
    override changed no price and the whole of the difference between this row and its /invoice
    sibling (13_000¢) is the withheld coupon.
The gating is deliberate — it stops a draft from consuming a `once` coupon that a refresh would have to give back — so this row is intended behaviour, not characterization. The cell's real answer lives in b20/plan-override/coupon_application/invoice, and this row is what says the draft could never have shown it.

THE ONE JOIN IN THIS BLOCK SOMEBODY ALREADY FIXED, and the row that stops it regressing. A coupon limited to `plan_codes: [golden_b20_w1_cpi]` discounts 2_000¢ of a 15_000¢ period (5_000¢ plan + 100 units x 1.00). March is the control: fees 15_000, coupon 2_000, total 13_000. On 10 April the subscription is overridden, so from then on `subscription.plan_id` is the CLONE's and the coupon names the parent. April still discounts 2_000¢, because Credits::AppliedCouponService#plan_related_fees scopes on `plan: {id: applied_coupon.coupon.parent_and_overriden_plans.map(&:id)}` (applied_coupon_service.rb:113-118) and Coupon#parent_and_overriden_plans is `plans + plans.map(&:children)` (coupon.rb:91-93) — Plans::OverrideService sets `p.parent_id = plan.id` on the clone, so the clone is one of those children. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 15_000¢, and it is not hypothetical: it is what the PREVIEW of this same period quotes, because Coupons::PreviewService compares plan_id exactly. See b20/plan-override/coupon_application/preview. fees_amount_cents is asserted on both invoices so the row cannot pass on a period that billed nothing, and sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents alongside the coupon amount because the coupon is the only thing between the two: 15_000 − 2_000 = 13_000. `frequency_duration: 6` is generous on purpose — the coupon is spent twice here and must still be live in April, so a 0 in that column can only mean the plan join missed, never that the coupon ran out.

CHARACTERIZATION — the same coupon, the same period, two implementations of the same plan join, and only one of them was taught about overrides. The customer is quoted 15_000¢ and billed 13_000¢. The invoice keeps the coupon: Credits::AppliedCouponService#plan_related_fees scopes on `applied_coupon.coupon.parent_and_overriden_plans.map(&:id)` (applied_coupon_service.rb:113-118), which includes the override plan because it is a child of the plan the coupon names. The preview does not: Coupons::PreviewService#plan_related_fees is `if applied_coupon.coupon.plans.map(&:id).include?(invoice.subscriptions[0].plan_id) then invoice.fees else Fee.none end` (preview_service.rb:87-93) — an exact plan_id membership test with no `children`. After the 10 April override the subscription's plan_id is the clone's, the test is false, `fees` is empty and `next if fees.none?` skips the coupon entirely. No credit is built, so coupons_amount_cents stays 0 and the previewed total is the gross 15_000¢. A PREVIEW THAT DISAGREES WITH THE INVOICE IT FORECASTS IS THE BUG WORTH CATCHING, and 2_000¢ is the whole of the disagreement: fees are 15_000¢ on both sides, so nothing else moved. This is also the direction that hurts — the quote is HIGHER than the bill, so it does not merely mislead, it argues the customer out of a discount they have. THE CONTROL IS MARCH, before the override: the coupon's plan is the subscription's plan, the exact match holds, and preview and invoice would agree at 13_000¢. Both April invoices are asserted at 2_000¢ discounted so the row fails if the coupon was simply exhausted rather than unmatched.

A refresh AFTER the override, and the row is built so that the refresh provably happened — which the /draft sibling cannot show. The override on 2 May carries `amount_cents: 9000` as well as a name, so the clone's subscription fee is 9_000¢ rather than the original 5_000¢. The April draft was built on 1 May at the old price (5_000 + 10_000 = 15_000¢); the refresh on the 3rd rebuilds it from `subscription.plan` — now the clone — and it comes back at 9_000 + 10_000 = 19_000¢. Without that price change a refreshed draft and an unrefreshed one would read the same number and the cell would assert nothing about the surface. The coupon stays at 0 for the reason it does on any draft: `should_create_coupon_credit?` returns false while the invoice is not finalizing (calculate_fees_service.rb:367-373), and RefreshDraftService calls CalculateFeesService with `context: :refresh`, so the refreshed draft is still a draft. So a refresh does not consult the plan-limited coupon join at all — a plan-limited coupon can neither be lost nor kept here, and 0 is the only value this surface has. THE POSITIVE EVIDENCE IS MARCH, finalized in this same row at 15_000¢ with 2_000¢ discounted: the coupon is applied, limited to the parent plan, and live (frequency_duration 6). And the per-fee assertion is what makes the 19_000¢ readable — 9_000¢ of subscription fee is the override, 10_000¢ of charge is the unchanged 1.00 price, and neither number can be reached without the refresh having re-read the clone. When the invoice finalizes on 6 May the coupon returns: RefreshDraftAndFinalizeService runs the same service with `context: :finalize`, the gate opens, and the 2_000¢ is taken off the 19_000¢. The draft understates the discount; it does not lose it.

The same 20_000¢ delta with the April invoice held open, and the row that makes the /regenerated sibling a defect rather than a setup artefact. Identical to b20/plan-override/paid_advance_fee/invoice except for a 5-day grace period declared in `setup`, which is legitimate here (unlike the progressive-billing rows) because there is no earlier invoice to protect: the 1 April invoice is the first thing that happens. THE PLAN PAYING IN ADVANCE IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT DECORATION. Only Invoices::SubscriptionService consults `grace_period?` (subscription_service.rb:177,193), and it is the service that raises the subscription-start invoice for an ADVANCE plan. With an arrears plan whose only content is an advance fixed charge, the first invoice comes from a path that finalizes on creation and there is no draft to hold — three attempts at lead 2 died there, which is why it is written down in reference/invoice-paths.md. So the draft carries a 0¢ subscription fee and the 100_000¢ fixed-charge fee for its 10 units, fees_count 2, and the delta invoice adds 20_000¢: April is owed 120_000¢ across the two. The delta is still 20_000¢ and not 120_000¢ because `find_already_paid_units` has no invoice-status filter (build_pay_in_advance_fixed_charge_service.rb:63-83) — a DRAFT fee counts as already paid, which is correct here and is itself worth pinning. THIS IS THE CONTROL. Everything that could disturb the draft has happened — the plan was cloned, the fixed charge was replaced by a child, the delta invoice was issued — and the draft is intact. So when b20/plan-override/paid_advance_fee/regenerated finds it empty, the fee is not missing because the clone removed it, nor because the delta invoice claimed it at creation time. It is missing only after a refresh.

THE CONTROL for lead 2's join, on the churn that rewrites the fixed charge's id rather than its event stream — and it passes, because ONE of the two lookups was given a parent fallback. The plan pays in advance and its fixed charge carries 10 units at 100.00, so 1 April raises a `subscription` invoice with a 0¢ subscription fee and a 100_000¢ fixed-charge fee against the PLAN's fixed charge. (Lead 2's shape put the 10 units on a creation-time override instead; here they are on the plan, which is what makes the next step create a child rather than update one.) On 16 April the units are raised to 12 with `properties` sent as well. That extra key is the whole churn: `units_only_fixed_charge_params?` is false (fixed_charge_units_override_detection_concern.rb:26-31), so Subscriptions::UpdateOrOverrideFixedChargeService takes `override_via_plan`, Plans::OverrideService clones the plan, and FixedCharges::OverrideService dups the fixed charge with `c.parent_id = fixed_charge.id` (override_service.rb:30). The subscription now bills through a fixed charge that has never been invoiced for anything. `apply_units_immediately` then fires Invoices::CreatePayInAdvanceFixedChargesJob, and Fees::BuildPayInAdvanceFixedChargeService prices the DELTA: `find_already_paid_units` scopes on `fixed_charge: [fixed_charge, fixed_charge.parent]` and on the period's fixed_charges_from/to (:63-83), so it reaches the 1 April fee through the clone's parent and reports 10 already-paid units. delta = 12 − 10 = 2, priced at 2 x 100.00 = 20_000¢. THE NUMBER IF THE PARENT FALLBACK WERE MISSING IS 120_000¢ — twelve units re-tiered from zero, on top of the 100_000¢ already invoiced, for a total April of 220_000¢ on a period worth 120_000¢. That is not speculation about the code: it is what the sibling lookup in Fees::FixedChargeService does without a parent, and it is F32's mechanism (`delta_units` handed to the charge model as if it were a fresh subscription). Both invoices are asserted with their per-fee units because the delta is only meaningful against what was already paid: without index 0's 10 units at 100_000¢ there is nothing for `find_already_paid_units` to find, and a 20_000¢ delta over an empty period would be just as consistent with a setup that never billed the fixed charge at all.

The fourth surface of the cell b20/plan-override/paid_advance_fee/{invoice,draft,regenerated} cover, and the one that was left blank because two things had to be read out of the preview code first. Both are now in the comment above this row. APRIL, invoiced. The plan pays in advance and its fixed charge carries 10 units at 100.00, so 1 April raises a `subscription` invoice at 100_000¢. Raising the units to 12 on the 16th WITH `properties` makes `units_only_fixed_charge_params?` false (fixed_charge_units_override_detection_concern.rb:26-31), so the plan is cloned and the fixed charge is duped with `parent_id` set (fixed_charges/override_service.rb:30); `apply_units_immediately` then prices the delta through `find_already_paid_units`, which scopes on `fixed_charge: [fixed_charge, fixed_charge.parent]` and on the period's boundaries (build_pay_in_advance_fixed_charge_service.rb:63-83), reaches the 1 April fee through the parent and bills 12 - 10 = 2 units = 20_000¢. Both invoices are asserted because they are the positive evidence that the already-paid state exists and was found: without index 0's 10 units there is nothing for the delta to be a delta of. THE PREVIEW IS A FORECAST OF MAY, NOT A RE-READ OF APRIL. Taken on 20 April on a persisted subscription, `billing_time` is `end_of_periods.first + 1.day` = 1 May, and Subscriptions::DatesService for a pay-in-advance plan at that instant gives the 1-31 May period. `should_create_fixed_charge_fee?` admits an advance fixed charge on a live subscription (preview_service.rb:452-458), so Fees::FixedChargeService prices May from the CLONE's current units: 12 x 100.00 = 120_000¢, plus the plan's own 0¢ subscription fee. THE NUMBER THE DELTA ARITHMETIC WOULD HAVE PRODUCED IS 20_000¢, and it is the wrong answer to a different question. `already_billed?` (fixed_charge_service.rb:53-75) matches only fees carrying THIS period's `fixed_charges_from_datetime`/`_to_datetime`; the 100_000¢ and 20_000¢ fees are both stamped 1-30 April, so May finds nothing and quotes its 12 seats in full. That is correct — May is a period nothing has been paid for — and it is why this row is NOT marked characterization while its /regenerated sibling, which loses 100_000¢ of April to the same family of lookups, is. 120_000 vs 20_000 is the whole content of the row: a reader who assumed the preview reuses the already-paid delta would expect the smaller number, and the two differ by the entire fixed charge.

CHARACTERIZATION — BIL-537 reproduced through a second churn, which is what says the bug is the lookup and not the units-only override path the ticket happened to arrive on. Lead 2 reached this by raising units on a subscription whose plan was ALREADY an override, so the child fixed charge was updated in place and only its event stream moved. Here the plan carries the 10 units, so sending `properties` alongside them clones the plan and creates a CHILD fixed charge with a fresh id (FixedCharges::OverrideService:30). Different churn, different column rewritten, same outcome. The refresh is where the two lookups disagree. Fees::FixedChargeService#already_billed? (fixed_charge_service.rb:53-75) asks whether this fixed charge has a fee for this period on any invoice that is not voided or deleted — scoped to `fixed_charge.fees`, WITH NO `fixed_charge.parent` fallback, unlike find_already_paid_units. After the clone, `subscription.fixed_charges` is the child, and the child does have such a fee: the 2-unit delta fee on the 16 April invoice, whose fixed_charges_from/to are the same 1–30 April. So `already_billed?` returns true, Fees::FixedChargeService returns before building anything, and the refreshed draft keeps nothing but its 0¢ subscription fee. CORRECT BEHAVIOUR IS THE 100_000¢ THE DRAFT WAS BUILT WITH, which its control row b20/plan-override/paid_advance_fee/draft asserts unchanged under an identical timeline minus the refresh. April is invoiced 20_000¢ on a period owing 120_000¢ — 100_000¢ of cash, deleted by a refresh, with no error anywhere. fees_count 1 is asserted with the amount because a fee that came back at 0¢ and a fee that never came back are different bugs, and only the count separates them.

REPORTED BUG, REPRODUCED — CHARACTERIZATION, and this is the surface where it costs money. Identical to b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/invoice except for a 5-day grace period, so the period invoice is a DRAFT. The override has already turned the 10_000¢ progressive credit into a credit note, exactly as it does there. But a draft withholds credit notes — `should_create_credit_note_credit?` returns false unless the invoice is finalizing (calculate_fees_service.rb:364) — so nothing offsets the fees. The draft reads 10_000¢ due on top of the 10_000¢ already collected: the customer is shown, and on finalization charged, twice for the same usage. Two rows, one cause, and only the pairing shows the severity. On a finalized invoice the diverted credit note is spent on the spot and the total is accidentally right; hold the same invoice open for a grace period and the money is simply gone. Any fix should make the progressive credit follow the override — matching on the override's parent charge rather than on charge_id alone — at which point both rows change and the credit note stops being created at all.

REPORTED BUG, REPRODUCED — CHARACTERIZATION. An override silently converts a progressive-billing CREDIT into a CREDIT NOTE. 100 units cross the 5_000¢ threshold on 5 March and 10_000¢ is collected. The subscription is then updated with `plan_overrides` — here only a name, deliberately, because the override itself is the cause and no price change is needed. `Subscriptions::UpdateService` takes the `handle_plan_override` branch (update_service.rb:84-85) and repoints the subscription at a NEW plan whose charges are fresh records with fresh ids. (A units-only override takes a different branch, :82-83, and does not create a plan — which is why that variant does not reproduce this.) The period invoice then bills the same 100 units at the same 1.00 = 10_000¢ and tries to credit what was collected. ProgressiveBillingService caps the credit at `invoice.fees.charge.where(charge_id: progressive_billing_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id))`. Across the override boundary that join matches NOTHING, so the cap is 0 — and because `amount_to_credit > total_charges_amount`, the whole 10_000¢ is diverted into CreditNotes::CreateFromProgressiveBillingInvoice and `amount_to_credit` is set to 0. Hence the row: progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 0, and a 10_000¢ credit note which the invoice then spends on itself at stage :62, landing on a 0¢ total. THE TOTAL BEING RIGHT IS A COINCIDENCE OF THIS SURFACE. A credit note is a numbered, customer-facing, refundable document that should not exist here; it can be spent on a DIFFERENT invoice, leaving this one unpaid; and it is recognised differently in reporting. The sibling row b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/draft shows what happens when the credit note cannot be spent on the invoice that created it — the customer is billed twice.

CHARACTERIZATION. The surface on which the diverted credit cannot be disguised: the preview quotes the whole period again. The setup is lead 1's, with a preview taken on 25 March — after the 10 March override and before the period closes. Invoices::PreviewService keeps its OWN copy of the cap. It reuses the read-only Subscriptions::ProgressiveBilledAmount (which is subscription-scoped and still finds the threshold invoice), then filters the fees it may credit with `billed_charge_ids = progressive_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id)` and `next 0 unless billed_charge_ids.include?(fee.charge_id)` (preview_service.rb:346-352). The previewed fee comes from the OVERRIDE plan's charge, so the include? is false, `creditable_amount_cents` is 0, `amount_cents = [10_000, 0].min` is 0 and the guard `next unless amount_cents.positive?` drops the credit entirely. And a preview may not issue a credit note — the comment at :344-345 says the excess is simply dropped — so there is no second spelling of the money to make the total look right. The quote is 10_000¢ for a period on which 10_000¢ has already been collected: exactly the overstatement the comment at :324-329 says this code exists to prevent. THE INVOICE IS ASSERTED BESIDE IT AND DISAGREES: 10_000¢ of fees, credit 0, a 10_000¢ credit note, total 0. Same lost join, two different disguises — the invoice hides it in a credit note and settles at zero, the preview hides nothing and doubles the bill. That contrast is why `observed_via` is an axis of this block, and it is the reason a row asserting only the finalized total would have reported this cell as healthy. THE CONTROL NUMBER IS A 10_000¢ CREDIT AND A ZERO TOTAL ON BOTH SIDES, which is what b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/preview asserts with the same shape and the same preview code.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the version of lead 1 in which the loss is caused by the refresh and can be watched happening. The order is deliberately the opposite of the /invoice and /draft rows. The threshold invoice takes 10_000¢ on 5 March; the grace period is raised on the 6th (after it, because Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 issues drafts when a period is shortened); the March period invoice is drafted on 1 April WHILE THE PLAN IS STILL THE ORIGINAL, so its charge fee carries the same charge_id as the threshold fee, the cap at progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33 matches, 10_000¢ is credited and the draft sits at 0¢. The override lands on 2 April; the draft is refreshed on the 3rd. RefreshDraftService then does three things in sequence that together lose the money: `reset_invoice_values` destroys `invoice.credits.progressive_billing_invoice_kind` and zeroes progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents; CalculateFeesService rebuilds the charge fee from `subscription.plan.charges`, which is now the CLONE's charge with a fresh id; and ProgressiveBillingService re-runs, finds `total_charges_amount` 0 because the fee it just built no longer matches the threshold fee's charge_id, and — `amount_to_credit` being 10_000 and the threshold invoice's `to_credit_amount` being back to the full 10_000 now that the credit which had netted it down is destroyed — diverts the entire amount into CreditNotes::CreateFromProgressiveBillingInvoice and sets `amount_to_credit` to 0. THE DRAFT GOES FROM 0¢ TO 10_000¢ AND A 10_000¢ CREDIT NOTE APPEARS, which the draft may not spend (`should_create_credit_note_credit?` is false while not finalizing, calculate_fees_service.rb:364). The customer has paid 10_000¢ and is shown 10_000¢ more. THE CONTROL IS b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/regenerated: identical shape, identical refresh, charge_id rewritten by an upgrade instead — and there the draft comes back at 0. So the refresh is not the cause; the refresh is only when the rewritten id is first consulted. The credit note is asserted with `select: {index: -1}` because without a selector expect.credit_note reads the payload captured at CREATION by this row's own create_credit_note step — of which there is none — and because its 10_000¢ balance is the positive evidence that the threshold money existed and was diverted rather than never collected.

The prorated floor is visible on a draft, which is the useful fact about this surface: a commitment true-up is a fee PRODUCER (calculate_fees_service.rb:46), created above the `not_in_finalizing_process?` gate at :364-379, so unlike a coupon it is not withheld and a grace-period draft shows the customer the real number. Same arithmetic as b20/plan-upgrade/commitment_progress/invoice: March finalizes at 30_000¢ before the grace period is raised on 2 April (raising rather than shortening, because Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 issues existing drafts when a period is shortened); the 16 April upgrade's termination invoice is held open and reads 3_000¢ of usage plus a 13_000¢ true-up against a floor prorated to 30_000 x 16/30 = 16_000¢. coupons_amount_cents and credit_notes_amount_cents are asserted at 0 so the 16_000¢ cannot be read as a net figure: nothing has been taken off, and the draft is producers plus tax as always. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 3_000¢ — a draft with two fees and no true-up, which is what this surface would show if the commitment had been looked up through the NEW subscription's plan rather than the terminated one's. That is not a hypothetical shape either: it is exactly what plan B's own first period reads in the /invoice sibling. The timeline stops at the termination invoice, so `invoices: 2` also pins that the upgrade raised no invoice of its own for plan B — an arrears plan at amount_cents 0 bills nothing at subscription start, and a third invoice here would mean something else happened.

An upgrade does not lose the commitment — it PRORATES it and then leaves it behind, and the two halves of that sentence are the two invoices in the middle and at the end. March (index 0) is the whole-period control: 30 units x 1.00 = 3_000¢ against a 30_000¢ floor, so Commitments::Minimum::InArrears::CalculateTrueUpFeeService raises 27_000¢ (`commitment_amount_cents - fees_total_amount_cents`, calculate_true_up_fee_service.rb:37-41) and the invoice reads 30_000¢. The coefficient is 1 because the period is whole. The 16 April termination invoice (index 1) prorates the FLOOR, not just the usage. Commitments::CalculateAmountService multiplies the commitment by Commitments::CalculateProratedCoefficientService's days/days_total, and both are computed with `Utils::Datetime.date_diff_with_timezone`, which is `(to - from).fdiv(1.day).ceil` (utils/datetime.rb:55-69):
  days       = ceil((2024-04-16 10:00 − 2024-04-01 00:00) / 1d) = ceil(15.42) = 16
  days_total = ceil((2024-04-30 23:59:59 − 2024-04-01 00:00) / 1d) = ceil(29.99) = 30
30_000 x 16/30 = 16_000¢, and the usage inside the terminated period is 30 units x 1.00 = 3_000¢, so the true-up is 13_000¢ and the invoice reads 16_000¢. Note WHICH date service produces those bounds, because it is not the obvious one: Subscriptions::TerminatedDatesService returns its input unchanged when `subscription.next_subscription.present?` (terminated_dates_service.rb:12), and on an upgrade the next subscription is exactly what was just created. So the bounds are the CURRENT period's (1–30 April, `current_usage: true` for a terminated non-downgraded arrears subscription), not the terminated stub's. Had they been the terminated bounds, days_total would also be 16, the coefficient 1, and this invoice would read 30_000¢ with a 27_000¢ true-up. Plan B's own first period (index 2, 16–30 April) has NO floor at all: 40 units x 2.00 = 8_000¢, two fees, no commitment fee. Every lookup in the calculator is scoped by `subscription_id` (calculate_true_up_fee_service.rb, in_arrears/*), but it never runs, because the commitment is reached only through `subscription.plan.minimum_commitment` and B has none. THE THREE NUMBERS ARE 30_000 / 16_000 / 8_000 and each has a named counterfactual: 30_000¢ on index 1 if the proration used the terminated bounds, 3_000¢ if the commitment were looked up through the new subscription's plan, and 10_000¢ on index 2 if a floor of 30_000 x 14/30 followed the upgrade. fees_count is asserted throughout because the per-fee split is the only thing that says whether a total is usage or a true-up.

What the customer is quoted for life after the upgrade: 8_000¢, with no floor. Invoices::PreviewService reaches the commitment through the same single reference the invoice does — `add_commitment_fee` opens with `return unless subscription.plan.minimum_commitment` (preview_service.rb:259-260) — and after the 16 April upgrade the subscription's plan is B, which has none. So the previewed 16–30 April invoice is 40 units x 2.00 = 8_000¢ and nothing else, and the 1 May invoice confirms it at 8_000¢. fees_count differs between the two by design and the row asserts both: the preview builds ONE fee (the charge) because Invoices::PreviewService adds a subscription fee only where the plan has an amount, while the real invoice persists a 0¢ subscription fee alongside the charge — a shape difference that is worth pinning precisely because it is the kind of thing a reader would otherwise read as a missing commitment. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 16_000¢ ON BOTH SIDES: had the floor followed the upgrade, plan B's partial period would be topped up to 30_000 x 15/30. March, asserted here at 30_000¢ with its three fees, is what proves the commitment was configured and producing a true-up before the churn — without it an 8_000¢ preview is indistinguishable from a plan that never had a floor. The previewed period has usage on purpose (40 units on the 20th, previewed on the 25th): Invoices::PreviewService raises a 500 on a charge with no usage in the period.

A refresh that provably ran, and a total that provably did not move — which is the whole content of this cell. The termination draft is built on 16 April from the 30 units then known: 3_000¢ of usage and a 13_000¢ true-up against the 16_000¢ prorated floor. A BACKDATED event is then ingested on the 17th carrying `timestamp: 2024-04-10`, inside the terminated period, and the draft is refreshed. RefreshDraftService destroys the fees and re-runs CalculateFeesService, so the period now aggregates 40 units: the charge fee becomes 4_000¢ and the true-up is RE-DERIVED as 16_000 − 4_000 = 12_000¢. fees_amount_cents stays 16_000¢. That invariance is the assertion, and it is only readable through the per-fee split — 3_000/13_000 before the refresh, 4_000/12_000 after, 16_000 both times. A refresh that failed to re-derive the true-up would read 17_000¢ (4_000 of usage on top of a stale 13_000 true-up); one that dropped the commitment as an override does would read 4_000¢; and one that never picked up the late event would read 3_000/13_000. Three distinguishable wrong answers, all excluded. It also pins that the prorated coefficient survives the refresh. The coefficient is recomputed from `all_invoice_subscriptions.first.from_datetime` and `min(terminated_at, end_of_period)` (calculate_prorated_coefficient_service.rb), against invoice_subscriptions that RefreshDraftService destroys and rebuilds — so 16/30 has to come out the same the second time, and a floor that came back at 30_000¢ (coefficient 1) would show as a 26_000¢ true-up. March is asserted as the positive evidence that the commitment exists and produces a true-up on this subscription at all.

A DRAFT CANNOT ANSWER THIS CELL, and the row is built so that the reason is unambiguous rather than merely absent. The grace period is raised on 17 April, AFTER the upgrade's termination invoice has finalized. So both plan-A invoices (March and the termination) are finalized WITH their 2_000¢ discount, and only plan B's first period is held open. That ordering is what this row buys over its /invoice sibling: a plan-limited coupon is shown working twice, and then not working, on three invoices of one subscription lifetime. Plan B's draft reads 8_000¢ with no discount, and there are now two sufficient explanations — the coupon is gated on a draft (`should_create_coupon_credit?` is false while `not_in_finalizing_process?`, calculate_fees_service.rb:367-373) and the plan join misses B — so this surface CANNOT distinguish them. The row says so rather than claiming the churn was observed: the cell's real answer is in b20/plan-upgrade/coupon_application/invoice, where the same period finalizes at 8_000¢ and proves the 0 was not the gate. What the row does assert on its own account: credit_notes_amount_cents and prepaid_credit_amount_cents are 0, so no other gated reducer is standing in; and sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents equals fees_amount_cents, so nothing at all has been taken off. A draft here is fees and nothing else.

THE POINT AT WHICH THE OVERRIDE-AWARE JOIN STOPS BEING ENOUGH, in three invoices that share one coupon. March (index 0) is the control: 30 units x 1.00 = 3_000¢ on plan A, and the coupon — limited to `plan_codes: [golden_b20_w1_cui_a]` — takes 2_000¢ off. Total 1_000¢. The 16 April upgrade terminates A and bills it in arrears (index 1). The fees on that invoice belong to a subscription whose plan is still A, so Credits::AppliedCouponService#plan_related_fees matches through `parent_and_overriden_plans` (which contains A itself) and the coupon lands again: 30 units x 1.00 = 3_000¢ less 2_000¢ = 1_000¢. That second application is the second piece of positive evidence — the coupon is not merely configured, it is being spent, right up to the churn. Plan B's own first period (index 2, 16–30 April) is where the join fails: 40 units x 2.00 = 8_000¢ and NO discount. `parent_and_overriden_plans` is `plans + plans.map(&:children)` (coupon.rb:91-93); B is neither A nor a child of A — Subscriptions::PlanUpgradeService builds a fresh Subscription pointing at B with `previous_subscription_id` set (plan_upgrade_service.rb:52-72), and nothing in that lineage makes B a child of A — so `plan_related_fees` returns an empty relation, `return result unless fees.any?` fires, and no Credit is built. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 6_000¢. `frequency_duration: 6` is deliberately generous: the coupon has been applied twice and has four periods left, so coupons_amount_cents 0 on index 2 can only mean the plan join missed and never that the coupon was exhausted. That distinction is the whole reason the duration is asserted-by-construction rather than left at the default. Whether this is a DEFECT depends on what a plan-limited coupon is for, and the row does not pretend to settle it — a coupon naming plan A arguably should stop when the customer leaves A. What it does settle is that an upgrade silently ends a live discount with no event, no webhook and no trace on any invoice, which is the class of thing this block exists to make visible.

The one direction in which the preview's exact plan_id test is RIGHT, and it agrees with the invoice for the wrong reason. Preview and invoice reach the coupon by different code — Coupons::PreviewService#plan_related_fees is `coupon.plans.map(&:id).include?(invoice.subscriptions[0].plan_id)` (preview_service.rb:87-93) while the invoice uses `parent_and_overriden_plans` (applied_coupon_service.rb:113-118) — and across an UPGRADE the two tests happen to give the same answer: B is not A, and B is not a child of A either, so both refuse the coupon. Preview quotes 8_000¢ and the 1 May invoice bills 8_000¢. That agreement is worth a cell precisely because the same pair DISAGREES across an override: b20/plan-override/coupon_application/preview quotes 15_000¢ against a 13_000¢ invoice. So this row is the control that locates the preview defect — it is not "preview ignores plan-limited coupons", it is "preview's plan test has no `children`", and only a churn that produces a child distinguishes the two statements. THE COUNTERFACTUAL ON BOTH SIDES IS 6_000¢, and March is asserted at 1_000¢ to prove the coupon was live and limited to A rather than exhausted. The previewed period deliberately has usage (40 units on 20 April, previewed on the 25th): Invoices::PreviewService dies with a 500 on a charge that has no usage in the period, so a zero-usage preview would fail this row for an unrelated reason.

A refresh that provably ran, so the cell is about the surface and not about the number happening to match. Plan B's 16–30 April draft is built on 1 May from the 40 units ingested on the 20th: 40 x 2.00 = 8_000¢. A BACKDATED event is then ingested on 2 May carrying `timestamp: 2024-04-25` — inside the period the draft covers — and the draft is refreshed. RefreshDraftService destroys the fees and re-aggregates the period, which now holds 50 units, so the draft comes back at 10_000¢ with a single charge fee of 50 units. 8_000¢ against 10_000¢ is what says the refresh happened; without the late event a refreshed and an unrefreshed draft would read the same and the row would assert nothing about `regenerated`. The coupon stays at 0 across the refresh, and for a structural reason worth stating: a refresh does not open the coupon gate. RefreshDraftService calls CalculateFeesService with `context: :refresh`, `not_in_finalizing_process?` is still true, and `should_create_coupon_credit?` still returns false (calculate_fees_service.rb:367-373). So no amount of refreshing can make this surface consult the plan join at all — which is the honest answer for this cell, and different from "the join was consulted and missed". THE POSITIVE EVIDENCE IS MARCH, asserted in this row: 3_000¢ of plan-A usage with 2_000¢ discounted. The coupon exists, is limited to plan A, and had four periods left when the upgrade happened. Its absence from plan B's draft is therefore about identity, not about supply — and b20/plan-upgrade/coupon_application/invoice is where that is shown on a finalized invoice.

The control from the /invoice row with a 5-day grace period, and the row that says WHICH of the upgrade's five invoices a grace period can still reach. Not the advance ones. Invoices::CreatePayInAdvanceChargeService calls Invoices::TransitionToFinalStatusService directly (:46) and never consults `grace_period?` — only Invoices::SubscriptionService does (subscription_service.rb:177,193) — so index 0 (10_000¢) and index 3 (5_000¢) are both asserted `finalized`. The 5_000¢ that the upgrade's new period correctly starts charging from zero is taken the moment the event lands, five days inside a grace period that has no bearing on it. What the grace period does hold is index 4, plan B's 12-31 March period invoice, at 0¢ with a single 0¢ subscription fee — `create_charges_fees` skips the in-advance charge on a non-recurring metric (calculate_fees_service.rb:130-132), so the open invoice carries nothing from the advance path and cannot reconcile it. THE TWO READINGS OF THE COLUMN ARE STILL 5_000¢ AND 0¢ ON INDEX 3 — the fee a lost cache prices from zero versus the 0¢ a carried one would produce — and here 5_000¢ is the CORRECT one, because the upgrade moved the period boundary as well as the charge id. `fees_count: 1` on index 4 is what says the draft did not quietly acquire a second reading of the same usage.

THE CONTROL for the `paid_advance_fee` column, on the churn that rewrites charge_id by changing plans rather than by swapping a record underneath one — and the reset it causes is CORRECT. The state is the same one b20/charge-replaced/paid_advance_fee/invoice loses: the CachedAggregation row that records how much of the period's peak has been paid for, found by `charge_id` together with `external_subscription_id` and the period's from/to datetimes (aggregations/base_service.rb:230-243). 100 units on 5 March bill 10_000¢ and write `current 100, max 100`; -60 on the 8th bills 0¢ and rewrites it to `current 40, max 100`, which is the state a lost join throws away. The upgrade on 12 March terminates the plan-A subscription and starts a plan-B one. Plan B's charge is a different record, so charge_id is rewritten exactly as a replacement rewrites it — BUT THE PERIOD IS REWRITTEN WITH IT. The new subscription's boundaries start on 12 March, so the 50 units on the 18th are aggregated over 12-31 March, the earlier events fall outside that window, and the sum is 50 rather than 90. `find_cached_aggregation` would have missed on `from_datetime` even if the charge id had been carried across. So the 18 March fee is 50 x 1.00 - 0 = 50.00 -> 5_000¢ AND THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER: a new plan is a new period and a new peak, and the 100 units paid for under plan A do not entitle the customer to 100 free units under plan B. The counterfactual is 0¢ — what a carried cache would produce — and it would be a give-away, which is the opposite of the error the /charge-replaced row commits with the identical column rewritten. THIS ROW IS WHY THAT ONE IS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A DESIGN. Same state, same key, same rewrite, and here the loss is accounted for by a boundary change the customer can see; there the boundaries are untouched and nothing accounts for it. The final `subscription`-type invoice is asserted at 0¢ to say the plan-B period does not re-bill the advance fees, and `credit_note: null` is not written — the row asserts no credit note by asserting the amounts that a credit note would move.

The last surface of the control column, and it is the same structural blindness the other two `paid_advance_fee` preview rows pin — reached here through an upgrade instead of a churn that breaks something. The preview is taken on 25 March, thirteen days after the upgrade, as a projection of plan B's current period (`billing_time` = `end_of_periods.first + 1.day`, preview_service.rb:141-151). `add_charge_fees` filters with the same two clauses CalculateFeesService uses — `.where(invoiceable: true)` and `.where.not(pay_in_advance: true, billable_metric: {recurring: false})` (preview_service.rb:184-192) — so plan B's only charge is excluded and the quote is the plan's 0¢ subscription fee alone. `fees_count: 1` IS THE LOAD-BEARING ASSERTION HERE, because every amount on this preview is 0 and a preview that had returned nothing at all would read the same. One fee at 0¢ says the projection ran and produced the subscription fee; it is the charge that is missing, not the answer. THE PREVIEWED NUMBERS ARE 0 WHETHER THE CACHE WAS CARRIED OR RESET, so this surface cannot observe its own cell — the same finding as b20/charge-replaced/paid_advance_fee/preview and b20/metric-deleted/paid_advance_fee/preview, and worth stating three times because in this column a healthy-looking preview means nothing at all. The discriminating assertions are the invoices: index 0 at 10_000¢ is the evidence the cache existed, and index 3 at 5_000¢ with 50 units is the post-upgrade fee that a carried cache would have priced at 0¢ — correctly 5_000¢ here, because the upgrade moved the period boundary with the charge id.

The /draft row plus a refresh of plan B's open period invoice on 2 April, and the answer is that the refresh consults none of it. Invoices::RefreshDraftService rebuilds the draft from current configuration, and the configuration still says plan B's only charge pays in advance on a non-recurring metric — excluded by `create_charges_fees` (calculate_fees_service.rb:130-132) — so the draft comes back with the same single 0¢ subscription fee. `fees_count: 1` and `fees_amount_cents: 0` are the assertions: nothing was added, and no charge fee for the 50 units already billed in advance appeared. THAT IS THE CONTROL RESULT THIS SURFACE EXISTS FOR. On the fixed-charge side of the same cell a refresh is destructive — b20/plan-override/paid_advance_fee/regenerated and BIL-537 itself both show one DELETING a 100_000¢ fee it decides is already paid, because Fees::FixedChargeService#already_billed? (fixed_charge_service.rb:53-75) goes looking for one. On the metric-charge side there is no equivalent lookup in the refresh path at all: the advance fees live on their own finalized invoices, the refresh never reads CachedAggregation, and index 3 stays at 5_000¢ before and after. THE TWO READINGS REMAIN 5_000¢ AND 0¢ ON INDEX 3, still with 5_000¢ correct because the upgrade moved the period. What this row adds over /draft is that a recomputation is not a second chance: whatever the advance path charged is final, right or wrong, and the two rows in this column that are marked characterization — /charge-replaced and /metric-deleted — are wrong for good.

The surface on which lead 1's override loses money, applied to the upgrade — and here it does not, which is what makes the pair a diagnosis rather than a symptom. Identical to b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/invoice except that the grace period is raised to 5 days on 6 April, AFTER the threshold invoice is finalized. That ordering is deliberate: Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 finalizes every existing draft when the period is SHORTENED, so a grace period declared in `setup` would have put the threshold invoice itself at risk, and raising it later leaves the threshold invoice finalized at 10_000¢ while the 16 April termination invoice is held open. Progressive billing is the one reducer a draft still applies — it runs at calculate_fees_service.rb:53, ahead of the `not_in_finalizing_process?` gate at :364-379 that withholds coupons, credit notes and prepaid credit. So the credit of 10_000¢ appears on the draft and the draft settles at 0. THIS IS THE EXACT LINE THE OVERRIDE FALLS OVER. There the credit is diverted into a credit note, and a credit note IS behind the gate: b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/draft reads 10_000¢ due on top of the 10_000¢ already collected. Here nothing is diverted, so there is nothing for the gate to withhold. The three zero assertions (coupons, credit notes, prepaid) are what distinguishes "credited" from "diverted then withheld" — without them a draft reading 0 could mean either, and only one of the two is correct.

THE CONTROL for lead 1's plan-upgrade sibling, and it passes: an upgrade rewrites plan_id and charge_id exactly as an override does, and the credit is NOT lost — because the churn closes the period it belonged to before anything has to be joined across it. 100 units cross 5_000¢ on 5 April and 10_000¢ is collected. The upgrade on 16 April terminates plan A and bills it in arrears for the same 100 units at A's own 1.00 = 10_000¢ (plan B prices the metric at 2.00 deliberately, so re-pricing A's usage at B's rate would read 20_000¢ and this row would fail loudly instead of quietly). Both halves of the join then still match. Subscriptions::ProgressiveBilledAmount scopes on `.where(subscription: subscription)` (progressive_billed_amount.rb:39) and the termination invoice belongs to the OLD subscription record, which is the one the threshold invoice was raised against; and ProgressiveBillingService's cap, `invoice.fees.charge.where(charge_id: progressive_billing_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id))` (progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33), reads A's charge on both sides because the new subscription's B charges are on a DIFFERENT invoice that this period never produces. So `amount_to_credit` 10_000 is not greater than `total_charges_amount` 10_000, no credit note is minted, and the 10_000¢ is credited as a credit: sub_total 0, total 0. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS THE OVERRIDE ROW. Had the join missed — as it does in b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/invoice — `total_charges_amount` would be 0, the whole 10_000¢ would be diverted into a credit note and this invoice would read progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 0 / credit_notes_amount_cents 10_000. Both spellings land on total 0, which is precisely why the credit and credit-note fields are asserted here rather than the total alone: the total cannot tell them apart, and `credit_notes_amount_cents: 0` is the assertion that says no customer-facing refundable document was created. The threshold invoice is asserted alongside so the row fails if the 10_000¢ was never collected — a setup that produced no state to lose would otherwise satisfy every line above.

What the customer is QUOTED for the plan change, next to what they are billed — the fourth surface, and a fourth implementation of the same join. An upgrade is previewed as the termination it performs: passing `subscriptions.terminated_at` puts Preview::SubscriptionsService in its `termination` context, which is the invoice the upgrade on 16 April actually raises for plan A. The preview is taken on the 15th, before the change, so it is a genuine forecast rather than a re-read. Invoices::PreviewService REIMPLEMENTS the credit rather than sharing it (preview_service.rb:330-358): it reuses the read-only Subscriptions::ProgressiveBilledAmount, then applies its own copy of the cap — `billed_charge_ids = progressive_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id)` and `next 0 unless billed_charge_ids.include?(fee.charge_id)` (:346-352). SAME COLUMN, SECOND IMPLEMENTATION, so the preview is exposed to exactly the churn the invoice is. Across the upgrade both agree: 10_000¢ of fees, 10_000¢ credited, total 0. THE NUMBER THAT WOULD APPEAR IF THE JOIN MISSED IS 10_000¢, not 0 — the preview drops the excess rather than diverting it (`amount_cents = [to_credit_amount, creditable_amount_cents].min` with creditable 0, then `next unless amount_cents.positive?`), so it cannot issue the credit note that disguises the loss on a finalized invoice. That makes preview the surface on which a lost credit is most visible, and it is why the sibling b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/preview quotes the whole period again. Asserting the invoice in the same row is what proves the forecast was right rather than merely self-consistent, and the threshold invoice is what proves there was a credit to forecast at all.

A refresh is where a lost join stops being theoretical, because RefreshDraftService recomputes the credit from scratch: `reset_invoice_values` destroys `invoice.credits.progressive_billing_invoice_kind` (refresh_draft_service.rb) and zeroes progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents, then CalculateFeesService runs the whole pipeline again against the configuration as it stands NOW. For the upgrade that recomputation still succeeds. The termination invoice's fees are rebuilt for the same subscription record and the same plan-A charge, so Subscriptions::ProgressiveBilledAmount finds the threshold invoice again (`to_credit_amount` is back to the full 10_000¢ because the credit that had netted it down was just destroyed) and the charge_id cap matches again. The draft comes back at 0. THE SIBLING THIS PAIRS WITH IS b20/plan-override/progressive_billing_credit/regenerated, where the same refresh rebuilds the fees against the OVERRIDE plan's charges: there the cap misses, 10_000¢ is minted as a credit note the draft may not spend, and the draft goes from 0¢ to 10_000¢. The two rows differ in one step only — which churn happened — so the refresh is not the cause and the identity rewrite is. Asserting fees_amount_cents 10_000 with the credit is not decoration: a refresh that failed to rebuild the charge fee at all would also read total 0, and would do so with fees 0.

The control for BIL-537, and the row that makes the bug a bug. Identical to b20/subscription-override/paid_advance_fee/regenerated in every respect except that the draft is never refreshed. The units are still raised from 10 to 12 with immediate application, so the delta invoice is still issued — everything that could plausibly disturb the draft has happened. And the draft is intact: a 0¢ subscription fee and the 100_000¢ fixed-charge fee for its 10 units, 120_000¢ owed for April across the two invoices. So the fee is not missing because the override removed it, nor because the creation-time override never billed it, nor because the delta invoice claimed it. It is missing only after a refresh. That is the entire content of the pairing, and without this row the characterization could be explained away as a setup that never had the fee to begin with.

Lead 2's exact setup with the grace period removed, which is what the finalized surface of that cell means — and it is the row that shows the join WORKING before any refresh consults it. The plan's fixed charge carries 0 units, so the 10 arrive as a creation-time override (Subscriptions::CreateService#create_fixed_charge_units_overrides). With no grace period the 1 April `subscription` invoice finalizes immediately at 100_000¢: a 0¢ subscription fee and 10 units at 100.00. The subscription is therefore already on a CHILD plan, which decides what the next step does. Raising the units to 12 on 16 April with a units-only body would normally write a Subscription::FixedChargeUnitsOverride, but `units_only_change?` opens with `return false if subscription_plan_parent_present` (update_or_override_fixed_charge_service.rb:44-48) — the plan already has a parent, so it takes `override_via_plan` instead, `ensure_plan_override` returns the existing child plan unchanged (plan_override_concern.rb:8-10), and `find_or_create_fixed_charge_override` finds the child's own fixed charge and UPDATES it in place. So no id is rewritten here; what moves is the fixed charge's event stream, which is the other column `subscription-override` rewrites. The delta is then priced correctly: `find_already_paid_units` matches `fixed_charge: [fixed_charge, fixed_charge.parent]` on the same 1–30 April boundaries (build_pay_in_advance_fixed_charge_service.rb:63-83), finds the 10-unit fee on the very record it just updated, and bills 12 − 10 = 2 units at 100.00 = 20_000¢. April is owed 120_000¢ across two finalized invoices. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 120_000¢ ON THE SECOND INVOICE — twelve units re-tiered from zero, F32's mechanism — for an April of 220_000¢. AND THE PAIR THAT MATTERS IS WITH THE OTHER SURFACES OF THIS SAME CELL: the /draft row shows the same two invoices with the first held open, and the /regenerated row shows the refresh deleting the 100_000¢ fee. This row is what says the state was found correctly at every point before a refresh was asked for, so the 0¢ there is the refresh and nothing else.

The last surface of BIL-537's own cell, and it agrees with its plan-override twin — which is what says the previewed number depends on the PERIOD and not on which churn rewrote which column. Lead 2's setup exactly: the plan's fixed charge carries 0 units so the 10 arrive as a creation-time override (Subscriptions::CreateService#create_fixed_charge_units_overrides), 1 April finalizes at 100_000¢, and the 16 April units-only body takes `override_via_plan` anyway because `units_only_change?` opens with `return false if subscription_plan_parent_present` (update_or_override_fixed_charge_service.rb:44-48) — the plan already has a parent, so the child's own fixed charge is UPDATED IN PLACE. No id is rewritten; what moves is the fixed charge's event stream. `find_already_paid_units` finds the 10-unit fee on the very record it just updated and bills 12 - 10 = 2 = 20_000¢. THE PREVIEW ON 20 APRIL PROJECTS MAY, for the same reason as in the plan-override row: `billing_time` is `end_of_periods.first + 1.day` for a persisted subscription (preview_service.rb:141-151). May's fixed-charge fee is priced from the override's current 12 units at 12 x 100.00 = 120_000¢, and `already_billed?` (fixed_charge_service.rb:53-75) finds nothing to subtract because both April fees carry April's `fixed_charges_from_datetime`. THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS 20_000¢ — the delta number — and it is the answer a reader gets by assuming the preview reuses `find_already_paid_units`. It does not: that service is only reached from Invoices::CreatePayInAdvanceFixedChargesJob, never from PreviewService, so no already-paid state is consulted on this surface at all. THIS IS THE CELL WHERE ID CHURN IS AT ITS MOST DANGEROUS — the /regenerated sibling is BIL-537 itself, a refresh deleting the 100_000¢ fee — so it matters that the previewed 120_000¢ is asserted against the two April invoices in the same row: the quote is right, and it is right for a reason (a period nothing has paid for) rather than by accident.

BIL-537 — REPRODUCED. CHARACTERIZATION: the refresh deletes the fixed-charge fee. Correct behaviour is the 100_000¢ the draft was built with, which its control row b20/subscription-override/paid_advance_fee/draft asserts unchanged. Three details are load-bearing and none is obvious from the symptom. The PLAN pays in advance, so a subscription fee is raised at period start and the invoice is a `subscription` invoice — the kind Invoices::SubscriptionService raises, and therefore the kind that consults `grace_period?` (subscription_service.rb:177,193) and can be held open as a draft. With an arrears plan the first invoice comes from another path that is finalized on creation, and there is no draft to refresh at all. The plan's fixed charge carries 0 units, so the 10 arrive as a creation-time override (Subscriptions::CreateService#create_fixed_charge_units_overrides) rather than from the plan. The grace period is 5 days, which is what leaves the 1 April invoice open. So the draft holds a 0¢ subscription fee and a 100_000¢ fixed-charge fee for 10 units. Raising the units to 12 with `apply_units_immediately` then issues a separate invoice for the 2-unit delta, correct in itself and covered by b13/standard/advance/not-prorated/subscription-override. The question is what a REFRESH makes of the draft. Rebuilding its fees means deciding whether the period's fixed charge is already paid — a lookup that reaches the fee through the fixed-charge event stream rather than through the charge. The reported symptom is that it matches the delta fee, concludes the period is settled, and deletes the 10-unit fee, leaving April at 20_000¢ rather than 120_000¢. B13 covers this units change 36 ways and cannot see it: no grace period, no `observed_via`, so none of its invoices is ever open long enough to refresh. The pair is what makes this a defect rather than a setup artefact. Identical rows, one with the refresh step and one without: without it the draft carries 100_000¢, with it the draft carries NOTHING but the 0¢ subscription fee. The refresh is the whole difference, and the customer is invoiced 20_000¢ for a period they owe 120_000¢ on.

CHARACTERIZATION, AND THIS IS WHERE THE MONEY GOES. The customer has paid 10_000¢ and is shown 10_000¢ more for the same 100 units. Identical to b20/subscription-override/progressive_billing_credit/invoice except that the grace period is raised to 5 days on 6 March — after the threshold invoice is finalized, because Customers::UpdateInvoiceIssuingDateSettingsService:24-32 issues existing drafts when a period is shortened rather than lengthened. The diversion happens exactly as it does on the finalized invoice: the clone's charge_id defeats the cap, `amount_to_credit` exceeds `total_charges_amount` of 0, and a 10_000¢ credit note is minted. But a credit note is BEHIND the finalization gate — `should_create_credit_note_credit?` is `!not_in_finalizing_process?` (calculate_fees_service.rb:364) — so the draft cannot spend the thing that made its total look right on the other surface. progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents 0 and credit_notes_amount_cents 0 together are the finding: the money is in neither column. The other two gated reducers are asserted at 0 for the same reason the /draft sibling of lead 1 asserts them: a draft carries fees plus tax and nothing else, so a reader can see that 10_000¢ is the whole of what will be demanded and not a figure awaiting a discount. THE CONTROL IS b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/draft — same surface, same grace-period ordering, same threshold, and a total of 0 — which is what says the 10_000¢ here is the rewritten charge_id and not the draft.

CHARACTERIZATION. Lead 1's defect reached by a request that mentions neither the plan nor the metered charge. 100 units cross the 5_000¢ threshold on 5 March and 10_000¢ is collected. On 10 March the subscription's fixed charge is updated with the units it already has (1) and the price it already has ("0") — a request that changes NOTHING about what is billed. Because `properties` is present the body is not units-only, so Subscriptions::UpdateOrOverrideFixedChargeService takes `override_via_plan`, `ensure_plan_override` calls Plans::OverrideService, and that service dups the plan and then runs Charges::OverrideService over EVERY charge on it (override_service.rb:44-49). The metered charge the threshold invoice was billed against is now a different record with a different id, and the subscription points at the clone. The April invoice then reproduces lead 1 exactly. The cap `invoice.fees.charge.where(charge_id: progressive_billing_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id))` (progressive_billing_service.rb:29-33) matches nothing, `total_charges_amount` is 0, and because `amount_to_credit` (10_000) exceeds it the whole sum is diverted into CreditNotes::CreateFromProgressiveBillingInvoice and `amount_to_credit` becomes 0. So progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents is 0, a 10_000¢ credit note exists, and the invoice spends it on itself at calculate_fees_service.rb:62 to land on a total of 0. THE FIXED CHARGE IS PRICED AT ZERO ON PURPOSE, so no number here can come from it and the only thing the request did was move a UUID. THE TOTAL BEING RIGHT IS THE ACCIDENT lead 1 already documented: the credit note is a numbered refundable document that should not exist, can be spent on a different invoice, and is withheld entirely on a draft — which is what the /draft sibling charges the customer twice for. THE CONTROL IS b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/invoice: same threshold, same 10_000¢, charge_id rewritten by a churn that closes the period, and there the credit is found and no note is minted. Asserting credit_notes_amount_cents and the note itself is what separates "credited" from "diverted", since the total cannot.

CHARACTERIZATION. The quote and the bill disagree by the whole progressively billed amount, and the quote is the honest one. Invoices::PreviewService keeps its own copy of the cap, keyed on the same column: `billed_charge_ids = progressive_invoice.fees.charge.pluck(:charge_id)` then `next 0 unless billed_charge_ids.include?(fee.charge_id)` (preview_service.rb:346-352). After the 10 March fixed-charge update cloned the plan, the previewed fee carries the clone's charge_id, the include? is false, `creditable_amount_cents` is 0 and `amount_cents = [10_000, 0].min` is dropped by `next unless amount_cents.positive?`. A preview may not issue a credit note — the comment at :344-345 says the excess is simply dropped — so there is no second spelling of the money here. The customer is quoted 10_000¢ on a period for which 10_000¢ has already been taken, which is exactly the overstatement the comment at :324-329 says this code exists to prevent, and the 1 May invoice asserted beside it settles at 0 by spending a credit note instead. Same lost join, two disguises: the invoice hides it and the preview does not. THE CONTROL IS b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/preview — same preview code, same threshold, charge_id rewritten by an upgrade — where the credit is found and both surfaces read 0. The previewed period has usage by construction (100 units on 5 March, previewed on the 25th); Invoices::PreviewService raises a 500 on a charge with no usage in the period, so a preview row that dies rather than disagrees is that, not this.

CHARACTERIZATION, and the sequence in which a working draft is broken by a refresh whose only trigger was a no-op price update on an unrelated fixed charge. The March period draft is created on 1 April while the plan is still the original, so its charge fee shares the threshold fee's charge_id, the cap matches, 10_000¢ is credited and the draft sits at 0¢. On 2 April the fixed charge is updated with its own units and its own price — nothing changes — but because `properties` was sent the request clones the plan and every charge on it. On the 3rd the draft is refreshed. RefreshDraftService destroys the fees and `invoice.credits.progressive_billing_invoice_kind`, zeroes progressive_billing_credit_amount_cents, and re-runs CalculateFeesService against `subscription.plan.charges` — now the clone's. The threshold invoice's `to_credit_amount` is back to the full 10_000¢ (the credit that had netted it down was just destroyed, and no note existed yet), the cap misses, and the whole amount is diverted into a credit note the draft may not spend. THE DRAFT GOES FROM 0¢ TO 10_000¢ AND A 10_000¢ CREDIT NOTE APPEARS. The credit note is asserted with `select: {index: -1}` — without a selector expect.credit_note reads a creation-time payload this row never produced — and its 10_000¢ balance is the positive evidence that the threshold money existed and was diverted rather than never collected. THE CONTROL IS b20/plan-upgrade/progressive_billing_credit/regenerated: identical refresh, identical threshold, charge_id rewritten by an upgrade, and the draft comes back at 0. The refresh is when the rewritten id is first consulted, not the cause.

b10/fixed_amount/once/charge held open, and it separates the block's two halves cleanly: the LADDER survives the draft and the coupon does not. The ladder is intact. Fees::ApplyTaxesService runs per fee inside Invoices::ComputeTaxesAndTotalsService at calculate_fees_service.rb:56, which is above the gate, and #applicable_taxes resolves the same three rungs it resolves on the finalized invoice (apply_taxes_service.rb:64-78): the charge's own 25% for b21_w1_b10d_taxed, the plan's 15% for the subscription fee and for the untaxed metric, and neither the customer's 10% nor the entity's 5% anywhere. That is asserted per fee because 150 / 2_500 / 750 and any uniform blend summing to 3_400 are indistinguishable in an invoice total. The coupon is absent, and the ladder is what makes its absence expensive. Finalized, the 1_600¢ coupon is spread across the three fees in proportion — 100 / 1_000 / 500 — and each remainder is taxed at ITS own rate: 900×15% + 9_000×25% + 4_500×15% = 135 + 2_250 + 675 = 3_060¢, total 17_460¢. On the draft every fee is taxed gross: 150 + 2_500 + 750 = 3_400¢, total 19_400¢. So the draft overstates by 1_940¢ — 1_600 of missing discount and 340 of tax charged on it. The tax on a discount that will never be billed is the part a row asserting only coupons_amount_cents would miss, and it is why sub_total_excluding_taxes and taxes_amount_cents are both named. The coupon is not consumed either: `once` and still whole, because Credits::AppliedCouponsService was never called (:54, guarded by :368).

The two surfaces AGREE on the hardest number in the block, and PreviewService gets there through its own code. Both read 3_060¢ of tax and 17_460¢ due, matching b10/fixed_amount/once/charge exactly. That is not a shared implementation: #compute_tax_and_totals reimplements the pipeline (preview_service.rb:292-321), and it happens to preserve both properties this block tests. The order is right — Coupons::PreviewService at :299, taxes at :309 — and so is the per-fee distribution: Coupons::PreviewService#add_credit walks the fees and increments precise_coupons_amount_cents by fee.compute_precise_credit_amount_cents (preview_service, coupons/ preview_service.rb:57-62), the same method the real Credits::AppliedCouponsService uses. So the spread is 100 / 1_000 / 500 and each fee is taxed at its own rung on what remains: 900×15% + 9_000×25% + 4_500×15% = 135 + 2_250 + 675. The per-fee taxes are asserted on the PREVIEW rather than on the invoice, because the invoice side is already pinned by the borrowed row and the preview side is where a second implementation could drift. Two drifts are excluded: a preview that taxed before discounting would read 3_400¢ and 17_800¢ (b21/b10/draft's tax figure — the same mistake the draft makes for a different reason), and a preview that discounted at invoice level without touching the fees would read the same 3_400¢ of fee tax while claiming a 14_400¢ sub_total, which is precisely the inconsistency b21/b5/preview catches on the progressive-billing path. Nothing is consumed: the coupon is `once` and still whole when 1 April spends it, which is why one period is enough here — the preview and the invoice are looking at the SAME period, not consecutive ones. `no_transaction: true` is REQUIRED and is not decoration. Invoices::PreviewService#add_charge_fees wraps each charge in `ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.with_connection` inside a Parallel block (preview_service.rb:204-226); with more than one charge that releases the connection carrying RSpec's test transaction, and the next lazy association load — `applied_coupon.coupon` at coupons/preview_service.rb:22 — comes back nil against an empty database, so the request 500s with `undefined method 'fixed_amount?' for nil`. Verified by bisection: the identical row with ONE charge does not raise, and this row with the deletion strategy does not either. It is the same mechanism as F73 (recorded as F86) and it makes every MULTI-CHARGE preview row in the suite need this flag.

The b21/b10/draft ladder rebuilt, and the reason this cell earns a row is that a refresh throws the applied taxes away and has to find the same rungs again. #reset_invoice_values calls `invoice.applied_taxes.destroy_all` and destroys every fee (refresh_draft_service.rb:121-122); the Fee::AppliedTax rows go with them. The second pass resolves the ladder from scratch, per fee, and must land on 150 / 2_500 / 750 — the same three rungs, still shadowing the customer's 10% and the entity's 5%. Three regressions are excluded by the per-fee figures and by nothing else. A rebuilt fee that lost its charge association would fall to the plan's 15% and read 1_500¢ instead of 2_500¢, total 18_400¢. A refresh that appended taxes rather than replacing them would double them to 6_800¢. A refresh that resolved the ladder against the invoice instead of the fee would apply one blended rate. All three are invisible in fees_amount_cents, which is 16_000¢ throughout. The coupon stays absent and unconsumed — `context: :refresh` keeps not_in_finalizing_process? true — so the surface still asks 19_400¢ where b10/fixed_amount/once/charge asks 17_460¢. Two passes do not move the customer any closer to the number they will pay, which is the honest reading of "refreshed and nothing moved" for a reducer that is gated rather than stale.

b12/in-arrears/calendar/monthly held open, and the row that shows the gating is drawn in the right place rather than arbitrarily. The commitment true-up is PRESENT on the draft: 2_000¢ subscription + 3_000¢ of usage against a 10_000¢ floor gives a 5_000¢ `commitment` fee, all three fees exactly as on the issued invoice. That is because a true-up is a fee PRODUCER, created alongside the others (calculate_fees_service.rb:46), and the finalizing gate sits below the producers. The coupon is absent, so the draft asks 12_000¢ where the issued invoice asks 9_600¢. So on one draft, in one row: the producer survives and the reducer does not, and the line between them is where the gate is. Asserting the three fees individually is what makes that visible — fees_amount_cents is 10_000¢ either way and could not tell the true-up was computed at all.

The two surfaces AGREE, on the only fee in the suite that a preview has to invent rather than project. Both read three fees totalling 10_000¢, a 2_000¢ coupon, 1_600¢ of tax and 9_600¢ due. The preview's true-up comes from a different service and a different input: Invoices::PreviewService#add_commitment_fee (:259-289) builds an UNSAVED InvoiceSubscription and hands Fees::Commitments::Minimum::CalculatePreviewFeeService the running fee total it has summed in memory — 2_000 + 3_000 = 5_000 — rather than letting the service read fees back from the database as the real InArrears path does. Two routes to `[10_000 − 5_000, 0].max`, and this row is what says they meet. The mid-period timing is where a commitment preview could plausibly go wrong and does not. The quote is taken on 20 March with only 3_000¢ of usage recorded, so a preview that measured usage to Time.current instead of to the period end would still find 3_000¢ here — but a preview that treated the partial period as SHORT would prorate the floor: Commitments::CalculateAmountService applies a proration_coefficient, and a coefficient of 20/31 would give a 6_452¢ floor, a 1_452¢ true-up, 6_452¢ of fees and 5_342¢ due. It quotes the full month because billing_time is 1 April (:145), not 20 March. The coupon then lands identically on both surfaces, spread 400 / 600 / 1_000 across the three fees, and the per-fee amounts are asserted on the preview because fees_count 3 alone cannot say the true-up was 5_000¢ rather than the floor charged whole.

b21/b12/draft rebuilt. Same three fees, same 12_000¢, and the true-up is the assertion because it is the one fee computed FROM the other fees — so a refresh has to recreate them in an order that lets it see them. #reset_invoice_values destroys all three fees; CalculateFeesService then recreates the subscription and charge fees inside the per-invoice_subscription loop and calls create_minimum_commitment_true_up_fee LAST, at :46. Commitments::Minimum::InArrears:: CalculateTrueUpFeeService reads its fees back through FetchInvoicesService, which for a plan with no monthly-split intervals is `Invoice.where(id: invoice_subscription.invoice_id)` — this very invoice (fetch_invoices_service.rb:26-28). So it sums the 2_000¢ and 3_000¢ just written and charges the 5_000¢ shortfall against the 10_000¢ floor. Three wrong numbers are excluded. 10_000¢ of true-up (15_000¢ of fees, 18_000¢ due) is what a refresh that computed the true-up before the other fees, or against the destroyed ones, would produce — the floor charged in full as if the customer had spent nothing. 0¢ is what a refresh that counted the OLD commitment fee as spend would produce. And a stale 5_000¢ carried over rather than recomputed is excluded by the fee having been destroyed at all. The coupon stays withheld, so this surface asks 12_000¢ where the issued invoice asks 9_600¢ (10_000 − 2_000 = 8_000 taxed at 20%). Producer above the gate, reducer below it, twice over: the line held on the first computation and holds on the second.

b15/coupon/tax held open instead of issued. That row is the suite's canonical proof that a coupon applies BEFORE tax: 10_000¢ of fees less a 4_000¢ coupon = 6_000¢ taxed at 20% = 1_200¢, total 7_200¢. As a draft the same period reads 12_000¢. The coupon is not applied at all — `should_create_coupon_credit?` returns false unless the invoice is finalizing (calculate_fees_service.rb:368) — so tax falls on the full undiscounted 10_000¢ and there is no discount to subtract. Both numbers are correct for what they are, and that is the point: the interaction B15 exists to pin is INVISIBLE on a draft, because only one of its two stages has run. A customer reading this invoice mid-period sees 12_000¢ and will be billed 7_200¢ — a 67% overstatement, and the larger the coupon the worse it gets. coupons_amount_cents is asserted as 0 rather than omitted, because "no coupon" and "a coupon of zero" look identical in a total.

The two surfaces AGREE on the ORDER, which is the only thing B15 measures. b15/coupon/tax is the suite's canonical proof that the coupon precedes the tax on a finalized invoice: 10_000¢ of fees, a 4_000¢ fixed coupon, 20% on the 6_000¢ that remains = 1_200¢, total 7_200¢. The preview taken on 20 March reaches the same four numbers, and it is a genuinely independent derivation — Invoices::PreviewService#compute_tax_and_totals calls Coupons::PreviewService at :299 and only then apply_taxes at :309, mirroring calculate_fees_service.rb:54 and :56 in a file that shares no code with it. The row is sized so the two orders cannot coincide. Taxing first would give 10_000 + 2_000 = 12_000 and then the coupon → 8_000¢, so a preview with the stages transposed would quote 800¢ more than the invoice it forecasts. A percentage coupon would commute and prove only that both stages ran. fees_amount_cents is 10_000¢ under either order and is asserted only as a control; the sequence lives in sub_total_excluding_taxes 6_000 and taxes 1_200. Both are asserted on both surfaces deliberately. Assert the preview alone and a wrong preview matching a wrong invoice would look like parity; assert the invoice alone and this becomes a duplicate of the B15 row it borrows from. The pair is the cell.

b15/coupon/tax rebuilt instead of held. The issued invoice is 7_200¢ — 10_000¢ of fees less a 4_000¢ coupon, taxed at 20% on the 6_000¢ that remains. The refreshed draft is 12_000¢, the same figure b21/b15/draft reports, and reporting it AGAIN after a rebuild is the point. "Changed something, refreshed, nothing moved" is the sentence this row exists to make safe to say. A refresh that had applied the coupon would read 7_200¢ and would have consumed a `once` coupon on an invoice nobody has issued — and Invoices::RefreshDraftService contains no recredit path, so a subsequent void or a further refresh would not give it back. The 12_000¢ is therefore not a limitation of the refresh; it is the refresh declining to spend something it cannot un-spend, and `context: :refresh` keeping not_in_finalizing_process? true (calculate_fees_service.rb:368) is the single line that decides it. The block's whole subject — that the coupon comes BEFORE the tax — is undecidable on this surface, and the row says which field would have decided it: taxes_amount_cents. 2_000¢ is 20% of the gross 10_000¢; the issued invoice's 1_200¢ is 20% of the discounted 6_000¢; the reverse order would have given 2_000¢ of tax and an 8_000¢ total. Two of those three readings produce 2_000¢ of tax, so a refreshed draft cannot tell "coupon withheld" from "tax applied first" — which is exactly why the interaction needs the finalized surface and why this row asserts the sub_total alongside it.

b19/coupon/equal/invoice held open. Issued, that invoice discounts 4_000¢ — two 2_000¢ coupons that both apply and add — and settles at 11_000¢. As a draft it reads the full 15_000¢ with neither coupon applied, and the multiplicity question B19 exists to answer cannot even be asked: whether two coupons add, compete or are consumed in an order is undecidable on a surface that applies none of them. There is a reason this gating is right, and it is worth stating because it looks like a bug. Both coupons are `frequency: once`. Had the draft consumed them, a refresh would have to give them back, and `should_terminate_applied_coupon?` has already decided one of them is spent. Withholding until finalization is what keeps a grace period from destroying a customer's discounts.

The two surfaces AGREE that two coupons ADD, and reaching that through PreviewService means surviving a loop that could have stopped after one. Both read 4_000¢ of discount on 15_000¢ of fees and 11_000¢ due, matching b19/coupon/equal/invoice. Coupons::PreviewService iterates `applied_coupons` and breaks only on `unless invoice.sub_total_excluding_taxes_amount_cents&.positive?` (coupons/preview_service.rb:23) — the same guard as the real Credits::AppliedCouponsService:28. With a 15_000¢ base neither 2_000¢ coupon exhausts it, so the loop runs twice, each AppliedCoupons::AmountService call returns the full 2_000¢, and coupons_amount_cents accumulates to 4_000¢. 2_000¢ would be the answer if the preview took only the first applied coupon, and 15_000¢ if it read `customer.applied_coupons` in a scope that excluded them; both are plausible in a service whose coupons arrive as an injected array rather than from the invoice (preview_service.rb:7-10, populated by PreviewContextService from customer.applied_coupons.active). Neither coupon is consumed by the quote: `once` and both still whole when 1 April spends them for real, which is why the preview and the invoice can look at the same period and agree. Had the preview terminated them, the invoice on 1 April would have found none and billed 15_000¢ — so the invoice's own 4_000¢ is the control that the preview was read-only, exactly as the wallet is in b21/b6/preview and the credit-note balance in b21/b8/preview.

b19/coupon/equal rebuilt: 5_000¢ plan + 100 units = 15_000¢, two 2_000¢ `once` coupons that both apply and add on the issued invoice, settling it at 11_000¢. The refreshed draft reads 15_000¢ with neither applied. The multiplicity question is undecidable here, and the row says how badly: one coupon applied would give 13_000¢, both 11_000¢, and this surface reports 15_000¢ — further from either than they are from each other. A block that varies HOW MANY instances of a feature meet cannot be measured on a surface that admits none. What the refresh does establish is that both coupons are still spendable after two passes. `should_terminate_applied_coupon?` fires only from inside Credits::AppliedCouponService (applied_coupon_service.rb:78-85), which the gate at calculate_fees_service.rb:368 keeps unreached, so neither `once` coupon is marked consumed by either computation. That is the failure worth excluding rather than the totals. Had a refresh evaluated the coupons — even without booking the credits — the first pass could have terminated one and the second the other, and the finalized invoice would then discount 0¢ and bill 15_000¢ for real: a grace period silently destroying a customer's discounts, which is precisely what withholding exists to prevent. The three zeroes are asserted individually because the three withheld reducers share one total: 15_000¢ is equally consistent with a coupon lost, a credit note lost or a wallet not spent, and only naming each says which of them this scenario had none of.

b05/fixed/single/credited-on-final with 20% VAT added and the period held open. That row's finalized period invoice reads fees 3_000¢, progressive_billing_credit 3_000¢, total 0 — and the draft here reads EXACTLY the same, which is the assertion.
